title: [Feature]: Supports Speculative Speculative Decoding
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch # Motivation vLLM already supports speculative decoding to accelerate autoregressive generation using a draft model. However, speculative decoding still suffers from a sequential dependency between drafting and verification: the draft model must wait for the target model to finish verifying tokens before generating the next speculation batch. Recent work proposes Speculative Speculative Decoding (SSD), which removes this dependency by running drafting and verification asynchronously and precomputing speculations for predicted verification outcomes. paper link: [https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03251](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03251) In SSD, while the target model verifies a speculation, the draft model predicts likely verification outcomes and pre-speculates tokens for those outcomes in advance. If the actual verification result matches one of the predicted outcomes, the next speculation can be returned immediately, eliminating drafting latency. This approach enables overlapping speculation and verification and significantly reduces idle GPU time. The paper reports: - Up to 2× speedup over optimized speculative decoding - Up to 5× speedup over autoregressive decoding across several workloads and datasets. Given that vLLM is widely used for high-performance inference, supporting SSD could provide meaningful latency improvements.
### Additional context [_No response_](https://github.com/tanishqkumar/ssd) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: comment on vllm-project/vllm #36037
body:
My thoughts:
- Substantial engineering work would be required to support SSD in the vLLM framework. It would be very difficult to build this into the vLLM scheduler+worker infrastructure, a lot of the speculative decoding and kv cache management logic would need to be redesigned. A hacky prototype could put something together but this would be a very complex system to debug and maintain in the long term.
- GSM8k @ concurrency=1 with TP4 is a very favorable benchmark. Using MTBench as a proxy for chat workloads would show a much steeper falloff in AL, so it would not be as valuable to run with >8 spec tokens in that scenario. Using TP1 or TP2 would also be more affordable by a large margin, the TPS would be a bit lower but the cost-effectiveness makes a huge difference in practice. This would also be exaggerated if another H100 was needed for the drafter, notably also since it no longer can fit 2 replicas in a single 8xH100 node.
- Please share the actual ITL metrics you have measured for this, it is hard to tell the value in drafting so many tokens if we cannot quantify the increase in verification time.
- We have some work in the pipeline to reduce drafting overhead, such as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33503 as well as some open work on full-graphs and torch.compile for the draft model. There is a lot of room to improve the drafting overhead with simpler approaches.

title: comment on vllm-project/vllm #36037
body:
@benchislett  @celsowm  
I did some MTP testing on Qwen3.5-27B with the following setup:

- H100, TP=4
- Model: Qwen3.5-27B
- Dataset: GSM8K

In my tests, as `mtp-draft-tokens` increases, the average accepted length (AL) also increases:

mtp-draft-tokens | AL
-- | --
3 | 3.64
4 | 4.335
5 | 4.70
6 | 5.25
7 | 5.66
8 | 5.93
10 | 6.44
12 | 6.85
14 | 6.90
16 | 7.04



However, under concurrency=1, I also found that the drafting cost becomes significant:

- with 8 draft tokens, drafting takes 27.76% of (verification + drafting) time
- with 16 draft tokens, drafting takes 43.45% of (verification + drafting) time

So although increasing speculative length improves AL, the extra autoregressive drafting cost starts to offset the gain. Combined with the increase in verification cost as well (more obvious at higher concurrency), this is why in my tests the overall speedup starts to decline beyond around 8~9 speculative tokens.

This makes me think that in high-acceptance-rate scenarios, autoregressive drafting methods like MTP / EAGLE-3 can themselves become a bottleneck. In that sense, parallel drafting ideas are very interesting.

That said, from my reading of the SSD paper, true overlap between drafting and verification seems to assume that the draft runner and target runner are placed on different hardware. Otherwise they would contend for the same GPU resources, which could reduce or even eliminate the overlap benefit. The issue description also frames SSD as asynchronous drafting + verification. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

So my impression is that supporting SSD in vLLM may require quite substantial runtime / scheduler / device-placement changes, rather than being a small extension of the current speculative decoding path.

Curious what the maintainers think about this.

title: comment on vllm-project/vllm #36037
body:
I'm skeptical that this project would provide a lot of value for vLLM. For most workloads we use MTP or EAGLE3, for which drafting is very rarely a significant bottleneck and therefore overlapping it with verification is not an especially promising proposition.

While vLLM does currently support draft-target speculation (e.g. Llama 1B with Llama 70B, Qwen3-0.6B with Qwen3-8B etc.) all model pairs I know of have publicly-available EAGLE3 models which can exceed the speed of the draft-target pair. The paper claims this:
> In our experiments Llama-3.2-1B outperforms Eagle-3 as a draft model for Llama-3.1-70B in SGLang.
I have not found this to be true in my experience. I have serious concerns that the evaluations in the paper are incomplete and do not highlight a representative set of benchmarks. 

I do not consider this to be a priority feature for vLLM. You are welcome to attempt to reproduce the paper's results for vLLM, and I am happy to reconsider if the results are indeed compelling for a standard set of models/benchmarks (e.g. Qwen3/Llama3.3/GPT-OSS validated on [MTBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/philschmid/mt-bench)/[SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench))

## Overview

Update the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash "B200 AgentX tuning" guide with the settings qualified in [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#3837](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3837) (head `d2d90439`). It changes only `recipes/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.yaml` (guide text).

## Claims

- **DEP2:** document c24 alongside c32 (piecewise graphs to 4096 tokens, `--prefill-schedule-interval 64`). State the per-concurrency `--max-num-seqs`: 16 at c8/c16 and 32 at c24/c32. #1106 said it "matches the concurrency", which is wrong for c8 and c24.
- **DEP4:** document c96 alongside c128 (`--prefill-schedule-interval 48`, `--max-num-seqs` equal to concurrency), and add the DEP4 `--compilation-config` with separate decode-replay capture sizes.
- **DEP2 host KV:** extend native CPU KV offload (32 GiB per DP rank, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.955`, `--max-num-seqs 48`) from c128 to c64 as well, with graph capture stopping at 576 tokens.

## Overview

Run Reflection Beam with attention DP + expert parallelism on FlashInfer CuTeDSL MegaMoE (`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`). **Stacked on #62366** (Beam's fused all-reduce, base branch `woosuk/beam-fused-allreduce`), which builds on the merged #62074. The diff shows only this PR's commit.

**Depends on FlashInfer nightly** for `forward_unfinalized`, `do_finalize` and `create_workspace`. These are detected at runtime, and the new paths stay off with older FlashInfer.

## Claims

- **Prefill throughput:** attention DP4 + MegaMoE reaches 1.71× TP4's peak prefill throughput for Beam.
- **MegaMoE deferred finalize:** `defer_moe_finalize(allow_ep=True)` now also covers MegaMoE under DP/EP. MegaMoE returns `UnfinalizedMoEOutput` through `forward_unfinalized`. Beam finalizes the local rows in a new kernel (`moe_finalize.cu`) fused with the post-MoE norms and residual.
- **Decode workspace:** MegaMoE keeps a second, decode-sized workspace: `max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens per sequence-parallel rank. It is used when every DP rank's batch fits, since peer buffer offsets depend on the capacity.
- **Idle ranks:** passthrough-all2all experts now run on ranks with zero tokens instead of returning early, because these experts own the EP collective that every rank must join.

## Validation

**Prefill**, 4×GB300, 32K input / 1 output token, FlashInfer nightly:

| Configuration | Peak input throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|
| Attention DP + MegaMoE | 168.8K |
| TP4 | 98.7K |

**Unit tests** on this branch (rebased onto #62366), GB200 with FlashInfer 0.7.2, which has none of the nightly APIs:

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/models/test_beam_weight_mapping.py tests/transformers_utils/test_beam_config.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py \
  "tests/test_config.py::test_dflash_candidate_draft_forces_v2_model_runner"
# 382 passed, 4 skipped, 8 failed
```

- **Failures:** the 8 are `test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py::test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs`, which fail identically on `main` in this environment.
- **Skipped:** the DP-boundary MegaMoE test, which checks bit-exact output for unequal and empty batches with CUDA graph replay, needs FlashInfer nightly. The MegaMoE runtime paths still need CI or a nightly-FlashInfer machine.

## Details

- **Effect on existing MegaMoE users (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 with `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`):**
  - With FlashInfer nightly, they also get the decode workspace. This adds one more workspace allocation and its warmup.
  - Idle ranks now run the experts and join the collective.
  - Deferral stays off unless a model asks for it.
- **Rebase onto the released Beam schema:** Beam now hardcodes its post-feedforward norm and depth-scaled residuals, so the MegaMoE boundary always receives a post-norm weight and scales. `beam_norm_residual_norm` regains an optional post-norm only for the fused finalize, which applies the post-norm itself.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR adds EP deferral or MegaMoE workspace selection.

+def _torch_megamoe_finalize(experts, weights, routed_scale, post_weight, post_eps):
+    # BF16 x FP32 fits in FP64; round once per fused multiply-add to FP32.
+    value = (experts[:, 0].double() * weights[:, 0, None].double()).float()
+    for k in range(1, experts.shape[1]):

+def _beam_moe_gather_worker(rank, world_size, port, hidden_size):
+    from datetime import timedelta
+
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_output import UnfinalizedMoEOutput
+    from vllm.models.beam.nvidia.allreduce import (
+        BeamAllReduceWorkspace,
+        beam_allreduce_norm_residual_norm,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.beam.nvidia.moe_finalize import (
+        beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm,
+    )
+
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(
+        "nccl",
+        init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=world_size,
+        timeout=timedelta(seconds=120),
+    )
+    group = dist.new_group(backend="gloo")
+    workspace = BeamAllReduceWorkspace(group, hidden_size, 513)
+
+    def make_case(tokens, seed, *, next_norm):
+        local_rows = (tokens + world_size - 1) // world_size
+        valid_rows = max(0, min(local_rows, tokens - rank * local_rows))
+        torch.manual_seed(seed)
+        residual = torch.randn(tokens, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        affine = torch.randn(hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        torch.manual_seed(seed + rank + 1)
+        experts = torch.randn(
+            local_rows + 3, 8, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        weights = torch.rand(local_rows + 3, 8, device="cuda")
+        permutation = torch.arange(
+            (local_rows + 3) * 8, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        ).view(local_rows + 3, 8)
+        experts[:valid_rows:2].mul_(1e-3)
+        experts[:valid_rows, :, ::97] = -0.0
+        experts[:valid_rows, :, 1::97] = -1e-40
+        # Both capacity padding and SP padding must stay outside live outputs.
+        experts[valid_rows:] = float("nan")
+        weights[valid_rows:] = float("nan")
+        return (
+            UnfinalizedMoEOutput(experts.flatten(0, 1), weights, permutation),
+            residual,
+            affine,
+            1e-6,
+            affine if next_norm else None,
+            1e-6 if next_norm else None,
+            (0.125, 0.9682458365518543),
+            workspace,
+            0.137,
+        )
+
+    def check(actual, args):
+        output, residual, pw, peps, nw, neps, scales, _, scale = args
+        tokens = residual.shape[0]
+        local_rows = (tokens + world_size - 1) // world_size
+        valid_rows = max(0, min(local_rows, tokens - rank * local_rows))
+        weights = output.expert_weights[:valid_rows]
+        experts = output.gemm2_permuted.view(-1, 8, hidden_size)[:valid_rows]
+        local = torch.zeros(
+            local_rows, hidden_size, dtype=residual.dtype, device=residual.device
+        )
+        local[:valid_rows] = _torch_megamoe_finalize(experts, weights, scale, pw, peps)
+        gathered = torch.empty(
+            world_size * local_rows,
+            hidden_size,
+            dtype=local.dtype,
+            device=local.device,
+        )
+        if tokens:
+            dist.all_gather_into_tensor(gathered, local)
+        expected = _torch_boundary(
+            gathered[:tokens], residual, None, None, nw, neps, scales
+        )
+        _assert_boundary_close(actual, expected, relative_tolerance=1e-3)
+
+    batches = (0, 1, world_size + 1, 513)
+    for iteration, tokens in enumerate(batches):
+        args = make_case(tokens, 200 + iteration, next_norm=iteration % 2 == 0)
+        for strategy in ("unfused", "oneshot", "twoshot", None):
+            check(
+                beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm(*args, strategy=strategy),
+                args,
+            )
+
+    # Independent captured graphs share the Lamport generation state. Replaying
+    # one then two stages must work after eager collectives and changed inputs.
+    graphs = []
+    for strategy, tokens in (
+        ("oneshot", world_size - 1),
+        ("oneshot", 17),
+        ("twoshot", world_size - 1),
+        ("twoshot", 129),
+    ):
+        args = make_case(tokens, 300 + tokens, next_norm=True)
+        beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm(*args, strategy=strategy)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        dist.barrier()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            actual = beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm(
+                *args, strategy=strategy
+            )
+        graphs.append((graph, actual, args))
+    # Without a reference collective between replays, empty ranks may lag more
+    # than a Lamport generation. Padded rows must still acknowledge each rank.
+    for graph, actual, args in graphs:
+        if rank == world_size - 1:
+            torch.cuda._sleep(2_000_000)
+        for _ in range(16):
+            graph.replay()
+        check(actual, args)
+    for iteration in range(2):
+        for graph, actual, args in graphs[:: 1 if iteration % 2 else -1]:
+            output = args[0]
+            output.gemm2_permuted.mul_(0.75)
+            output.expert_weights.copy_(output.expert_weights.roll(1, dims=1))
+            args[1].mul_(0.5)
+            args[2].neg_()
+            graph.replay()
+            check(actual, args)
+            # Attention AR and MoE gather reuse this workspace in production.
+            residual, weight = args[1], args[2]
+            x = residual * (rank + 1)
+            scales = args[6]
+            ar_args = (x, residual, weight, 1e-6, weight, 1e-6, scales, workspace)
+            actual_ar = beam_allreduce_norm_residual_norm(*ar_args)
+            reduced = x.float()
+            dist.all_reduce(reduced)
+            _assert_boundary_close(
+                actual_ar,
+                _torch_boundary(
+                    reduced.bfloat16(), residual, weight, 1e-6, weight, 1e-6, scales
+                ),
+                relative_tolerance=1e-3,
+            )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    for graph, _, _ in graphs:
+        graph.reset()
+    dist.barrier()
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("world_size,hidden_size", [(2, 8192), (4, 5120)])
+def test_megamoe_gather_restores_tokens_and_alternates_graph_strategies(
+    world_size, hidden_size
+):
+    """Keep SP rank order, BF16 casts, and generation state across all strategies."""
+    from torch.multiprocessing import spawn
+
+    from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+    if torch.accelerator.device_count() < world_size:
+        pytest.skip(f"Requires {world_size} GPUs")
+    mnnvl = pytest.importorskip("flashinfer.comm.mnnvl")
+    if not mnnvl.is_multicast_supported(0):
+        pytest.skip("NVLink multicast required")
+    spawn(
+        _beam_moe_gather_worker,
+        args=(world_size, get_open_port(), hidden_size),
+        nprocs=world_size,
+    )
+
+

+            or self.experts.shared_experts is not None
+            or self.experts.routed_input_transform is not None
+            or self.experts.routed_output_transform is not None
+            or moe.pcp_size != 1
+            or moe.tp_size != 1
+            or moe.ep_size <= 1
+            or not supports_flashinfer_moe_ep_deferred_finalize()
+        ):
+            return False
+        fuse_gather = (
+            workspace is not None
+            and moe.sp_size == workspace.world_size == moe.ep_size
+            and moe.dp_size == 1
+        )
+        if not self.is_sequence_parallel or fuse_gather:
+            self.gather_workspace = workspace if fuse_gather else None
+            self.output_boundary_fused = True
+            moe.defer_moe_finalize(allow_ep=True)
+            self._compilation_config.static_forward_context[
+                self._boundary_layer_name
+            ] = self
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def forward_boundary(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        residual: torch.Tensor,
+        post_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        post_eps: float,
+        next_weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+        next_eps: float | None,
+        scales: tuple[float, float],
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+        hidden, normalized = torch.ops.vllm.beam_moe_forward_boundary(
+            hidden_states,
+            residual,
+            post_weight,
+            post_eps,
+            next_weight,
+            next_eps,
+            *scales,
+            self.experts._encode_layer_name(),
+        )
+        return hidden, normalized if next_eps is not None else None
+
+    def _forward_boundary(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        residual: torch.Tensor,
+        post_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        post_eps: float,
+        next_weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+        next_eps: float | None,
+        scales: tuple[float, float],
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+        from .moe_finalize import (
+            beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm,
+            beam_moe_finalize_norm_residual_norm,
+        )
+
+        local_states = (
+            sequence_parallel_chunk(hidden_states)
+            if self.is_sequence_parallel
+            else hidden_states
+        )
+        output = self.experts._forward_impl(local_states, local_states, None)
+        assert isinstance(output, UnfinalizedMoEOutput)
+        # Consume the borrowed expert workspace inside the same opaque op.
+        if self.gather_workspace is None:
+            return beam_moe_finalize_norm_residual_norm(
+                output,
+                residual,
+                post_weight,
+                post_eps,
+                next_weight,
+                next_eps,
+                scales,
+                routed_scale=self.experts.routed_scaling_factor,
+            )
+        return beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm(
+            output,
+            residual,
+            post_weight,
+            post_eps,
+            next_weight,
+            next_eps,
+            scales,
+            self.gather_workspace,
+            routed_scale=self.experts.routed_scaling_factor,
+        )
+
     def forward(
         self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor
     ) -> torch.Tensor | UnfinalizedMoEOutput:
-        if self.experts.moe_config.should_defer_moe_finalize(hidden_states.shape[0]):
+        num_tokens = hidden_states.shape[0]
+        if self.is_sequence_parallel:
+            hidden_states = sequence_parallel_chunk(hidden_states)
+        elif self.experts.moe_config.should_defer_moe_finalize(num_tokens):
             output = self.experts._forward_impl(hidden_states, hidden_states, None)
             assert isinstance(output, UnfinalizedMoEOutput)
             return output
 
-        return self.experts(hidden_states=hidden_states, router_logits=hidden_states)
+        output = self.experts(hidden_states=hidden_states, router_logits=hidden_states)
+        if self.is_sequence_parallel:
+            output = tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(output, 0)[:num_tokens]
+        return output

title: vllm/models/beam/nvidia/moe_finalize.cu
vllm/models/beam/nvidia/moe_finalize.py
body:
@@ -0,0 +1,271 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Finalize live MegaMoE tokens with Beam's post normalization."""
+
+import functools
+import hashlib
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_output import UnfinalizedMoEOutput
+
+from .allreduce import BeamAllReduceWorkspace
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _module(packs_per_thread: int = 1):
+    from flashinfer.jit import env as jit_env
+    from flashinfer.jit.core import current_compilation_context, gen_jit_spec
+
+    source = Path(__file__).with_suffix(".cu")
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
+    flags = current_compilation_context.get_nvcc_flags_list(
+        supported_major_versions=[9, 10]
+    )
+    spec = gen_jit_spec(
+        f"beam_moe_finalize_{digest}_{packs_per_thread}",
+        [source],
+        extra_cuda_cflags=[
+            *flags,
+            "--fmad=false",
+            f"-DBEAM_MOE_PACKS_PER_THREAD={packs_per_thread}",
+        ],
+        extra_include_paths=[jit_env.FLASHINFER_CSRC_DIR],
+    )
+    spec.extra_cuda_cflags.remove("-use_fast_math")
+    return spec.build_and_load()
+
+
+def beam_moe_finalize(
+    expert_outputs: torch.Tensor,
+    expert_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    output: torch.Tensor,
+    routed_scale: float = 1.0,
+    post_weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    post_eps: float | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reduce only output rows, preserving BF16 casts before scale and RMSNorm.
+
+    Args:
+        expert_outputs: Contiguous BF16 expert results [capacity, top_k, hidden].
+        expert_weights: Contiguous FP32 routing weights [capacity, top_k].
+        output: Contiguous BF16 destination [live_tokens, hidden].
+        routed_scale: Multiplier applied after rounding the expert reduction.
+        post_weight: Optional BF16 RMSNorm affine weight [hidden].
+        post_eps: RMSNorm epsilon, or None to omit normalization.
+
+    """
+    assert expert_outputs.ndim == 3 and expert_weights.ndim == output.ndim == 2
+    capacity, top_k, hidden = expert_outputs.shape
+    assert 1 <= top_k <= 32
+    assert 256 <= hidden <= 8192 and hidden % 256 == 0
+    assert output.shape[1] == hidden and output.shape[0] <= capacity
+    assert expert_weights.shape[1] == top_k
+    assert expert_weights.shape[0] >= output.shape[0]
+    assert expert_outputs.dtype == output.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert expert_weights.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert output.is_cuda
+    for tensor in (expert_outputs, expert_weights, output):
+        assert tensor.is_contiguous() and tensor.device == output.device
+    if post_weight is not None:
+        assert post_eps is not None
+        assert post_weight.shape == (hidden,) and post_weight.is_contiguous()
+        assert post_weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        assert post_weight.device == output.device
+    if output.shape[0]:
+        _module().beam_moe_finalize(
+            expert_outputs,
+            expert_weights,
+            output,
+            post_weight,
+            routed_scale,
+            post_eps or 0.0,
+            post_eps is not None,
+        )
+    return output
+
+
+def beam_moe_finalize_gather_norm_residual_norm(
+    x: UnfinalizedMoEOutput,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    post_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    post_eps: float,
+    next_weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    next_eps: float | None,
+    scales: tuple[float, float],
+    workspace: BeamAllReduceWorkspace,
+    routed_scale: float = 1.0,
+    *,
+    strategy: str | None = None,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+    """Finalize MegaMoE output and restore the replicated token boundary.
+
+    FlashInfer's ``forward_unfinalized`` guarantees token-major expert rows and
+    an identity route map, so a view recovers its [tokens, top_k, hidden] layout.
+    This consumer requires that producer contract.
+
+    Each rank owns ceil(global_tokens / TP) consecutive tokens. Capacity rows
+    and the final rank's token padding do not contribute to the returned tensors.
+    ``strategy`` overrides the token-count heuristic for validation and benchmarking.
+    """
+    assert residual.ndim == 2 and residual.is_cuda
+    tokens, hidden_size = residual.shape
+    local_tokens = (tokens + workspace.world_size - 1) // workspace.world_size
+    assert tokens <= workspace.max_tokens and hidden_size == workspace.hidden_size
+    expert_weights = x.expert_weights
+    assert expert_weights.ndim == 2
+    assert x.gemm2_permuted.ndim == 2 and x.gemm2_permuted.is_contiguous()
+    assert x.gemm2_permuted.shape[1] == hidden_size
+    expert_outputs = x.gemm2_permuted.view(*expert_weights.shape, hidden_size)
+    assert expert_weights.shape[0] >= local_tokens
+    assert 1 <= expert_weights.shape[1] <= 32
+    assert expert_outputs.dtype == residual.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert expert_weights.dtype == torch.float32
+    for tensor in (expert_outputs, expert_weights, residual):
+        assert tensor.is_contiguous() and tensor.device == residual.device
+    for weight, eps in ((post_weight, post_eps), (next_weight, next_eps)):
+        if weight is not None:
+            assert eps is not None
+            assert weight.shape == (hidden_size,) and weight.is_contiguous()
+            assert weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and weight.device == residual.device
+    if strategy is None:
+        if tokens <= workspace.moe_gather_oneshot_max_tokens:
+            strategy = "oneshot"
+        elif (
+            workspace.moe_gather_separate_norm_min_tokens is not None
+            and tokens >= workspace.moe_gather_separate_norm_min_tokens
+        ):
+            strategy = "unfused"
+        else:
+            strategy = "twoshot"
+    if strategy not in ("unfused", "oneshot", "twoshot"):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown MegaMoE gather strategy: {strategy}")
+    if not tokens:
+        hidden = torch.empty_like(residual)
+        return hidden, torch.empty_like(residual) if next_eps is not None else None
+    if strategy == "unfused":
+        from .layernorm import beam_norm_residual_norm
+
+        local = torch.empty(
+            (local_tokens, hidden_size), dtype=residual.dtype, device=residual.device
+        )
+        beam_moe_finalize(
+            expert_outputs, expert_weights, local, routed_scale, post_weight, post_eps
+        )
+        if workspace.all_gather is not None:
+            gathered = workspace.all_gather(local)
+        else:
+            gathered = torch.empty(
+                (local_tokens * workspace.world_size, hidden_size),
+                dtype=residual.dtype,
+                device=residual.device,
+            )
+            torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor(
+                gathered, local, group=workspace.device_group
+            )
+        return beam_norm_residual_norm(
+            gathered[:tokens], residual, None, None, next_weight, next_eps, scales
+        )
+    hidden = torch.empty_like(residual)
+    normalized = torch.empty_like(residual) if next_eps is not None else None
+    w = workspace.workspace
+    workspace.module.beam_moe_gather(
+        expert_outputs,
+        expert_weights,
+        residual,
+        post_weight,
+        next_weight,
+        hidden,
+        normalized,
+        w.uc_ptrs_dev,
+        w.buffer_flags,
+        w.mc_ptr,
+        w.uc_ptr_local,
+        workspace.world_size,
+        workspace.rank,
+        post_eps or 0.0,
+        next_eps or 0.0,
+        *scales,
+        post_eps is not None,
+        next_eps is not None,
+        scales is not None,
+        strategy == "oneshot",
+        routed_scale,
+    )
+    return hidden, normalized
+
+
+def beam_moe_finalize_norm_residual_norm(
+    x: UnfinalizedMoEOutput,
+    residual: torch.Tensor,
+    post_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    post_eps: float,
+    next_weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    next_eps: float | None,
+    scales: tuple[float, float],
+    routed_scale: float = 1.0,
+    *,
+    strategy: str | None = None,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None]:
+    """Finalize local MegaMoE tokens through the next normalization boundary.
+
+    Requires FlashInfer's token-major expert rows and identity route map.
+    Only the live rows in ``residual`` are read from the workspace capacity.
+    ``strategy`` can force the unfused reference for validation and benchmarking.
+    """
+    assert residual.ndim == 2 and residual.is_cuda
+    tokens, hidden_size = residual.shape
+    assert 256 <= hidden_size <= 8192 and hidden_size % 256 == 0
+    expert_weights = x.expert_weights
+    assert expert_weights.ndim == 2 and expert_weights.shape[0] >= tokens
+    assert 1 <= expert_weights.shape[1] <= 32
+    assert x.gemm2_permuted.ndim == 2 and x.gemm2_permuted.is_contiguous()
+    assert x.gemm2_permuted.shape[1] == hidden_size
+    expert_outputs = x.gemm2_permuted.view(*expert_weights.shape, hidden_size)
+    assert expert_outputs.dtype == residual.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert expert_weights.dtype == torch.float32
+    for tensor in (expert_outputs, expert_weights, residual):
+        assert tensor.is_contiguous() and tensor.device == residual.device
+    for weight, eps in ((post_weight, post_eps), (next_weight, next_eps)):
+        if weight is not None:
+            assert eps is not None
+            assert weight.shape == (hidden_size,) and weight.is_contiguous()
+            assert weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and weight.device == residual.device
+    if strategy not in (None, "fused", "unfused"):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown local MegaMoE finalize strategy: {strategy}")
+    if strategy == "unfused":
+        from .layernorm import beam_norm_residual_norm
+
+        finalized = torch.empty_like(residual)
+        beam_moe_finalize(
+            expert_outputs,
+            expert_weights,
+            finalized,
+            routed_scale,
+            post_weight,
+            post_eps,
+        )
+        return beam_norm_residual_norm(
+            finalized, residual, None, None, next_weight, next_eps, scales
+        )
+    hidden = torch.empty_like(residual)
+    normalized = torch.empty_like(residual) if next_eps is not None else None
+    if tokens:
+        _module().beam_moe_finalize_norm_residual_norm(
+            expert_outputs,
+            expert_weights,
+            residual,
+            post_weight,
+            next_weight,
+            hidden,
+            normalized,
+            routed_scale,
+            post_eps or 0.0,
+            next_eps or 0.0,
+            *scales,
+            post_eps is not None,
+            next_eps is not None,
+            scales is not None,
+        )
+    return hidden, normalized

title: [Bug/Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 8xTP): extremely low decode throughput with --enforce-eager; CUDA graphs unusable — please prioritize SM120 graph capture fix
body:
## Environment

- **GPU**: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (96 GB each), compute capability **12.0 (SM120)**
- **Driver**: 590.48.01
- **vLLM**: official image `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909` (V4.1-Flash day-0 image, 2026-09-09)
- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (FP8 checkpoint), served with the community SM120 patch set (patched `indexer.py`, `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `cache_utils.py`, `attention.py` under `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`, plus `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`)
- **Launch flags**:

```
--tensor-parallel-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 \
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-model-len 524288 \
--enforce-eager --language-model-only
```

## What works

- Model loads cleanly (48/48 shards, ~48 GiB/GPU), KV cache 28+ GiB/GPU, serving works, outputs are correct.
- TileLang kernels (`mhc_post_tilelang`, `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`, …) compile and run.

## Observed problem: decode throughput is ~2–4 tok/s TOTAL (3 concurrent requests)

Engine-side metrics during a 3-concurrent-request benchmark (300 completion tokens each):

```
Engine 000: Avg generation throughput: 2.3–4.0 tokens/s, Running: 3 reqs
```

i.e. roughly **~1 tok/s per request** on 8x 96 GB Blackwell GPUs — orders of magnitude below what this hardware class delivers on other backends (for reference, DS-V4-Flash on the same 8x RTX PRO 6000 reaches ~2452 tok/s aggregate in published recipes).

### Why: `--enforce-eager` is mandatory on SM120 for this model

CUDA graph capture is not usable on SM120 for V4.1-Flash (known limitations carried over from the V4-Flash SM12x bring-up: graph capture failures / instability with the MLA-sparse + MoE path). Without CUDA graphs, every decode step pays full Python/dispatch overhead on a 552B-parameter model, which produces the ~1 tok/s/request result above.

### Additional data point: DSpark speculative decoding is net-negative on SM120

With `--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'` (note: `num_speculative_tokens` must be divisible by `n_predict=5`; `7` fails validation at startup):

```
SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 1.67–2.40,
Avg Draft acceptance rate: 13.3%–28.0%
```

~72–87% of drafted tokens are rejected, so speculation only adds overhead on top of eager mode. We removed DSpark.

Two deployment footguns hit along the way (maybe worth a docs/UX note, not the main topic):
1. `/dev/shm` 64 MiB default is too small once DSpark is enabled → `RuntimeError: Insufficient space in /dev/shm: 160 MiB required`; fixed with `--shm-size=8g --ipc=host`.
2. DSpark `num_speculative_tokens=7` → pydantic validation error (`must be divisible by n_predict=5`).

## Ask

**Please prioritize making CUDA graph capture work on SM120 (compute capability 12.0) for the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 architecture.** Eager-mode decode on SM120 is effectively unusable for interactive serving of this model. With the FlashMLASparse MTP work landing on main (e.g. `4be3dcf0`), SM120 users would benefit greatly from graph-capture support in the same path.

Happy to run any test builds / capture logs on this 8x SM120 machine if useful.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot run on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000): compressed-layer page_block_size=32 has no FlashInfer sparse-MLA decode kernel instantiation (only pbs=64)
body:
### Your current environment

- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96GB), single node TP8
- vLLM: 0.30.1rc1.dev327+g9af952c55 (nightly, pip)
- FlashInfer: 0.7.0 (flashinfer-python + flashinfer-cubin + flashinfer-jit-cache sm120f+cu130, all three packages installed)
- Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (official 476GiB mixed MXFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint)
- Config: TP8, `--language-model-only`, `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`, `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash fails to start on SM120 with:

```
ValueError: SM120 sparse-MLA has no decode kernel for this shape: num_tokens=8,
num_heads=8, topk=128, d_qk=512, page_block_size=32, model_type=dsv4, extra_topk=0.
```

### Root cause analysis

V4.1's two-tier sparse attention gives each layer a `compress_ratio` (this checkpoint: `[0,0,2,2,...,2,1,1,1,1,1]`). vLLM computes the compressed-layer KV page block size as `attn_metadata.block_size // compress_ratio`, so ratio-2 layers get pbs = 64//2 = **32**.

FlashInfer's SM120 dispatch planner (`flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120_plan.py`) hard-codes `_PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64` and instantiates the dsv4 decode kernels **only** at pbs=64 (the error message itself lists `page_block_size=32` as unsupported).

There is **no single global block size that works**:
- global block_size=64 → ratio-2 compressed layers compute pbs=32 → this crash
- global block_size=128 → vLLM reports "No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; ...)" because the SM120 kernel set has no pbs=128 dsv4 instantiation either (only 64)

So the two-tier architecture (mixed ratios 1 and 2) is fundamentally incompatible with the current SM120 kernel instantiation set, which only covers pbs=64.

### Steps we already walked through to get this far (all gates passed)

1. `indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"` → rejected on SM120 ("requires Blackwell datacenter GPUs sm_10x"); switched to `"fp8"`.
2. `indexer_sparse_logits=true` → requires MXFP4 indexer cache; removed the flag.
3. `flashinfer_jit_cache` shim wheel (4KB) had to be installed with `--no-deps` in addition to the `sm120f` provider wheel (the provider wheel alone lacks the Python module `flashinfer_jit_cache.__version__`).
4. torch/torchaudio CUDA mismatch from the nightly upgrade → uninstalled torchaudio.
5. Applied #53425 (SM12x block size 64 for DeepSeek-V4) — but it only covers the `deepseek_v4` (V4) family; the `deepseek_v41` family has its own two-tier block-size chain.

A debug stack trace (added at the raise site) confirms the failing path: `deepseek_v41/attention.py::forward` → `nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py::_forward_prefill` → `flashinfer_trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` with `page_block_size=32` derived from the compressed cache tensor shape.

### What is needed (either/or)

1. **FlashInfer**: add SM120 dsv4 decode kernel instantiation at pbs=32 (or 32 and 128), OR
2. **vLLM**: allow per-layer/per-cache block sizes so compressed layers can keep pbs=64 independently of the global block size.

Until then DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is effectively unusable on SM120/SM121 hardware (the official recipe only verifies H100/H200/B200/GB200-class GPUs).

### Environment details available

Full `collect_env` available on request; reproduction environment is a dedicated 8x PRO 6000 node we can keep available for testing a fix.

Thanks!

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark speculative decoding — illegal memory access in SM120 sparse-MLA prefill on long prompts
body:
# [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark speculative decoding — illegal memory access in SM120 sparse-MLA prefill on long prompts

> Cross-ref: #55757 (same box family, same reporter — sequential sm_120 sparse-MLA investigation; that one covers the non-spec MHA prefill faults, this one is DSpark-specific).

## Environment

- **Model**: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (476 GiB), vision enabled
- **Hardware**: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GiB each), PCIe-only (no NVLink)
- **vLLM**: nightly `69db1c26` + PR #56214 overlay (`e77daef89`), flashinfer-python 0.6.18
- **Patches for SM120 serving**: topk 1152/640 instantiations in `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4.cu` + the Python `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` mirror, prefill dispatch arms for the same shapes (dual-cache `DISPATCH_BY_NH_PBSX_TK`), SWA cache block 32→64, divergent block sizes (ratio-1: 64, ratio-2: 128). Without DSpark this configuration serves cleanly: 60 tok/s c=1, 12K prefill in 2.1 s, stable in production.

## Repro

Serve with:

```json
{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}
```

Then send any prompt ≳4K tokens (12K reproduces reliably). Short prompts work; long prompts hard-crash the engine with an illegal memory access.

## Findings (instrumented)

1. `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` localizes the fault to `flashinfer` `sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu`, `launch_prefill_mg_dual` (`cudaLaunchKernelExC`, ~line 212/268), instantiation `<DSV4, FP8, nh=16, TOPK=1152, pbs=64, pbs_x=64>`, on the chunked-prefill chunks (`ntok=4092` with k=5).
2. **The same instantiation with the same shape tuple runs clean without DSpark** (12K prefill → 456× `(topk=1152, pbs=64, topk_x=512)`, zero errors), so it is input *content*, not kernel shape coverage.
3. Host-side launch-time probes of all kernel inputs found per-token lengths and index values plausible — but in some runs **garbage extra-topk lengths** (`max_elen=2139095040` on a 512-wide row → kernel K-loop reads OOB) in ~9/81 calls. In other runs the crash reproduces with clean lens at launch time, so the garbage lens are a symptom, not necessarily the trigger.
4. `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens` (`deepseek_v4_1/common/ops/cache_utils.py`) fully initializes every lens row, so garbage lens imply never-written or overwritten memory — consistent with a cross-stream/capture-time aliasing issue specific to the DSpark path.
5. PR #56598 (padded draft rows → generic MoE router, fixes #56389) does **not** fix this crash — tested on top of our tree. This is a different kernel (sparse-MLA prefill, not the dsv4_topk Triton router).

## Suspects

Cross-stream memory aliasing under DSpark (freshly-allocated lens tensors consumed by asynchronously-queued prefill kernels), or the DSpark SWA index widening (`get_dspark_swa_index_width(128,5)=192`) interacting with prefill metadata that assumes window 128.

Happy to provide probe outputs, shape histograms, and exact repro commands.

title: [SM120] Field report: running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash end-to-end on 8x RTX PRO 6000 — pitfall map + working configuration (1M context verified)
body:
## Summary

Cross-posting field data from a 3-day bring-up of **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (769B total, MXFP4 experts, Engram memory) on **8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, consumer Blackwell)**, since SM120 users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch. Related: #54929 (Triton sparse-MLA fallback — we left perf data there), #5135-tracked flashinfer instantiation gaps.

## What works (final configuration)

- vLLM `deepseekv41-flash-0909` image, TP=8, `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41`
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`
- 1M context enabled: 950K-token double-needle retrieval **correct**, 4584 tok/s prefill throughput (pure-torch logits path, eager mode)
- VRAM: ~91GB/96GB per GPU (Engram tables dominate: 2 x ~100GB shards = 189GiB across the TP group)

## Pitfall map (in the order we hit them)

1. **DeepGEMM autotune hang on first long-context batch** — warmup deadlocks at 128K+; needs skip or eager for first bring-up.
2. **flashinfer sparse-MLA SM120 instantiation gaps** — several `(num_heads, topk)` combos (e.g. `(16, 512)`) missing from `_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` / prefill dispatch (same family as flashinfer#3828). Vision path hits this too → we ran `--limit-mm-per-prompt {"image":0}` until resolved.
3. **FP8 KV-cache scale layout semantics** — the killer. Block layout is `[64tok x 128B fp8 | 64tok x 4B fp32 scale]` (block-appended), NOT per-token interleaved. Wrong interpretation passes short-prompt smoke tests and **only fails at ≥100K needle retrieval** — silent numerical corruption. Test with long needles, not perplexity.
4. **CUDA graph capture crash with flashinfer ops in graph** (>4K tokens) — resolved for us by replacing the ops with pure-torch; graphs now capture cleanly.
5. **MXFP4 expert path falls back to Marlin** on SM120 (known #30135) — works, perf hit acceptable.

## Verification methodology (cheap, catches #3)

Synthetic doc ~1M tokens with two inserted facts at 50% and 80% depth (e.g. meeting-room password + project codename/lead). Single prompt asking both. Catches numerical corruption that short-prompt tests miss. We publish numbers at 190K and 950K this way.

## Ask

- Would maintainers accept a PR adding the **pure-torch paged-MQA-logits fallback** (auto-selected on SM12x when flashinstantiation is missing)? It's ~90 lines, numerically exact, and would have saved us days. Can also serve as golden reference for #54929's Triton kernels.
- Long-needle (≥100K) test cases for SM12x CI would have caught pitfall 3 upstream.

Env: vLLM 0.1.dev20904 (deepseekv41-flash-0909), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, 8x RTX PRO 6000 96GB.

title: [Bug][Spec Decode] DSpark corrupts thinking/chat outputs on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (all k; both v0.32.0 and nightly; clean without speculation)
body:
## Environment

- Hardware: 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96G (SM120), single node, TP8 + EP
- vLLM: **0.32.0 release** and **0.32.1rc1.dev24** (latest nightly) — both reproduce
- torch: 2.13.0+cu132 (release env) / 2.14.0+cu132 (nightly env) — both reproduce
- FlashInfer: 0.7.1rc5 (python + jit-cache; cubin 0.7.0.post1)
- Checkpoint: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (site copy, 48 shards)
- Local patch: #60762 (SM120 uniform-64 block-size declaration only — 2 files, declaration-level; symptom is identical with/without it)
- Flags: `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --enable-expert-parallel --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 128 --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":N}'`

## Symptom

With DSpark enabled, `/v1/chat/completions` in thinking mode returns degenerate loops in the reasoning stream (e.g. `"to invoketo invoke..."`, `"*75*75*75..."`) and no structured tool calls are produced. Plain-text `/v1/completions` is **not** affected: a 25-tier benchmark suite (1K ladder c1-c128, long-context 32K-1M, 64K/64K ramp) ran with speculation on, all zero failures, and a 256-prompt needle-retrieval task scored 99.6% coherent — so the corruption is specific to the chat/thinking format.

## Isolation (every variable tested on the same box)

| Configuration | chat/thinking output |
|---|---|
| 1017 + DSpark k=3, vLLM nightly (torch 2.14) | degenerate loops |
| 1017 + DSpark k=3, vLLM 0.32.0 (torch 2.13) | degenerate loops |
| 1017 + DSpark k=4 / k=5 / k=7 | degenerate loops |
| **1017, no speculation (same boot, same parsers)** | **clean**: reasoning/content correctly separated (`17*19` -> reasoning "We need answer only number..." + content `323`); tools -> structured `tool_calls` (`get_gpu_alert({"node":"gpu-03"})`); 12-turn tools-API agent session 12/12, 0 errors |
| Original `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` + DSpark k=3, same hardware/config family | clean (prior deployment records on this box: 26-32 structured tool calls, 0 errors) |

Also ruled out: tokenizer files (byte-identical between the two checkpoints), template rendering (vLLM's built-in `deepseek_v41` template output is byte-identical to the official `encoding/encoding.py` reference for single-turn chat), tokenization (`/tokenize` parses the special tokens into their single IDs correctly), sampling temperature (0.0 and 1.0 both corrupt), and the parser flags (no-spec run uses the same three flags and is clean).

## Repro (minimal)

```bash
vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017> --tensor-parallel-size 8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41

curl .../v1/chat/completions -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"17*19=? answer with the number only"}],"max_tokens":512,"temperature":0}'
# with spec: reasoning = repetitive token loops; without --speculative-config: reasoning "..." + content "323"
```

## Context

- The encoder/renderer sync PRs #62199 / #62196 / #62200 address the tool-result turn encoding delta from DeepSeek's `314113f` encoding fix — a separate problem. Our corruption is single-turn, reproduces on the current encoder, and flips solely on speculation.
- #58485 reports a related class (spec decode x thinking markers) on another model family.
- 1017 is a weight-only update of V4.1-Flash (config/tokenizer unchanged; the release notes describe shortened outputs/agent tuning), so the delta is in the fine-tuned `mtp.*` draft heads or their interaction with the verifier in thinking-format contexts.

## Impact / workaround

Chat or agent serving on the 1017 checkpoint should disable DSpark speculation until this is fixed (plain-text completion workloads are unaffected). Happy to run any follow-up experiment on this box.

title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot use TP > 8: Engram hash-head sharding assertion rejects tp_size=16 across 2 nodes
body:
### Summary

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot be served with `--tensor-parallel-size 16` (2 nodes x 8 GPUs) because the Engram embedding shards its hash heads over the **TP** degree only, and its assertion rejects any `tp_size` where `ceil(n_hash_cols / tp_size) * (tp_size - 1) >= n_hash_cols`. For this checkpoint `n_hash_cols = (max_ngram_size - 1) * n_heads = (4 - 1) * 8 = 24`, so the assertion only holds for `tp_size <= 8` (or 12, which does not divide `num_attention_heads = 64`). Engine core init aborts.

A 2-node x 8-GPU deployment is a very common shape, and there is no way to use it as a single replica for this model today.

### Reproduction

Two nodes, 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) each, identical vLLM venvs, ray 2.58.0 cluster spanning both:

```bash
ray start --head --port=6379 --node-ip-address=<head> --num-gpus=8      # node A
ray start --address=<head>:6379 --node-ip-address=<worker> --num-gpus=8 # node B

vllm serve <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash> --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --language-model-only
```

The ray placement group is created fine (16/16 GPUs reserved), weights start loading, then:

```
File "vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py", line 302, in __init__
    super().__init__(num_embeddings, dim, head_sizes, block_size)
File "vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py", line 668, in __init__
    assert (num_shards - 1) * self.part_n_hash_cols < self.n_hash_cols, (
AssertionError: Engram sharding leaves ranks without hash heads: 24 heads over 16 shards
```

The same command with `--tensor-parallel-size 8` on one node works (we have been serving this model with TP8 successfully, including GSM8K 99/100).

### Analysis

`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py`:

```python
self.n_hash_cols = len(head_sizes)                      # 24 for this checkpoint
self.tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
num_shards, head_rank = self._get_shard_info()          # -> (self.tp_size, tp_rank)
self.part_n_hash_cols = triton.cdiv(self.n_hash_cols, num_shards)
# TODO: Support row-wise sharding when there are too few hash heads.
assert (num_shards - 1) * self.part_n_hash_cols < self.n_hash_cols, (...)
```

`_get_shard_info()` returns `(self.tp_size, get_tensor_model_parallel_rank())` unconditionally - the sharding degree is hard-wired to the TP degree, and neither `EngramConfig` (`cpu_offload` / `embedding_across_dp` / `dp_shared_memory` / `use_thp`) nor any env var changes it.

`n_hash_cols = (max_ngram_size - 1) * n_heads = 3 * 8 = 24` is fixed by the checkpoint's `text_config`. Evaluating the assertion for all TP degrees that divide `num_attention_heads = 64`:

| tp_size | `ceil(24/tp)` | `(tp-1) * ceil(24/tp)` | `< 24` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 24 | 0 | yes |
| 2 | 12 | 12 | yes |
| 4 | 6 | 18 | yes |
| 8 | 3 | 21 | yes |
| 16 | 2 | 30 | **no** |
| 32 | 1 | 31 | **no** |

So the only usable degrees for this model are 1/2/4/8; 16 GPUs cannot form one replica.

### What is *not* the problem

Worth noting because it rules out the usual suspects for multi-node TP:

- **Kernels**: at TP16 the attention heads per rank become 4, which `_pad_to_supported_q_heads` pads up to 8, i.e. exactly the same `flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120._DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` entry `(8, 512)` used at TP8. We verified the dispatch check passes before launching.
- **Interconnect**: we benchmarked the 2-node fabric first (8x ConnectX-7 400G NDR per node, GDR enabled): 16-rank cross-node `all_reduce_perf` gives 39.5us @ 8 KB and 42.3us @ 32 KB, i.e. essentially the same per-collective latency as the single-node 8-rank collective we measured inside the decode loop with the torch profiler (43.8us for a 10 KB payload). So a small-message cross-node collective is not an obstacle here; the Engram assertion is the *only* thing blocking TP16.

### Expected behavior / suggestion

Either
1. implement the TODO (`row-wise sharding when there are too few hash heads`) so that `n_hash_cols < tp_size` is handled, or
2. at minimum make the sharding degree configurable (e.g. shard over a sub-group of the TP group / over DP) and/or fail with an actionable message that names the constraint (`n_hash_cols` vs `tp_size`) instead of a bare assertion.

A `ValueError` early in config validation would also be friendlier than aborting during model init after the placement group and weight loading have been set up.

### Environment

- vLLM 0.30.1rc1.dev382+g09c47db1c (nightly, uv), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, FlashInfer 0.7.1 (built from main), DeepGEMM 2.8.0+6901431 (main)
- 2 nodes x 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB, SM120), driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13
- ray 2.58.0, `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=0`
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`max_ngram_size` 4, `engram_n_heads` 8, `num_attention_heads` 64)

Happy to test a patch - we still have the 2-node ray cluster standing and can re-run immediately. This came out of the same SM120 bring-up tracked in #59203.

title: [Spec Decode] Fix KV cache group explosion for hybrid models
body:
## Purpose When profiling Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, we found the KV cache group_size become 1. This increases build metadata overhead. We found the target model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B layer buckets are [30 mamba, 10 full]. The DFlash drafter z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash adds [5 sliding, 1 full], the added 1 full attention layer that can't merge with the target's 10 full attention layers. The current logic used `min` as the group size [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.27.0/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L1245-L1246). `group_size = min([30, 10, 5, 1]) = 1` makes it to split into 46 groups of 1 layer each. So this PR update `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` to exclude buckets with 1 layer from the `min` computation. Result: layers [30 mamba, 10 full, 5 sliding, 1 full] become 10 groups instead of 46 groups. e2e output throughput improves 102% at batch size 1 on H200. ``` Group 0: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 1: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 2: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 3: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 4: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 5: MambaSpec, layers=5 Group 6: FullAttentionSpec, layers=5 Group 7: FullAttentionSpec, layers=5 Group 8: SlidingWindowSpec, layers=5 Group 9: FullAttentionSpec, layers=1 ``` Note: This PR does not cause regression for other models. ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┐ │ Model │ Before │ After │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B │ 4 groups (10 layers each) │ 4 groups (unchanged) │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash │ 46 groups (1 layer each) │ 10 groups │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + Eagle │ 41 groups (1 layer each) │ 5 groups │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (5:1 sw/full) │ 6 groups │ 6 groups (unchanged) │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤ │ gpt-oss-20b (12 sw + 13 full) │ 2 groups │ 2 groups (unchanged) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## Test Plan ``` pytest -s -v tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py ``` ## Test Result Unit tests passed. ## Profiling Profiled Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash on H200. Main: PR: Main: `build_attn_metadata` takes around 31ms, because [attn_metadata_builder.build](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.27.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py#L583) are called 46 times. PR: `build_attn_metadata` takes around 6ms, because [attn_metadata_builder.build](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.27.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py#L583) are called 10 times. ## title: [Perf] Enable small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill for DS V4.1 on SM90
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview


 Enable SM90 small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill for DeepSeek V4.1 by passing the actual TP-local query heads instead of padding them to 64

Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/pull/26
<!-- Summarize the change in 1-2 lines. Link relevant issues and PRs. -->

## Claims

  - Use native 8/16/32-head sparse prefill on SM90.
  - Preserve padding for FP8 decode and other architectures.

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

## Validation

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
---
```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
--seed 0 --port 8012 --max-model-len 500000 \
--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
--tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true,"revision":"dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277"}' \
--no-enable-prefix-caching --moe-backend humming -ep \
--max-num-seqs 1024 \
--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
-cc '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

title: [Attention] Move GDN common metadata compute out of per-group build

## Purpose During profiling I notice GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build() takes a long time (~900µs), because the batch level GDN spec decode metadata (masks, decode/prefill/spec split, token indices, query_start_loc cumsums) is computed repeatedly in each group build(). title: Support multimodal speculative decoding in draft_model mode
body:
## Purpose
This PR follows the needs discussed in the following issues and adds support for multimodal speculative decoding in vLLM’s `draft_model` (**both parallel and non-parallel draft mode**) mode:

* [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28947](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28947)
* [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33458](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33458)

Currently, vLLM does not support speculative decoding for multimodal models in `draft_model` mode. This PR adds support for the following scenarios:

1. **Target model + draft model are both multimodal models (VLMs)**
   Example: `Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct + Qwen2.5-VL-3B`

2. **Cross-modal speculative decoding** (target model is VLM, draft model is text-only)
   Example: `Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct + Qwen3-0.6B`  `Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct + amdPARD-Qwen3-0.6B`

The cross-modal adaptation is implemented with reference to the speculative decoding design in **SGLang standalone mode**.

---

## Background and Problem Statement

There are several key issues in the current vLLM `draft_model` path for multimodal scenarios:

* Multimodal support is determined using the **target model config**, which causes misclassification in the “VLM target + text draft” case
* M-RoPE / positional encoding cache and kernel position handling are incorrect in some paths, which can lead to:

  * startup failures (`NotImplementedError` / `AttributeError`)
  * position corruption under concurrency
  * reduced acceptance rate
* When both target and draft are VLMs (both using M-RoPE), the 3D M-RoPE positions are not preserved correctly
* Heterogeneous vocab-size combinations are overly restricted, blocking some practically safe combinations (e.g., using `Qwen3-0.6B` as draft for `Qwen2.5-VL-32B`)

This PR focuses on **correctness and functionality enablement**, so that multimodal / cross-modal speculative decoding can run correctly in `draft_model` mode.

---

## Changes

### 1. `eagle.py` (6 changes)

* **Use draft model config (instead of target model config) to determine `supports_mm_inputs`**
  Avoids misclassifying the draft model as multimodal in the `VLM target + text draft` scenario and entering the wrong code path.

* **Always initialize `self.positions`**
  Fixes potential `AttributeError` when the Triton kernel writes position buffers in the M-RoPE draft-model path.

* **Fix incorrect broadcasting in `_set_positions` under concurrency**
  Prevents 1D `positions` from being accidentally reduced to a scalar and broadcasting request-0’s position to the entire batch.

* **Fix `kernel_positions` computation in `set_inputs_first_pass` for cross-modal cases**
  In the `target(M-RoPE) + draft(1D RoPE)` scenario, computes the real sequential positions instead of using compressed M-RoPE time positions, preventing draft position / KV-cache misalignment.

* **Fix `mrope_positions` filling for dual-VLM (dual M-RoPE) scenarios**
  Directly copies the target’s 3D M-RoPE positions for input tokens, avoiding corruption of image-token H/W dimensions caused by kernel-written 1D positions.

* **Complete positional-encoding compatibility paths for multimodal / cross-modal speculative decoding**
  Unifies position propagation and cache alignment logic across M-RoPE and 1D RoPE combinations for target/draft pairs.

### 2. `speculative.py` (1 change)

* **Relax heterogeneous vocab validation**
  Only raises when `draft_vocab > target_vocab` (possible out-of-bounds risk); allows safe combinations where `draft_vocab < target_vocab` (may slightly reduce acceptance rate).

---

## Summary: Supported Scenarios

| Scenario                 | Before                                                     | After                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| VLM target + text draft  | Startup error `NotImplementedError`                        | ✅ Works, positional encoding aligned correctly |
| VLM target + VLM draft   | Startup error `AttributeError`, incorrect M-RoPE positions | ✅ Works, full 3D M-RoPE preserved              |
| Text target + text draft | Already worked                                             | ✅ Unaffected                                   |

---
## Test Plan

Dataset: MMStar
Environment: 4090D
Target model: `Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct`
Draft models: `Qwen3-0.6B`, `Qwen2.5-VL-3B`

### Commands

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
vllm serve /models/Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct/ \
--host 0.0.0.0 \
--port 30000 \
-tp 4 --max-model-len 10240 \
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 \
--speculative_config '{"model": "/models/Qwen3-0.6B/", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "method": "draft_model"}'
```

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \
vllm serve /models/Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct/ \

```

title: [ModelRunner V2] Speculative Decoding NGram GPU Implementations
body:
## Purpose


1. Added a new NGram GPU speculator.
The main feature is a new implementation at: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/ngram/speculator.py`, similiar to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29184.

2. Updated request state storage for NGram GPU.
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`
This changes how RequestState is initialized so that all_token_ids can stay densely resident on GPU instead of defaulting to UVA when ngram_gpu is active. As discussed in   #29184, the new n-gram speculator repeatedly scans active request token history, doing that from GPU-resident dense storage is much more appropriate than pulling through UVA-backed memory, this is a performance-oriented architectural change supporting the new feature.
The `model_runner.py` also injects req_states into speculators that need direct access to the persistent token store.

3. Added variable-length draft token plumbing
Several files were updated to support draft proposals where different requests may have different numbers of valid draft tokens:
`vllm/v1/outputs.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`
`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`
`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`

DraftTokenIds now includes:
`num_valid_draft_tokens: list[int] | None`.
Scheduler logic now truncates speculative tokens based on `num_valid_draft_tokens`.
`EngineCore adds _maybe_update_async_draft_token_ids()` to consume draft metadata from async execution and update scheduler state at the right time.

title: [Core] Shared abstractions for specialized decode kernels
body:
_(the text below is written by myself)_

This is an effort to (1) increase standardization and (2) limit LoC changes in model files as a result from adding numerous specialized decode kernels (_aka "monokernels"_). 

The kernels themselves will naturally remain difficult to review thoroughly, but ideally model code should remain easy to review. The abstraction layer should deliberately be made as thin as possible,

Heavily inspired by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61867, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60904.

**Note: this PR drops `--monokernel` in favor of `--specialized-decode`**

# 1. Goal

**An author of a specialized decode kernel should write:**

1. A FlyDSL/CuTeDSL implementation and its utilities, in `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`
2. The conditions under which it can run
3. Minimal glue connecting it to the model code

**The author should not have to write:**

1. Another new way to glue the kernel into the model code
3. Basic config checks during start up, re-used by many specialized kernels needs anyway (parallelism, spec decode, graph mode)
4. Checks of whether to run the specizlied kernel or regular vllm code at every step
5. TP rank agreement of the above
6. Updating of CUDA graph capture sizes
7. Kernel selection when one model has more than one specialized kernel
8. Optional: JIT/warm-up registration


This PR implements the latter points.

# 2. How

Declare when the specialized kernel can run:
```python
# refuse causes crash, skip causes fallback to regular vllm execution

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DecodeSpec(Generic[KernelT]):
    name: str
    supports: frozenset[Feature]
    widths: Callable[[VllmConfig], tuple[int, ...]]
    refuse_config: Callable[[VllmConfig], list[str]]
    refuse_model: Callable[[Any], list[str]]
    refuse_caches: Callable[[VllmConfig, KernelT, Mapping[str, Any]], list[str]]
    skip_step: Callable[[VllmConfig, KernelT, int], str | None]
    build: Callable[[VllmConfig, Any, tuple[int, ...]], KernelT]
```

`KernelT` is a stand-in for the entire model forward, implementing

```python
class DecodeImpl(Protocol):
    cache_layers: tuple[str, ...]

    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any: ...
    def bind_caches(self, caches: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None: ...
```

**Optional:** A kernel that compiles its launches from keys (one per width, per layer plan, or whatever the kernel keys on) can additionally implement

```python
@runtime_checkable
class DecodeWarmable(Protocol):
    def warmup_keys(self) -> list[Any]: ...
    def compile(self, key: Any) -> None: ...
```

which will cause the dispatcher to auto-register it for warmup. The existing DSv41 implementation uses this, and so would https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60889, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731, and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60683. The Kimi K3 nvidia kernel jits eagerly since its specialized decode kernel is not created in a region with an active jit registry; hence, this feature is optional.

Once the kernel author has written their CuteDSL/FlyDSL kernel, the two remaining points

> 2. The conditions under which it can run
> 3. Minimal glue connecting it to the model code

is implemented through a Spec and wiring the kernel code through a DecodeImpl. The remainder is taken place by the shared `SpecializedDecode` utility.

_Note: we deliberately put no further constraint on how one implements `run`. There is a big benefit letting each model decide exactly how to structure this. We've already seen many different ways of structuring the underlying flydsl/cutedsl kernels._

## 2.1 Model-side code

The model-side code will look like this:

```python
class MyForCausalLM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config, prefix=""):
        self.decode_spec = select_decode_spec(vllm_config, SPECS)
        self.specialized_decode: SpecializedDecode[MyKernel] | None = None

    def process_weights_after_loading(self):
        # optionally: this code can also be placed in the model state init, but then you cannot benefit from auto-registration of warmup
        if self.decode_spec is not None:
            self.specialized_decode = SpecializedDecode(
                self.model, self.vllm_config, self.decode_spec
            )

    def forward(self, input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors=None, inputs_embeds=None, **kwargs):
        decode = self.specialized_decode
        if decode is not None:
            step = decode.plan(positions, intermediate_tensors)
            if step is not None:
                return decode.run(step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
        return self.model(input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
```

plus one hook to prepare the kv cache

```python
class MyModelState(DefaultModelState):
    def initialize_kv_cache(self, kv_cache_config, block_tables):
        super().initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config, block_tables)
        if self.model.specialized_decode is not None:
            self.model.specialized_decode.bind_caches()
```

On the model side nothing else needs to be touched. 

# 3. How to: adding a second kernel for the same model

Say DSv4.1 gets a gfx942 kernel next to the gfx950 one. Write the FlyDSL kernel, then:

```python
# vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/specialized_decode.py

class DSV41Gfx942Kernel(DSV41Kernel):           # reuse what you want
    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any: ...
        ...
        return self.runner.run_gfx942_kernel(...)

    def compile(self, key):
        width, idx = key
        self.runner.kernels(width, self.plans[idx])


def _refuse_config_gfx942(vllm_config) -> list[str]:
    reasons = []
    if not current_platform.is_gfx942():
        reasons.append("needs a gfx942 GPU")
    ...
    return reasons


DECODE_SPEC_GFX942 = DecodeSpec[DSV41Gfx942Kernel](
    name="dsv41-cdna3",
    supports=frozenset({Feature.PIPELINE_PARALLEL}),   # no spec decode here
    widths=lambda cfg: tuple(range(1, 17)),            # fewer rows than gfx950
    refuse_config=_refuse_config_gfx942,
    refuse_model=_refuse_model,                        # shared with gfx950
    refuse_caches=_refuse_caches,
    skip_step=_skip_step,
    build=DSV41Gfx942Kernel,
)

SPECS = (DECODE_SPEC_GFX950, DECODE_SPEC_GFX942)
```

Then one line in the model:

```python
self.decode_spec = select_decode_spec(vllm_config, SPECS)
```

The dispatcher takes the first compatible spec. Specializing on something other than arch works the same way. A hyper-specialized batch-size 1 kernel can just set `widths= lambda cfg: (1,)` and be placed first in the `SPECS` list.

# 4. How to: a kernel that only covers part of a layer

A specialized decode kernel might cover only part of a layer, e.g. only o-proj through post-moe AR.

The common dispatcher has no concept of this, and does not need one, because the kernel owns the layer loop. Hence it can decide at every layer whether to run it as a single monokernel, or to run it in the regular vllm model code. 

When we run part of a layer as a specialized kernel, we simply run the regular vllm model code and _inject_ the specialized kernel:

```python
class DSV41Kernel:
    def run(self, step: Step, input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs) -> Any:
        self.model.prologue(input_ids, inputs_embeds, **kwargs)
        ....
        for idx in range(self.embed_layer, self.layer_end):
            layer, plan = model.layers[idx], self.plans.get(...)
            ffn = out = None
            if plan.ffn_only:
                ffn = partial(self.launch_ffn, plan)      # a part of a layer
            else:
                out = self.launch_whole(plan, hidden, positions, ...)
            if out is None:
                out = layer(hidden, positions, ..., decode_ffn=ffn) # run regular vllm and inject
            hidden, residual, post_mix, res_mix, pre_mix = out
        ...
```

```python
class DeepseekV4DecoderLayer(nn.Module):

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        ...
        decode_ffn: Callable | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        ... # run pre etc
        x = self.attn(positions, x, None)
        if self.use_sequence_parallel:
            x = sp_reduce_scatter(x)
        elif not self.attn.wo_b.reduce_results:
            # run the "partial-layer specialized decode kernel"
            if decode_ffn is not None:
                out = decode_ffn(x, residual, post_mix, res_mix, attn_pre)
                if out is not None:
                    return out

```

## 5. Add specialized decode support for a drafter

See the DSv41 code for an example. It's treated basically identically as to another other regular model.

# Validation

# 1. DeepSeek-v41 on MI350

On MI350, force max 8 seqs
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \

  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \

  --speculative-config "{\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":5}" \
```


title: [Bugfix] Fix pipeline load imbalance in scheduler
body:
## Purpose
In the current pipeline parallel implementation (non-Ray V2), the scheduler allows the first stage to greedily schedule requests up to the global max_num_seqs limit. It does not account for the capacity of downstream pipeline stages. This leads to severe load imbalance where the first stage becomes a bottleneck, causing downstream stages to starve or forcing the pipeline to process requests in inefficient "stop-and-wait" bursts.
This PR fixes the imbalance by introducing a constraint on the number of requests scheduled in the "pre-pipeline" phase. We calculate a fair share of requests per pipeline stage (max_num_pre_pipeline_reqs) and enforce this limit during the scheduling of running, new, and resumed requests.

**Examples:**
1. Underutilization (Small Batch): With max_num_seqs=32 and pipeline_parallel_size=2, if a user sends 16 requests, the scheduler might try to push all 16 into the first stage. This leaves the second stage idle initially and creates a bursty workload. Ideally, the load should be balanced (8 requests per stage) to keep the pipeline full.
2. Imbalance (Large Batch): With max_num_seqs=32 and pipeline_parallel_size=2, if the system is under heavy load (e.g., 32 requests), the first stage might grab a disproportionate share (e.g., 18 requests) while the second stage handles fewer (14 requests). Since the pipeline speed is limited by the slowest stage, the stage with 18 requests becomes a straggler, increasing overall latency.
