title: [Bug]: custom all-reduce creates its NVLink multicast reduce-scatter buffer mid-serving (not at startup); the run then crashes (Xid + CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED)
body:
## Summary

In `CustomAllreduce` (`vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py`), the NVLink-multicast ("multimem") reduce-scatter buffer is not created at startup. It is created the first time a reduce-scatter of a particular size happens, which can be many minutes into serving. On our 8× B300 node, the two runs that took this path both crashed right after the buffer was created. The many runs that never took it ran clean.

## Background

On NVLink-connected GPUs (MNNVL), custom all-reduce can run reduce-scatter on a low-SM "multimem" kernel. That kernel needs a dedicated multicast buffer: device memory mapped into an NVLink multicast object shared by all ranks. The other MNNVL buffers are set up when the communicator is constructed. This one is not.

## What the code does

1. `_select_reduce_scatter_backend` (`custom_all_reduce.py:621` on main at `242e4213f`) picks the `mnnvl_multimem` backend only when the reduce-scatter input is **larger than 16 MiB and at most 64 MiB**. These are `_DEFAULT_MNNVL_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE` and `_DEFAULT_MNNVL_MULTIMEM_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE` (lines 132–133).
2. The first time it picks that backend, it calls `_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer()` (line 674). That allocates and maps the multicast buffer **in the middle of serving**, while other kernels and CUDA graphs are running.
3. It then logs `Using the low-SM MNNVL multimem reduce-scatter kernel.` (line 682).

Whether a run ever lands in the 16–64 MiB window depends on how many tokens are batched at runtime. So the same deployment can hit this path in one run and not in another. The two thresholds are hard-coded defaults; there is no setting to change them.

## What we observed

- **Setup:** 8× NVIDIA B300 (sm_103), one node with NVSwitch. NCCL 2.30.7, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Kimi-K3 with TP=8 + expert parallel + decode-context-parallel 8, MegaMoE, CUDA graphs on.
- **Run 1:** the log line above appeared 13–14 minutes into the run. In the same second the GPU raised an NVML Xid error and cuBLAS failed with `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`, and the engine died.
- **Run 2:** same log line at the same point, then `EngineDeadError`.
- **Every other run on the same GPUs** (dozens, same config family) never logged that line and finished cleanly. ECC errors stayed at 0 and there were no row remaps, so a faulty GPU is unlikely.

We have not proven causation. The lazy buffer creation is the only code path unique to the two failing runs, and it ran immediately before the fault.

## Suggested fix

Do either of these:
- Create the multimem reduce-scatter buffer at communicator setup, like the other MNNVL buffers, so it never happens during serving.
- Make the two size thresholds configurable, so a deployment can stay out of the 16–64 MiB window without disabling custom collectives altogether.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Handle missing DP metadata in the two-sided NVLink all2all
body:
## Purpose

#54016 fixed this in `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py`: with expert parallelism but no data parallelism — it was hit with `TP=1, PCP=4, EP` — `ForwardContext.dp_metadata` is None, and `get_local_sizes()` asserted that it is not.

`flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided.py` still carries the unfixed copy of the same function:

```python
def get_local_sizes():
    dp_metadata = get_forward_context().dp_metadata
    assert dp_metadata is not None
    return dp_metadata.get_chunk_sizes_across_dp_rank()
```

The consumer in the same file is already written for the None case:

```python
# flashinfer_alltoall_dispatch
max_num_token = (
    max(global_num_tokens_cpu) if global_num_tokens_cpu is not None else x.shape[0]
)
```

so that fallback branch is unreachable today — the assert fires first. `flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided` is a currently selectable `all2all_backend`; only the older `flashinfer_all2allv` spelling of it is deprecated (`cuda_communicator.py:231`).

Reproduced without a GPU:

```python
>>> with patch.object(two_sided, "get_forward_context",
...                   lambda: SimpleNamespace(dp_metadata=None)):
...     two_sided.get_local_sizes()
AssertionError
>>> # same call on one_sided, after #54016
None
```

## Changes

- `get_local_sizes()` returns `None` when there is no DP metadata, exactly as #54016 did for the one-sided module.
- Widen `flashinfer_alltoall_dispatch`'s `global_num_tokens_cpu` annotation to `list[int] | None`, matching what its body already accepts.

I checked the other prepare/finalize backends that read `dp_metadata` — `deepep_v2.py:201`, `moonep.py:360`, `experts/batched_deep_gemm_moe.py:393` — and they all already guard for None. This was the last one that did not.

## Test

`tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_nvlink_local_sizes.py`, CPU-only (`cpu_test`), pins **both** modules to the same contract with and without DP metadata, so the two copies cannot drift apart again.

On current `main`:

```
FAILED tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_nvlink_local_sizes.py::test_get_local_sizes_without_dp_metadata[two_sided]
1 failed, 3 passed
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_nvlink_local_sizes.py
4 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files. I do not have an NVLink/MNNVL machine, so the end-to-end EP path is not exercised here; the change is the same three lines that were already reviewed and merged for the sibling module.

Found by taking a merged fix (#54016) and checking whether the same pattern survived in sibling implementations; the assertion failure and the new test were run on a CPU-only host, with and without the change. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [Performance]: FlashInfer AR+RMSNorm fusion cap is ~2x too high on multimem NVLink Hopper (TP8): it displaces the faster multimem all-reduce in the 256KB-512KB band
body:
### Proposal to improve performance

## Summary
On a multimem/NVSwitch sm90 node at TP8 (default settings), `AllReduceFusionPass` fuses `all_reduce + residual + RMSNorm` into flashinfer's one-shot trtllm AR whenever the message is below `FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB[90][8] = 0.5 MB`. But above **256 KB** the *unfused* all-reduce uses vLLM's fast `multimem_all_reduce` (NVLink multicast), which is faster than flashinfer's one-shot AR. So in the **256 KB–512 KB** band the pass trades the fast `multimem` AR for a slower fused AR — a net regression:
- **−1.9 to −4.3 µs/op** (microbench, CUDA-graph timed)
- **−3.4 % / −7.4 % decode throughput at batch 96 / 128** (Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP8)

Fix: cap the fusion at the size where the fast unfused AR takes over (256 KB here), gated on multimem availability.

## Environment
8×H200 (sm_90), NVLink/NVSwitch, TP8, bf16. vLLM `0.1.dev1916`, flashinfer `0.6.11.post2`. Defaults `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=1`, `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0`, `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0`.

## Root cause
`cuda_communicator.all_reduce` sends the unfused AR to vLLM's custom one-shot kernel below `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES["9.0"][8] = 262144 B` and to `multimem_all_reduce` at/above it (the NCCL-symm-mem and flashinfer-regular-AR branches are off by default). `AllReduceFusionPass` emits flashinfer's one-shot trtllm AR+RMSNorm for any message below `FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB[90][8] = 0.5 MB`. So in 256 KB–512 KB the pass replaces the fast `multimem` AR with the slower flashinfer one-shot; the ~2 µs RMSNorm saving doesn't offset flashinfer being ~2× slower than `multimem` there.

## Evidence
**1. Per-op** (microbench, CUDA-graph timed, default config, H=2048). `delta = unfused − fused` µs/op; `>0` = fusion wins:

| tokens | bytes | fused | unfused (AR backend) | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 48 | 192 KB | 10.4 | 11.2 (custom) | +0.86 |
| 64 | 256 KB | 12.1 | 12.1 (multimem) | +0.05 |
| 96 | 384 KB | 15.0 | 13.1 (multimem) | −1.87 |
| 128 | 512 KB | 17.9 | 13.6 (multimem) | −4.30 |

Crossover is byte-governed, constant at 256 KB across hidden sizes 2048/4096/7168 (token thresholds 64/32/18).

**2. The regression is specifically `multimem`.** With `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0` (unfused AR stays custom one-shot), the 256–384 KB band flips back to a win (N=64 +3.79, N=96 +1.48 µs). (A small −1 µs residual remains only at 512 KB.)

**3. End-to-end** (decode throughput, cap 0.5 vs 0.25 MB; median of 6, 256 steps):

| batch | cap=0.5 | cap=0.25 | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 10584 | 10655 | +0.7 % (noise) |
| 96 | 14421 | 14912 | +3.4 % |
| 128 | 17425 | 18713 | +7.4 % |

Localized to the band (≈0 at batch ≤64), well outside per-batch noise (~0.2–0.3 %).

## Proposed fix
Cap the fusion at the active fast-AR threshold: `min(current_cap, CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES["9.0"][8])` when multimem is on (or the ~128 KiB NCCL-symm-mem bound when `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1`), gated on availability; unchanged on non-multimem nodes (fusion wins to ~384 KB there). Keep byte/MB-shaped. Thresholds are config-overridable (#23722). Precedent: #42409, #37756.

## Config caveat
With the non-default `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1`, NCCL-symm-mem wins from ~128 KiB, moving the crossover lower — hence keying the cap to the active fast-AR threshold rather than a fixed value.

title: [Core] Add hybrid_ep backend
body:
## Purpose

Add `hybrid_ep` as a new `--all2all-backend` option for MoE expert parallel deployments, addressing a request from the Nemotron inference team. Standard DeepEP crashes on GB200 (aarch64 incompatible), blocking sparse MoE dispatch/combine on that platform.

This backend uses `HybridEPBuffer` from the DeepEP hybrid-ep branch with fused `dispatch_with_permute` / `combine_with_unpermute` kernels that merge routing permutation with all-to-all communication, reducing memory pressure and kernel launch overhead compared to the standard `deep_ep.Buffer` path. Freely inspired by the TorchTitan HybridEP integration (pytorch/torchtitan#2207).

Key differences from `deepep_high_throughput`:

- Uses `HybridEPBuffer` (fused permute+communication kernels) instead of `Buffer` (separate steps)
- NVLink-only mode -- works on any NVLink-connected topology (NVL8, NVL72, etc.)
- Supports CUDA graph capture -- during CG capture/replay, the dispatch handle from warmup is reused, bypassing the CG-incompatible permute_preprocessing path
- Dedicated `HybridEPPrepareAndFinalize` class with its own code path

This PR includes AI-generated code (Claude via Cursor).

Usage:
```bash
# Install DeepEP from hybrid-ep branch
bash tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh --deepep-branch hybrid-ep

# Serve with HybridEP
vllm serve <model> --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend hybrid_ep

# Or switch to standard DeepEP HT (no code change, just a flag)
vllm serve <model> --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput
```

## Test Plan


```bash
# Config wiring test (no GPU required)
pytest tests/compile/test_config.py::test_hybrid_ep_backend_wiring -v

# E2E with hybrid_ep (8 GPUs, dummy weights)
CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend hybrid_ep \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager

# E2E with CUDA graphs (default mode, no --enforce-eager)
CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend hybrid_ep \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --load-format dummy

# Verify deepep_high_throughput still works independently
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --load-format dummy --enforce-eager
```


## Test Result

- Config wiring test: pass
- E2E hybrid_ep (DP=8, 8x H100, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, dummy weights): server starts, logs confirm Using HybridEPAll2AllManager, completions API returns valid responses
- E2E hybrid_ep with CG (DP=8, 4-node GB200): pass, no error
- E2E deepep_high_throughput (DP=2): server starts, logs confirm Using DeepEPHTAll2AllManager, fully independent from hybrid_ep changes

title: [Core][Distributed] Size custom all-reduce buffers at init so batch-invariant mode can use them
body:
### Purpose

Fixes #50136.

`CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar()` decides per call whether to use the custom
all-reduce or fall through to NCCL, based on `inp_size < self.max_size`. The
all-reduce tensor is `[num_tokens, hidden_size]`, so that decision tracks the
token count of the forward pass — i.e. batch composition — and the same request
can take different reduction orders in different batches. Under
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` that is a correctness bug, which is why
`ParallelConfig` currently forces `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` and every
batch-invariant TP run pays the pinned-NCCL path.

This removes the size dependency instead of the whole code path.

**Which review this is, settled.** The open question was whether the intended guarantee is *per request* (a request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or *per engine* (a given engine configuration is internally consistent) — a bug under the first reading, a documented limitation under the second. @tolleybot answered it on this thread: per-request is what the production case needs, since regression tests and trusted production output require a prompt to give bitwise-identical logprobs however it is batched, across runs and restarts. This PR is therefore a fix, not a feature.

### What changed

**1. Decide once, at init** (`custom_all_reduce.py`). Under
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, derive the largest all-reduce the engine can ever issue
from `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size` and size `max_size` —
and therefore the IPC buffers — to cover it. The gate can then never flip
mid-run. If the requirement exceeds the cap, or the config cannot be read,
custom all-reduce declines at init and logs why, rather than disabling itself
silently.

**2. Fail loud, never fall back silently** (`should_custom_ar`). If an
all-reduce still exceeds the buffer, raise instead of falling through to NCCL.
This is the load-bearing design decision. A silent fallback is precisely the
mechanism in #50136; a fix whose failure mode reproduces the bug it fixes would
be worse than no fix. If the bound is ever wrong — an unmodelled path, a padded
width I did not account for — the run stops with a message naming the tensor
size and the buffer, instead of quietly producing non-reproducible logprobs.

**3. Pin the kernel** (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh`). Force
`cross_device_reduce_1stage` for all sizes under batch invariance, and hard
error on an explicit `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage`. The 1-stage kernel
sums over absolute rank indices with no address reordering (its own comment
notes the result is bitwise identical across ranks); the 2-stage kernel
partitions by size and rotates accumulation order per rank, so it cannot be
invariance-safe.

**4. Drop unaudited backends** (`cuda_communicator.py`). Under batch
invariance, exclude AITER's custom all-reduce from the dispatch chain.
FlashInfer is already excluded upstream by #52998, which landed the same guard
while flipping the FlashInfer default on; this change builds on that guard
rather than repeating it. QuickReduce is not excluded — it is constructed only
on ROCm (`current_platform.is_rocm()`), so it is unreachable on the CUDA
configurations validated here, but on ROCm it would be tried first. Under batch
invariance on CUDA the chain is `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`.

The env pin in `override_envs_for_invariance()` is retained as
belt-and-braces: since #52998, the communicator itself excludes FlashInfer
under batch invariance, so the pin is redundant for dispatch but guards
against future refactors of that logic.

**5. Stop forcing the disable** (`config/parallel.py`), now that (1) makes the
decision fixed for the process lifetime. The platform-support disable
(`if not current_platform.use_custom_allreduce()`) is untouched.

**6. Test + docs.** A TP≥4 batch-invariance test in `tests/v1/determinism/`
(the suite currently runs everything at TP=1, so the all-reduce path was
untested — that gap is why #50136 was possible to write), and
`docs/features/batch_invariance.md` updated to describe the new behaviour.

### Validation

Bitwise comparison of output token IDs **and** per-step logprobs as raw float32
bit patterns (not `allclose`) across batch compositions: bs=1 reference, full
mixed batch, shuffled batch, and tile-boundary batches of 17 and 65.

| Arm | Config | Invariance | Custom AR engaged | Largest tensor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | dense, TP=4, patched | clean | 4/4 ranks, 9918 calls each | 25,165,824 B |
| 2 | dense, TP=4, `disable_custom_all_reduce` (control) | clean | none, as expected | — |
| 3 | dense, long context (2048/4096) | clean | 4/4 ranks | 25,165,824 B |
| 4 | MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B), TP=4 | clean | 4/4 ranks | 33,554,432 B |
| 5 | fault injection (buffer forced to 4 KiB) | raises | — | — |
| 6 | throughput, patched vs control | clean both | 4/4 vs none | 25,165,824 B |

Three things make those greens checkable rather than merely green.

**The bound predicts the observed maximum exactly.** Dense: largest tensor
through the custom kernel = 25,165,824 B = `8192 × 1536 × 2`. MoE:
33,554,432 B = `8192 × 2048 × 2`. Both are exactly
`max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size`, which is the formula the
buffer is sized from. Resulting buffers were 30 MiB and 40 MiB per rank.
Engagement counts are read from each worker with `collective_rpc`, so they are
exact per-rank values (`calls=9918`, identical on ranks 0–3), not log-derived
estimates.

**Every patched arm crossed the old threshold.** 25,165,824 B is 3.0× the
8 MiB constructor default that applied before this change, and the MoE arm's
33,554,432 B is 4.0×. (The `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` clamp is unreachable
under batch invariance, since `override_envs_for_invariance()` sets
`VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0`.) So these runs exercised tensors that
previously fell through to NCCL — they sat in the regime where the gate used to
flip, not one where it never would have.

**Both guards fire with their intended messages.** Injecting a 4 KiB buffer so a
real all-reduce exceeds it:

```
RuntimeError: custom all-reduce received a 25165824 byte tensor, above the 4096
byte batch-invariant buffer. Falling back to NCCL would break batch invariance.
Re-run with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT unset, or file a bug with the model and
max_num_batched_tokens so the bound can be corrected.
```

And `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`:

```
VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage is incompatible with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1:
cross_device_reduce_2stage partitions the message by size and accumulates in a
rank-rotated order, so an element's summation order changes with message size
(i.e. with batch composition) and differs across owning ranks.
```

Throughput, batch-invariant mode, same workload, identical output (14,784
tokens in both arms):

```
patched (custom AR)    8006.4 tok/s   TTFT p50 53.40 ms   TPOT p50  8.48 ms
control (NCCL only)    3906.0 tok/s   TTFT p50 67.61 ms   TPOT p50 17.34 ms
                                                           → 2.05x
```

See the note on this number in "Tested / not tested" below — an earlier run on
a different workload measured +84%, so the direction reproduces but the
magnitude does not.

#### Re-validation on current main (post-#52998)

Rebased onto `main` @ `6259572b2` (which includes #52998's FlashInfer default
flip and its batch-invariance guard) and re-validated on the same hardware
class: 4× A100-SXM4-40GB, NVSwitch NV12 all-to-all (P2P 262.0 GB/s,
24 µs/hop — matching the original run).

- Dispatch under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, TP=4, with FlashInfer
  **installed**: resolves to `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`; FlashInfer, AITER,
  QuickReduce, and both symm-mem paths not constructed.
- Dense arm: CLEAN across all 5 batch compositions, 4/4 ranks engaged (exact
  per-rank counts via `collective_rpc`), largest tensor
  25,165,824 B = 8192 × 1536 × 2 — byte-identical to the original bound
  prediction — within the 30 MiB buffer, `largest <= max_size` on every rank,
  zero tracebacks.
- Routing tests 5/5 green; `pre-commit --all-files` clean for this PR's files
  (mypy ran and passed; the one repo-wide failure,
  `test-nonroot-entrypoint`, also fails on unpatched main).

Two recorded deviations from the original run: host driver 595.71.05 (vs
580.65.06; same nvcc 13.0.88 toolchain), and
`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;9.0a"` — required because current main does not
compile for SM 8.0 alone (a GDN/KDA `#ifdef` guard mismatch in
`csrc/libtorch_stable`, upstream and unrelated to this PR; will be reported
separately). The A100 still executes SM 8.0 code.

GPU evidence above was gathered at `d3cb5924b6`; the pushed commit
`edfb2f5b2d` differs from it by a one-line ruff-format wrap in a test file (no
runtime code).


The full determinism harness used for the matrix above now lives on a
follow-up branch --
https://github.com/mosafariuk/vllm/tree/test/batch-invariant-validation-harness
-- so this PR carries the fix plus its regression test: 175 LOC functional
(`vllm/` + `csrc/`) and 228 LOC of test, +404/-8 across 9 files.

The all-gather / reduce-scatter guards described under "not tested" below are
likewise split out, onto a branch that applies on top of this one and will be
opened as a PR once this lands.

### Tested / not tested


**Tested.** 4× A100-SXM4-40GB with NVSwitch (`NV12` all-to-all), driver
580.65.06, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, built from source. TP=4, bf16,
chunked prefill and CUDA graphs enabled, for a dense model (Qwen2.5-1.5B,
`hidden_size=1536`) and an MoE model (Qwen3-30B-A3B, `hidden_size=2048`).

Re-confirmed on the final head `2bd487e29f` on 4x A100-SXM4-80GB with NVSwitch
(`NV12` all-to-all), driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, from a
prebuilt `sm_80/sm_89/sm_90` wheel: TP=4 dense, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`,
bitwise invariant, with custom all-reduce engaged on 4/4 ranks (16,473
dispatches per rank) and a largest reduced tensor of exactly 25,165,824 bytes
against a 31,457,280 byte buffer. Engagement was read from the per-rank
counters via `collective_rpc`, not scraped from the log.

**Not tested, and guarded rather than assumed:**

- **The MXFP4-padded MoE path.** `fused_moe` pads the routed hidden dimension
  before the all-reduce and truncates after, so the reduced tensor is wider
  than `hidden_size`. That padding is gated to the TRT-LLM MXFP4 path
  (`hidden_dim_unpadded > 0`), which needs Blackwell-class hardware I do not
  have. The MoE arm exercised MoE collectives and expert-parallel shapes but
  not the padded width.
- **Multi-node symmetric memory / MNNVL multicast.** It disables itself when
  the group is not single-node, so TP=4 on one node cannot reach it.
- **TP sizes other than 4**, non-NVSwitch topologies, and speculative decoding.
- **Sequence parallelism (`pass_config.enable_sp`), which is measured
  non-invariant and is not fixed by this change.** The two size-gated
  collectives the SP path uses, `should_custom_all_gather()` and
  `should_custom_reduce_scatter()`, carry the #50136 defect verbatim. Guards
  for both are prepared on a follow-up branch, offered as a PR the moment this
  one lands; **this change leaves all-gather / reduce-scatter dispatch
  untouched.** Those guards would be necessary but not sufficient anyway.
  One mechanism is the compile-range split:
  `SequenceParallelismPass.is_applicable_for_range()` returns
  `compile_range.start >= sp_min_token_num`, observed here as
  `'compile_ranges_endpoints': [511, 8192]` with SP on against `[8192]` with
  it off, so batches below the threshold reduce with one all-reduce and
  batches at or above it with reduce-scatter + all-gather. **That is not the
  whole cause.** vllm-project/vllm#56370 reports the same divergence with
  `sp_min_token_num=1`, i.e. SP applied to every compile range and no split at
  all, so the SP path is not batch-invariant independently of the threshold.
  Either way the cause sits above the communicator, where no dispatch-level
  guard can reach it; the precise mechanism is still open. Measured on 4x A100 TP=4
  under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with `enable_sp=True, sp_min_token_num=512`,
  on a build that did carry those guards: both declined on all four ranks, the
  largest custom all-reduce tensor fell to 1,216,512 bytes, and 3 of 4 batch
  compositions still diverged, against a clean `enable_sp=False` control. So
  SP is non-invariant with the guards or without them, and nothing in this
  change's scope alters that. It wants the treatment vllm-project/vllm#51292
  gave `fuse_allreduce_rms`, which is not attempted here.
- **The `fuse_allreduce_rms` compile pass (cc >= 90).** Reported by @tolleybot
  on #50505 and confirmed in source: `enable_allreduce_rms_fusion` turns the
  pass on for TP>1 + FlashInfer + Hopper/Blackwell, independent of
  `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. The pass `register_replacement`s
  `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` with a direct
  `flashinfer_comm.allreduce_fusion(...)` call, so the reduction never enters
  the communicator and neither `should_custom_ar()` nor the `.cuh`
  `force_1stage` gate is consulted. It returns False on SM80, which is why the
  A100 matrix is clean — our own run logs show `fuse_allreduce_rms: False` in
  the config dump. Verified non-deterministic on H100 by @tolleybot (8 distinct
  bitwise groups over 8 runs). vllm-project/vllm#51292 disables the pass under
  batch invariance; the two changes compose.

For the unreached paths above **except** the fusion pass and sequence
parallelism, custom all-reduce
either declines at init with a logged reason or hits the fail-loud
`RuntimeError` in `should_custom_ar()`, so none of them can silently fall back
mid-run. The fusion pass and sequence parallelism are the exceptions. The fusion pass
bypasses the dispatch entirely, so on cc >= 90 it silently produces
non-reproducible output. Sequence parallelism is non-invariant above the
communicator — the compile-range split is one mechanism and, per
vllm-project/vllm#56370, not the only one — so it stays non-invariant whether
or not the dispatch-level guards are present. Both are the
same class of failure as #50136, moved up a layer.

**The throughput result is directional, not a specification.** Two runs on this
configuration measured **+84%** and **+105%** on different workloads — same
direction, materially different magnitude. The control is not ordinary NCCL:
`override_envs_for_invariance()` pins `NCCL_MIN/MAX_NCHANNELS=1` and
`NCCL_NTHREADS=1`, so the baseline is deliberately serialised NCCL, which is
the cost this change removes. Treat the direction as reproducible and the
magnitude as workload-specific.

### The memory trade-off — the call I made

**Correction: an earlier revision of this section counted only `max_size`, and
that understated the cost by roughly half.** Raising `max_size` grows two
buffers, not one:

- `meta_ptrs` = `ops.meta_size() + max_size` (`custom_all_reduce.py:289`)
- `buffer_ptrs` = `max(max_size, max_all_gather_size, max_reduce_scatter_size)`
  (`custom_all_reduce.py:297`), whose defaults are 2 MiB and 16 MiB
- `rank_data` = a fixed 8 MiB (`custom_all_reduce.py:310`), unchanged by this PR

`ops.meta_size()` is `sizeof(vllm::Signal)` = **4864 B**. So for
`max_size >= 16 MiB` the per-GPU total is `2 * max_size + 8 MiB + 4864 B`.

| `hidden_size` | raw bound | `max_size` (1.25× margin) | **total per GPU** | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1536 (Qwen2.5-1.5B, measured) | 24 MiB | 30 MiB | **68 MiB** | fits |
| 2048 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, measured) | 32 MiB | 40 MiB | **88 MiB** | fits |
| 8192 (70B class) | 128 MiB | 160 MiB | **328 MiB** | fits |
| 16384 | 256 MiB | 320 MiB | — | exceeds cap → declines at init, uses NCCL |

For reference the pre-PR default (`max_size` = 8 MiB) already allocated
32 MiB/GPU by the same formula, since `buffer_ptrs` is floored at the 16 MiB
reduce-scatter default.

Only the 1536 and 2048 rows are measured; the 8192 and 16384 rows are the
formula evaluated, not runs. The cap is on `max_size`, not on the total, so
**256 MiB/rank admits ~520 MiB/GPU at the limit** — that is the honest ceiling
and it is higher than the cap alone suggests. I have left the cap value
unchanged rather than quietly retuning it against the corrected arithmetic;
if 520 MiB/GPU is too much headroom, lowering the cap is a one-line change and
I would rather you pick the number. The 1.25× margin (which exists because I
could not bound the MoE padding exactly) is likewise a policy number.

If you would rather not spend the memory at all, the alternative is to keep the
blanket disable and document why it is load-bearing — I am happy to send that
instead; it is a small docs-and-comment change.

### How the validation was checked

Five defects were found during this work by cross-checks rather than by the
tests passing. Each is listed with the check that now catches its class,
because the checks are the part that generalises.

1. **`git apply --3way` reported per-file success, then rolled the whole patch
   back** when a later file failed — leaving the kernel gate, the config change
   and the backend filtering absent with no error printed. Caught by a semantic
   grep for the changed symbols, not by the tool's output. That grep now runs
   before every build.
2. **The hand-port to current `main` dropped `self._custom_ar_calls = 0` and
   `self._custom_ar_max_bytes = 0`** while keeping all six uses. `__init__` has
   ten early returns, so grepping the attribute name still passed; the defect
   surfaced as an `AttributeError` at engine init. Now covered by an AST check
   asserting that any attribute other methods read is assigned at the **top
   level** of `__init__`, so completing the constructor guarantees it exists.
   The check was verified to fail on the pre-fix file.
3. **The semantic grep itself produced two false alarms** — it matched
   lowercase `batch_invariant` where the code says `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`,
   and matched `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` against upstream's unrelated
   platform-support guard. It now asserts the batch-invariance disable is
   absent **and** the platform guard is present, as separate conditions.
4. **The test's engagement assertion read `capfd` before engine shutdown.**
   Under `capfd`, fd 1 is a regular file rather than a tty, so worker processes
   block-buffer their output and flush only on exit. The assertion read zero
   markers while 21 were present in the log — a false red that, if "fixed" by
   weakening the assertion, would have removed the guard. The test now reads
   the counters directly from each worker via `collective_rpc`, which is
   immune to buffering, yields exact per-rank counts, and additionally asserts
   `largest <= max_size`.
5. **An earlier harness summed per-rank milestone floors** and reported a call
   count the data did not support. It now reports rank count and per-rank
   floor separately, and the test reports exact counts.

The test ships with a counterpart, `test_engagement_assertion_can_fail`, that
runs the same engine with the custom path disabled: output stays invariant, so
a test checking only reproducibility would pass, and the engagement assertion
must fail. It runs by default rather than being skipped.

### The contract question — resolved

Is the intended guarantee **per request** (this request is bitwise reproducible
under any batching) or **per engine** (a given engine configuration is
internally consistent)? The size gate is a bug under the first reading and a
documented limitation under the second. I had assumed the first because it is
what makes batch invariance useful for RL rollouts where trainer and sampler
must agree, but flagged it as an assumption about intent.

@tolleybot resolved it in
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50505#issuecomment-5246281546:
per-request is what the production case needs — regression tests plus trusted
production output mean a prompt has to give bitwise-identical logprobs no
matter what it is batched with, across runs and restarts, and per-engine
consistency does not help there. He also noted that the `ParallelConfig` guard
in #51292 was a placeholder rather than a vote for per-engine. This PR is
scoped as a fix on that basis.

---

*Disclosure: this work was done with AI assistance (Claude). I ran the
experiments, reviewed the changes, and take responsibility for the content.*

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix mxfp8 scale swizzling after EP all-to-all
body:
## Purpose

Fixes vllm-project/vllm#42118.

The EP/DP-EP prepare-finalize paths delay scale swizzling until after all-to-all because swizzled scale layouts are padded/reordered and are not valid per-token communication payloads. The delayed swizzle logic only handled `nvfp4`, so `mxfp8` activation scales reached the FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP4/MXFP8 MoE kernel in row-major layout.

This PR centralizes post-all-to-all scale layout conversion and routes:

- `nvfp4` through the existing `nvfp4_block_scale_interleave` path.
- `mxfp8` through `swizzle_mxfp8_scale` to produce the CUTLASS F8_128x4 layout.

This is not duplicating an existing PR. I checked:

- `gh issue view 42118 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "42118 in:body"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "mxfp8 scale swizzle"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "FLASHINFER_CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP8"`

The open PR searches returned no matching PRs.

AI assistance was used to implement and validate this change. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing the changed lines and validating behavior.

## Test Plan

- Run whitespace diff check.
- Run focused Python compile check for changed files.
- Run relevant pre-commit hooks for changed Python files.
- Run focused unit test for the new scale-layout helper.

## Purpose

NCCL-based AlltoAll backend for DP + EP deployments. The implementation is straightforward torch.distributed alltoall. It could be helpful for many to have an option for running DP + EP on multi gpu pcie servers without nvlink.

## Test Plan

8x RTX PRO 6000 server:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/deepseek-moe-16b-chat --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 1024 --max_num_batched_tokens 8192 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend nccl_alltoall --api-server-count=1
```

## Test Result
This is a Prefill-only test with max output tokens 1. Please note that the results below are from a single run just to give ballpark numbers, and not a rigorous benchmark.

**nccl_alltoall**

| dataset | Throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|
| openai/openai_humaneval/None | 41,063.6 |
| hotpotqa/hotpot_qa/fullwiki | 77,943.0 |

| dataset | Throughput (tok/s) |

title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643.

## Claims

- EPLB raises decode throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 NVL72 by +3.7% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank and +7.7% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP16 the step is about 3% shorter, but the throughput gain is within run-to-run noise.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on this branch, one GB200 node with 4 GPUs. They ran before the rebase onto 64175d3827; the 5 newer commits on main touch none of these files.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_matches_router_under_graph_replay`) | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE parity test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.

title: RR-Evict: Fine-Grained Prefix Cache Eviction beyond LRU for Agentic LLM Serving
body: LLM-based agents execute long-horizon tasks through repeated model calls interleaved with tool execution and user interaction. As each call extends the history accumulated in previous turns, prefix caching avoids repeated prefill of the agent's entire context. However, the aggregate cache footprint grows with context length and concurrency, forcing serving systems to reclaim cached KV tensors. We identify recency synchronization: accesses to an agent's cached history refresh its cache nodes together, causing least recently used (LRU) eviction to concentrate on a few agents' private histories. When a fully evicted agent returns, it must recompute nearly its entire accumulated context, producing a large time-to-first-token (TTFT) outlier even if most other requests retain substantial cache reuse. We present RR-EVICT, a fine-grained prefix-cache eviction strategy that distributes reclamation across idle agent trajectories. RR-EVICT visits agents in round-robin order and evicts a tail chunk from each, preserving reusable prefixes for more agents when capacity remains for idle state. Returning agents can reuse these partial histories and recompute smaller missing suffixes. The policy requires no prediction of future arrivals or tool latency. We implement RR-EVICT in SGLang and evaluate conversational and coding-agent workloads under colocated and prefill-decode-disaggregated serving. Compared with LRU, RR-EVICT reduces P99 TTFT by up to 75.4% and P99 uncached prompt tokens by up to 65.7%.

title: [Misc] Report prefix cache hit rate in vllm bench serve
body:
## Purpose

`vllm bench serve` reports latency and throughput, but not the prefix cache
hit rate — so benchmarking prefix caching means manually scraping `/metrics`
and computing the rate by hand. That is error-prone: the Prometheus counters
are cumulative since server start, and the server's logged hit rate uses a
rolling 1000-request window — neither corresponds to "this run".

This mirrors the existing spec-decode / diffusion metric handling: snapshot the
`vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total` / `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` counters
before and after the main run and report the per-run hit rate (plus raw queries
and hits) in the console summary and the saved JSON. The rate uses vLLM's own
definition (`hits / queries` in tokens, see `CachingMetrics.hit_rate`). When
prefix caching is disabled or the backend is not vLLM, the fields are omitted.

## Test Plan

vLLM server with prefix caching (on by default), benchmarked with a shared
512-token prefix so the cache is exercised:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --port 8000
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --num-prompts 200 \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 64 --random-prefix-len 512 \
  --max-concurrency 16 --save-result --result-filename pc_on.json

title: [WIP][Kernel] Enable GDN batch-invariant prefix caching
body:
## Purpose

Enable `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` together with prefix caching on Qwen GDN hybrid models.

Today this fails at scheduler init (`NotImplementedError: ... does not yet support Mamba cache alignment`) because prefix cache puts GDN into mamba `align` mode while BIC needs a 64-token FLA grid.

This PR:

- Uses one shared grid `lcm(FLA_CHUNK_SIZE=64, mamba_state_block_size)` for prefill chunks and prefix-cache hits (hits are floored onto the grid; a full-prompt hit is not).
- Rounds hybrid `block_size` up to a multiple of 64 (1056 → 1088) so the grid stays usable for short prefixes.
- Temporarily includes GDN BIC from #49827 / #45819 so CI can run while those PRs are still open. Drop that commit when they land. 

Related: #49827, #45819, #48613, #42960.

## Test Plan

Set `VLLM_GDN_PC_TEST_MODEL` to a GDN checkpoint (e.g. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B). Tests skip without it.

```bash
export VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1
export VLLM_GDN_PC_TEST_MODEL=/path/to/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
export VLLM_TP_SIZE=2
export VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0
pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_gdn_prefix_cache_batch_invariant.py -s -v

```bash

## Test Result

**Before:** engine does not start (`NotImplementedError` above).

**After (bitwise):** engine starts, `block_size` 1056 → 1088, alignment=1088. Same-path hit BS=1 vs BS=N is bitwise identical (`prefix-1100` real hit; `ragged-200` floors to 0). `RESULT: PASS`.

title: [Bug]: Prefix caching silently inert on hybrid Mamba2 models when max_model_len < auto-selected block size
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

- vLLM main (0.23.1rc1.dev, commit 429f40574 base)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), single GPU
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4` (`NemotronHForCausalLM`, hybrid Mamba2 + attention)

</details>

### Describe the bug

On hybrid Mamba2 models (e.g. NemotronH), `--enable-prefix-caching` is silently inert whenever `max_model_len` is smaller than the attention block size that vLLM auto-selects for the hybrid KV layout. Prefix caching is accepted without warning, but the cache never records a single hit, so users get none of the expected TTFT benefit and no indication why.

**Mechanism.** For hybrid models, `Platform.check_and_update_config` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`, the "Setting attention block size to N tokens" path) raises `cache_config.block_size` up to `attn_block_size` so the attention page size is >= the mamba page size:

```python
if cache_config.block_size < attn_block_size:
    cache_config.block_size = attn_block_size
    logger.info("Setting attention block size to %d tokens ...", attn_block_size)
```

For this model that yields `block_size = 8320`. Block-hash prefix caching only registers a **complete** block, so if `max_model_len < block_size` no request can ever fill one block, and the prefix cache is structurally unable to hit. Nothing warns the user that enabling prefix caching will do nothing in this configuration.

### Reproduction

Same model and GPU, only `--max-model-len` differs. Send the same prompt three times (temperature 0), measure streaming TTFT and read `/metrics`.

**Inert — `--max-model-len 4096` (< block_size 8320):**

```
--enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 4096   # block size auto-set to 8320
```
| request | TTFT |
|---|---|
| 1 (cold) | 0.349 s |
| 2 (repeat) | 0.249 s |
| 3 (repeat) | 0.259 s |

```
vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total  10608.0
vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total     0.0      # zero hits across 10.6k queries
```

**Working — `--max-model-len 16384` (> block_size 8320), same prompt (~12.8k tokens):**

| request | TTFT |
|---|---|
| 1 (cold) | 1.510 s |
| 2 (repeat) | 0.313 s  (4.8x faster) |
| 3 (repeat) | 0.315 s |

```
vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total  38448.0
vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total     16640.0   # ~43% hit rate
```

Same model, same `block_size = 8320`; the only difference is `max_model_len`. Below the block size, hits are impossible; above it, prefix caching works as expected.

### Impact

Any hybrid-Mamba user (NemotronH, and likely other MambaMixer2 models whose page-size coupling inflates `block_size`) who runs with `max_model_len` below the auto-selected block size gets prefix caching that is enabled but completely inert, with no log message pointing at the cause. `max_model_len 4096` is a common setting, so this is easy to hit unknowingly.

### Suggested fix

At config validation, when `enable_prefix_caching` is set and the resolved `cache_config.block_size > max_model_len` for a hybrid model, emit a warning that prefix caching will be ineffective in this configuration (block size exceeds max model len, so no full block can form), and suggest raising `--max-model-len` at or above the block size. A warning is the minimal fix; auto-adjusting or erroring could be discussed.

Happy to send a PR for the warning if that direction is agreeable.

title: [Bug]: Speculative decoding (mtp and dflash) silently disables prefix-cache hits for hybrid GDN models on nightly; worked on v0.24.0
body:
(analysis by Fable 5)
### Your current environment

- DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`/`sm_121a`, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory), Docker `--network host --gpus all --ipc host`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` → reports `v0.28.1rc1.dev43+g6f7df92a8`
- Comparison baseline on the same host: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0`
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN: 48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers, built-in MTP head). Also reproduced with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (rev `dedf8df`).
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`, env `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the current nightly, enabling **any** speculative decoding method (built-in `mtp` or `dflash`) on a hybrid GDN model silently drops `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` to **0** — align-mode prefix caching engages at startup (log: `Mamba cache mode is set to 'align' for Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) but never hits, and repeated long prompts pay full re-prefill. The identical command minus `--speculative-config` hits normally. No crash, no warning — the caching is just inert, so this is easy to miss in production.

A/B on the same host, same model, same 18,219-token prompt sent twice (`max_tokens=10`):

| nightly config | TTFT req1 → req2 | `prefix_cache_hits_total` delta |
|---|---|---|
| APC only (no spec) | 9.46 s → **0.64 s** | **17,248** |
| APC + `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` | 23.6 s → 13.9 s* | **0** |
| APC + `{"method":"dflash", ..., "num_speculative_tokens":7}` | 12.9 s → 12.5 s | **0** |

\* the MTP row also shows a large decode regression on this platform (10.5 tok/s vs 19.7 on v0.24.0 with the same flags — possibly a separate sm_121 issue; noting it for context, not the subject of this report).

**On `v0.24.0`, MTP + align-mode APC coexist correctly** on the same host/model: repeated 9,901-token prompt → 8,000 tokens hit, TTFT 7.27 s → 1.33 s, with `mtp` k=3 active. So spec+APC coexistence for hybrids existed and regressed somewhere between v0.24.0 and the current nightly.

Repro (nightly):

```bash
docker run --rm --init --network host --gpus all --ipc host \
  -v /opt/models:/models -e CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a \
  vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4 \
  --served-model-name bench --port 10099 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# send any >3,300-token prompt twice; watch vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total stay 0
# drop --speculative-config and the second send hits ~all full blocks
```

Possibly related but distinct: #53670 (hits occur but recompute per hit), #41884 (DFlash+APC IndexError crash — we see silent zero-hit, not a crash), #26201 (tracking).

Is the suppression intentional (spec-decode + hybrid APC support not yet wired on the new path), or a regression? If intentional, a startup warning like the align-mode one would save users from silently losing their cache. Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware.

title: [Bugfix] Fix MLA KV cache blocks not zeroed on reuse, causing CUDA crashes under concurrent load
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

Fix a CUDA illegal memory access crash in MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) models under sustained concurrent load.

Reproduced with [kakaocorp/kanana-2-30b-a3b-instruct-2601](https://huggingface.co/kakaocorp/kanana-2-30b-a3b-instruct-2601) (DeepSeek V3 architecture) with FP8 dynamic quantization on NVIDIA H200.

When KV cache blocks are freed by completed requests and reallocated to new ones, they retain stale data from the previous request. For standard attention (`FullAttentionSpec`), these blocks are zeroed before reuse via the `KVBlockZeroer` pipeline. However, MLA attention (`MLAAttentionSpec`) is completely excluded from this zeroing pipeline, so reused blocks contain stale KV data that corrupts FP8 computation and crashes CUTLASS kernels.

The crash occurs under **continuous concurrent load** because sustained traffic causes frequent block alloc/free cycles, leading to stale data accumulation in reused blocks. It is reproducible both with and without prefix caching, though disabling prefix caching (`--no-enable-prefix-caching`) makes it deterministic since blocks are directly reused without hash-based validation.

**Root cause:** `MLAAttentionSpec` is a subclass of `FullAttentionSpec`, but three places use exact type matching (`type(x) is FullAttentionSpec`) instead of `isinstance()`, excluding MLA from the entire block zeroing pipeline:

1. **`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`** — `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` only checks `has_mamba_layers`. Since this property gates the entire zeroing pipeline (kernel initialization, block ID collection, and GPU zeroing execution), MLA models never have any blocks zeroed.

2. **`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`** (2 occurrences) — `type(self.kv_cache_spec) is FullAttentionSpec` in `allocate_new_blocks()` and the external-computed-tokens path excludes MLA blocks from the `new_block_ids` collection. Even if the pipeline is enabled, no MLA block IDs are ever collected for zeroing.

3. **`vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`** — `type(spec) is not FullAttentionSpec` in `KVBlockZeroer.init_meta()` skips MLA layers when building the GPU memory address table for the Triton zeroing kernel. Without MLA segment addresses, the zeroing kernel cannot zero MLA KV cache memory.

All three must be fixed together — the pipeline has a gate (1), data collection (2), and execution (3) stage, and MLA was excluded from all of them.

**Fix:**
- Add `has_mla_layers` property and include it in `needs_kv_cache_zeroing`
- Change `type(x) is FullAttentionSpec` → `isinstance(x, FullAttentionSpec)` (2 files, 3 occurrences)

## Test Plan

- **Serving benchmark** — Verify the model serves correctly under concurrent load with variable-length inputs:

```bash
# Start server
vllm serve <MLA_FP8_MODEL> --port 8000

# Run benchmark (128 concurrent, variable-length inputs)
vllm bench serve \
  --model <MLA_FP8_MODEL> \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name random \
  --num-prompts 2048 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 128 \
  --random-input-len 2048 \
  --random-output-len 512 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.3 \
  --ignore-eos \
  --seed 42
```

> **Note:** `--random-range-ratio 0.3` creates variable input/output lengths that diversify block alloc/free patterns, triggering stale-data reuse.

## Test Result

- **Environment:** NVIDIA H200 (141GB) x 1, vLLM v0.17.1
- **Model:** (DeepSeek V3 architecture, MLA + FP8)

Before fix — Server crashes after ~775 requests with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`:

title: [Quantization] Fix misleading NVFP4 Marlin linear warning on FP4-native GPUs
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #47749

`MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel.process_weights_after_loading` unconditionally logs
"Your GPU does not have native support for FP4 computation". That claim is wrong on
SM100/SM12x: `ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod` pins the Marlin kernel for weight-only
`W4A16_NVFP4` checkpoints on every GPU (`modelopt.py` — "For W4A16 there is exactly one
valid kernel, so we pin it"), because those checkpoints carry no activation scales and
native FP4 GEMM needs FP4 activations. So RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000 users loading ModelOpt
`W4A16_NVFP4` (or mixed) checkpoints are told their Blackwell GPU lacks FP4 support —
three reporters on #47749 read it exactly that way, and #23497 was filed off the same
message.

This PR branches the message on `cutlass_fp4_supported()` (the same predicate the NVFP4
kernel selection stack uses):

- FP4-native builds now get an accurate message: weights are dequantized to the
  activation dtype inside the Marlin kernel; weight-only FP4 checkpoints such as
  `W4A16_NVFP4` only support this path; performance may still degrade.
- All other configurations keep the existing message byte-for-byte.

The warning itself is kept in both branches — #31346 (which removed it) was closed
because maintainers want a warning here, since Marlin is still not native FP4 compute.

Not a duplicate: #45192 rewords the MoE-site copy of this message in
`prepare_nvfp4_moe_layer_for_marlin` (`marlin_utils_fp4.py`) and does not touch this
file. The `[marlin.py:34]` warning quoted in #47749's logs comes from the linear kernel
site fixed here; no open PR covers it. The two PRs are complementary.

This change was prepared with AI assistance. I ran
the verification below; the change affects a log message only, so model outputs,
accuracy, and kernel behavior are unchanged (no eval delta possible).

## Test Plan

A/B dummy-boot on real SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, CUDA 13.0), current main
(a0f6d767e): tiny 2-layer Qwen3-style config with
`quantization_config = {"quant_method": "modelopt_fp4", "quant_algo": "W4A16_NVFP4",
"group_size": 16, "ignore": ["lm_head"]}`, booted with `load_format="dummy"`,
`quantization="modelopt_fp4"`, `enforce_eager=True`, then one `llm.generate()` call so
the forward actually runs through `apply_fp4_marlin_linear`.

```bash
python boot_47749.py   # stock, then with this patch applied
ruff check vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/nvfp4/marlin.py
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/nvfp4/marlin.py
```

## Test Result

Stock main on SM120 (misleading):

```
WARNING [marlin.py:34] Your GPU does not have native support for FP4 computation but
FP4 quantization is being used. Weight-only FP4 compression will be used leveraging
the Marlin kernel. This may degrade performance for compute-heavy workloads.
```

With this PR on SM120:

```
WARNING [marlin.py:41] FP4 weights will be dequantized to the activation dtype inside
the Marlin kernel instead of using this GPU's native FP4 tensor cores (weight-only FP4
checkpoints such as W4A16_NVFP4 only support this path). This may degrade performance
for compute-heavy workloads.
```

Both runs boot and generate successfully through the Marlin kernel. Ruff check and
format pass. What I did not run: the non-FP4-native branch on real pre-Blackwell
hardware (none on hand) — that branch's string is asserted byte-identical to the
current message, so behavior there is unchanged by construction.

title: [Bug]: RTX 5090 / SM120 ModelOpt mixed NVFP4 checkpoint falls back to Marlin W4A16 path and warns no native FP4 support
body:
### Your current environment

### Environment

  - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
  - Compute capability: 12.0
  - VRAM: 32607 MiB
  - Driver: 610.43.02
  - CUDA UMD: 13.3
  - OS: Arch Linux, GNOME desktop
  - vLLM: 0.24.0
  - PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
  - flashinfer-python: 0.6.12
  - Python: 3.11.15
  - Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4`

  `nvidia-smi`:

  ```text
  NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 12.0, 610.43.02, 32607 MiB
  NVIDIA-SMI 610.43.02
  CUDA UMD Version: 13.3
  ```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

  `nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4` on RTX 5090 / SM120 resolves as `modelopt_mixed`, detects `W4A16_NVFP4`, then
  routes part of the model through the Marlin FP4 path and logs that the GPU does not have native FP4
  support.

  The hardware does support FP4: this is an RTX 5090 Blackwell GPU with compute capability 12.0. The issue
  appears to be vLLM backend selection / support for ModelOpt mixed NVFP4 checkpoints on SM120, or a
  misleading capability warning from the Marlin fallback path.

  ### Command

  vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8082 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --load-format safetensors \
    --attention-backend flashinfer \
    --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
    --max-model-len 32768 \
    --max-num-seqs 1 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1]}' \
    --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
    --skip-mm-profiling \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice

  ### Relevant Logs

  Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
  Using max model len 32768
  Chunked prefill is enabled with max_num_batched_tokens=8192.

  Detected ModelOpt fp8 checkpoint (quant_algo=FP8).
  Detected ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint (quant_algo=NVFP4).
  Detected ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint (quant_algo=W4A16_NVFP4).

  Initializing a V1 LLM engine ... quantization=modelopt_mixed ... device_config=cuda

  Using FlashInfer for top-p & top-k sampling.
  Selected FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for ModelOptFp8LinearMethod
  Using AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER backend.

  WARNING [marlin.py:34] Your GPU does not have native support for FP4 computation but FP4 quantization is
  being used. Weight-only FP4 compression will be used leveraging the Marlin kernel. This may degrade
  performance for compute-heavy workloads.

  ### Observed Behavior

  vLLM starts and serves the model, but prompt processing and token generation are much slower than expected
  for a native-FP4-capable Blackwell GPU.

  The concerning part is the Marlin warning saying the GPU lacks native FP4 support, despite the GPU being
  an RTX 5090 / SM120. From inspecting vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py in vLLM 0.24.0,
  the W4A16_NVFP4 path appears to instantiate MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel directly, so this may be a backend-
  selection/support gap rather than actual hardware detection failure.

  ### Expected Behavior

  On SM120 / RTX 5090, ModelOpt NVFP4 layers should use native Blackwell FP4-capable kernels where
  supported, or the warning should clearly state that only this specific W4A16_NVFP4 checkpoint path
  currently falls back to Marlin.

  If W4A16_NVFP4 native execution is not currently supported on SM120, it would be helpful for the logs/docs
  to make that explicit, because the current warning implies the GPU itself lacks native FP4 support.

  ### Additional Notes

  I also saw repeated FlashInfer autotune OOM fallback warnings during startup before disabling autotune:

  [Autotuner]: OOM detected, falling back to default tactic

  Disabling autotune reduced that noise/startup pressure, but does not address the Marlin FP4 fallback
  warning.

  Related issues I found, but none seemed to exactly cover this single-GPU RTX 5090 + Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 +
  modelopt_mixed + W4A16_NVFP4 Marlin fallback case:

  - #23497
  - #31085
  - #44022
  - #44881
  - #46268
  - #47365

title: [Bugfix] Fix NVFP4 shape mismatch in flashinfer_scaled_fp4_mm #50557
body:
Fixes: #50577

Fixes shape mismatch assertion error when loading NVFP4 checkpoints that store weights in transposed format (in_features Fixes shape mismatch assertion error when loading NVFP4 checkpoints that store weights in transposed format (in_features // 2, out_features) instead of the expected (out_features, in_features // 2).

The fix adds conditional weight transpose in
ModelOptNvFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading(), matching the pattern used in FP8 methods. This resolves the assertion 'a.shape[1] == b.shape[1]' failure in flashinfer_scaled_fp4_mm for models like AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4 on SM120+ hardware.

Fixes: #50577

## Purpose

Some NVFP4 checkpoints (e.g. AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4) store weights in the
standard PyTorch layout `(in_features // 2, out_features)` rather than the
vLLM-expected `(out_features, in_features // 2)`. Unlike the FP8 linear methods
in `modelopt.py` (which transpose weights after loading), the NVFP4 method did
not perform this transpose, causing `flashinfer_scaled_fp4_mm` to hit the
assertion `a.shape[1] == b.shape[1]` during `profile_run()` on SM120+ hardware
(e.g. RTX 5060 Ti).

## Test Plan

Reproduce the original failure:

```bash
vllm serve AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0}' \
  --port 8000

title: [NVIDIA] Support nvfp4 quantization
body:
Forked from [this PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/12519), we decide to separate the fp4 quantization and fp4 gemm as two PRs. (1) fp4 quantization focuses on how to convert higher precision to fp4, which only depends on the sm100a (i.e. ptx 8.7) and could be merged today (This PR); (2) fp4 gemm focuses on the gemm itself which needs to wait for the cutlass 3.8 to release.

And we have addressed the comments in the original PR in here as well for the quantization part. We will rebase the PR on this one later.

`tests/v1/determinism/test_nvfp4_batch_invariant.py::test_dense_nvfp4_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_e2e` compares the needle prompt's logprobs across batch sizes with `torch.testing.assert_close(needle_logprobs, baseline_logprobs)`, i.e. with the default fp32 tolerances (`rtol=1.3e-6`, `atol=1e-5`). title: LoRA Triton kernel crashes with NVFP4 (modelopt_fp4) quantization - CUDA illegal memory access
body:
## Environment

- **vLLM version**: 0.25.1
- **Model**: GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (NVFP4 quantized via ModelOpt, `modelopt_fp4` quant config)
- **LoRA**: Combined LoRA adapter, rank r=96
- **GPU**: NVIDIA GPU with NVFP4 support
- **vLLM launch command**:
```bash
vllm serve <model_path> \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-modules glm-lora=<lora_adapter_path> \
  --max-lora-rank 96
```

## Problem

The vLLM server starts successfully and the NVFP4-quantized model loads without errors. However, the **first generation request** crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access error originating in the LoRA `lora_shrink` Triton kernel:

```
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

The crash trace points to `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py` — the Triton kernel `lora_shrink` encounters an illegal memory access when processing the output of NVFP4-quantized linear layers.

## Key Observations

1. **Base model (no LoRA) works fine**: Serving the NVFP4-quantized model without LoRA adapters produces correct output. This isolates the crash to the LoRA path.

2. **The dtype mismatch was fixed but the crash persists**: NVFP4 kernels were outputting `float32` (from `torch.get_default_dtype()`), while LoRA expects `bfloat16`. A fix to set `out_dtype = model_config.dtype` (see companion PR #48861) resolves the dtype assertion error in `lora_shrink_op.py`, but the Triton kernel **still crashes** with an illegal memory access even after dtypes match.

3. **The crash is in the Triton kernel itself**: After the dtype fix gets past the assertion, the `lora_shrink` Triton kernel fails at runtime with a CUDA illegal memory access. This suggests a memory layout or alignment issue with how NVFP4-quantized layer outputs are passed to the LoRA Triton kernels — the tensor layout/strides from NVFP4 dequantization may not match what the Triton kernel expects.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Quantize a model to NVFP4 using TensorRT-ModelOpt (produces `modelopt_fp4` format)
2. Launch vLLM with LoRA enabled:
```bash
vllm serve <nvfp4_model_path> \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-modules my-lora=<adapter_path> \
  --max-lora-rank 96
```
3. Send a generation request using the LoRA adapter:
```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "my-lora", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 10}'
```
4. Observe the CUDA illegal memory access crash in `lora_shrink`

## Expected Behavior

LoRA adapters should work with NVFP4-quantized models, or at minimum fail gracefully with a clear error message rather than a CUDA illegal memory access.

## Additional Context

- The companion PR fixing the `out_dtype` dtype mismatch (#48861) is a prerequisite — without it, the crash manifests as a dtype assertion error rather than an illegal memory access.
- The issue appears to be in how the LoRA Triton kernels (`lora_shrink`, `lora_expand`) handle tensors produced by NVFP4 dequantization kernels — potentially a stride/contiguity/alignment assumption that does not hold for NVFP4 outputs.
- This was discovered while working with GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with a combined LoRA adapter (r=96), but may affect other NVFP4-quantized models with LoRA as well.

🤖 AI assistance was used in preparing this issue report.
