title: [deepseek_v4] DeepSeekV4MTP loader silently skips top-level head.weight + embed.weight → 0% MTP draft acceptance with no error
body:
## Summary

`vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.mtp.DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights` silently skips top-level `head.weight` and `embed.weight` when the saved artifact stores them at the top level (not as `mtp.0.head.weight` / `mtp.0.emb.tok_emb.weight`). The MTP layer's `shared_head.head` (ParallelLMHead) and `embed_tokens` (VocabParallelEmbedding) stay uninitialized → MTP draft head emits garbage logits → **0% MTP acceptance with no load-time error**. Speculative decoding produces draft tokens that are 100% rejected by the verifier.

## Mechanism

`DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights` runs this loop:
```python
for name, loaded_weight in weights:
    name = name.replace("mtp.0.", "")  # no-op on top-level keys like "head.weight"
    spec_layer = get_spec_layer_idx(name)
    if spec_layer is None:
        continue  # ← top-level head.weight, embed.weight die here
    ...
```

For a key like `head.weight`:
- `name.replace("mtp.0.", "")` returns `head.weight` unchanged
- `get_spec_layer_idx("head.weight")` returns `None`
- Loop hits `continue` → key never routed to the MTP layer
- MTP layer constructed `shared_head.head` as ParallelLMHead but no weight ever assigned → keeps init random values

## Repro

1. Save a DSv4-Flash artifact via `transformers.save_pretrained` (the canonical path). MTP weights land at upstream naming `mtp.0.*` but `head.weight` + `embed.weight` stay at top level.
2. Serve with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
3. Watch `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total / vllm:spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total`. Result: drafts produced, accepted = 0.

We hit this exact scenario in [`canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp) iteration 9. Smoke artifact had 797 `mtp.0.*` keys at first and got 0% acceptance silently. Diagnosis trace in [`FINDINGS_FOR_SIBLING.md`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/FINDINGS_FOR_SIBLING.md) §C14.

## Workaround (production-validated)

Postprocess injects `mtp.0.head.weight` (FP32 copy of `head.weight`) and `mtp.0.emb.tok_emb.weight` (BF16 copy of `embed.weight`) as full duplicates. Working example: [`scripts/fixup_artifact.py`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/scripts/fixup_artifact.py). The sibling artifact `canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4-FP8-MTP` applies the same pattern (799 mtp.* keys vs our pre-fix 797 — the 2 deltas are these aliases).

After the workaround, MTP acceptance lands at 69.94% over 200 random prompts (raw data in [`benchmarks/phase2/acc_*.json`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/tree/main/benchmarks/phase2)).

## Suggested fix

Option A — `DeepSeekV4MTP.load_weights` should explicitly route top-level `head.weight` to `mtp.{N}.shared_head.head.weight` and top-level `embed.weight` to `mtp.{N}.embed_tokens.weight` (one line added before the `continue`):

```python
for name, loaded_weight in weights:
    # Re-route top-level head/embed to the MTP slot (model-level keys that
    # the MTP draft tower needs but get filtered out by the spec-layer check)
    extra = []
    for layer_off in range(self.config.num_nextn_predict_layers):
        if name == "head.weight":
            extra.append((f"mtp.{layer_off}.shared_head.head.weight", loaded_weight))
        elif name == "embed.weight":
            extra.append((f"mtp.{layer_off}.embed_tokens.weight", loaded_weight))
    if extra:
        # process each routing manually + continue
        for n, w in extra: weight_loader(n, w)
        continue
    # ... existing mtp.0. routing
```

Option B — raise at construction time when `shared_head.head` / `embed_tokens` end up uninitialized. Either is fine; silent 0% acceptance is the worst possible failure mode for spec-decode.

## Severity

Anyone who quantizes DSv4-Flash and ships an artifact via the standard `transformers.save_pretrained` path will hit this silently. The sibling NVFP4 team hit it and worked around it; we hit it independently and worked around it; future MTP-preserving quantizations will hit it too unless this is fixed in the loader.

title: [deepseek_v4 / DeepGEMM] paged_mqa_logits kernel asserts on next_n=3 → num_speculative_tokens capped at 1 on Hopper
body:
## Summary

`vllm serve --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'` crashes during `profile_cudagraph_memory` on Hopper (H200, sm_90a) with:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Assertion error
  (/home/ubuntu/src/vllm/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits.hpp:233):
  next_n == 1 or next_n == 2'
```

vLLM passes `next_n = num_speculative_tokens + 1` into DeepGemm's `smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` kernel (k draft + 1 main verifier in the lookahead window). The assertion enforces `num_speculative_tokens <= 1`. With `k=1`, `next_n=2` passes. With `k=2`, `next_n=3` fails. The error message is misleading — it sounds like the kernel allows up to 2 speculative tokens, but it actually allows up to 2 total lookahead positions.

## Reproducible on

- vLLM `~/src/vllm` HEAD `50d9dd902` with cherry-picked PRs #43248+#43288+#43290+#43319
- H200 SXM5 (Hopper, sm_90a), TP=2
- DSv4-Flash W4A16+FP8+MTP artifact (`canada-quant/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A16-FP8-MTP`, public)
- `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`: same assertion fires (the paged_mqa_logits kernel is logits-side, not attention-backend-specific)

## What I've ruled out

DeepGemm has separate Blackwell-only assertions in `attention.hpp:210` and `:338` that constrain `arch_major == 10 and next_n == 1`. Those don't fire on Hopper. The `paged_mqa_logits.hpp:233` assertion is the active one on Hopper and accepts `next_n in {1, 2}`.

## Impact

`num_speculative_tokens=1` is the practical max on Hopper in this build. We measured 1.49× decode speedup at bs=1 with k=1 (TPOT median 6.02ms with MTP vs 8.93ms without). At k=2 the theoretical ceiling rises to ~1.85-2.0×, matching the sibling NVFP4-FP8-MTP B300 artifact's published 2.03× number. We're leaving ~25% of the MTP speedup on the table due to this assertion.

Raw throughput data:
- https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/tree/main/benchmarks/phase2
- Summary: https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/benchmarks/phase2/2026-05-22T195133Z-throughput-summary.md

## Suggested fix

Two options:

1. **Widen the assertion** in `smxx_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits.hpp:233` to allow `next_n` up to whatever the kernel actually supports (presumably 4 or higher; DSv4-Flash's MTP block is designed for higher k). This requires DeepGemm-side changes in `deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM`.

2. **Surface the constraint in vLLM's config validation** — when `--speculative-config num_speculative_tokens > 1` is set AND the model uses the paged_mqa_logits kernel path on Hopper, emit a clear error at startup rather than letting the cudagraph capture fail with a confusing assertion message.

Option 2 is the cheaper path for vLLM-side. Option 1 unlocks the actual speedup.

## Tracking

Filed by the canada-quant team during W4A16+FP8+MTP quantization work. See [`FINDINGS_FOR_SIBLING.md`](https://github.com/canada-quant/dsv4-flash-w4a16-fp8-mtp/blob/main/FINDINGS_FOR_SIBLING.md) §C15 for the full diagnosis. The sibling artifact (B300, NVFP4) is on `arch_major == 10` paths and may hit different assertions; happy to coordinate if there's a cross-arch fix.

title: [Bug]: b12x NSA+MTP speculative decoding hangs on PCIe TP=8 — NCCL topology-aware scheduling fix
body:
### Your current environment

8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, PCIe-only TP=8, Ubuntu 24.04, vLLM main + b12x

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug: b12x NSA + MTP speculative decoding hangs on PCIe TP=8

When running GLM-5.1 or Kimi-K2.6 with b12x `B12X_MLA_SPARSE` backend + MTP speculative decoding on PCIe-only 8-GPU setup (TP=8, no NVLink), vLLM **always hangs** during decode. This is not intermittent — it is deterministic.

### Root Cause

Three layers of conflict:

1. **NCCL on PCIe topology**: NCCL's default ring/tree communication pattern conflicts with b12x's barrier sync. During MTP verify, the all-reduce for draft token scoring and b12x's cross-GPU KV sync compete for the same PCIe bandwidth. Timing skew → deadlock.

2. **b12x scheduling vs MTP dynamic batch**: b12x's CUDA Graph requires fixed input shapes and static `page_table_1` layout. MTP verify produces variable-length accepted tokens, causing `nsa_cache_seqlens` to diverge from graph-captured state at replay time.

3. **NSA indexer dangling indices**: Draft tokens write temporary KV entries. If verify rejects them, KV cache rolls back but `topk_indices` from the indexer still reference the now-invalid entries → garbage attention output (e.g. XML tag leakage in tool calls).

### Fix

1. **NCCL patch**: Force NCCL to respect PCIe topology — route collective operations along the actual PCIe switch hierarchy instead of assuming uniform interconnect. This prevents barrier misalignment between MTP verify all-reduce and b12x KV sync.

2. **Rewrite b12x scheduling logic**: Replace the static CUDA-Graph-only decode path with a topology-aware scheduler that dynamically selects execution path based on current phase (draft / verify / committed). The scheduler is aware of which GPU pairs share PCIe switches and which cross NUMA boundaries, and adjusts sync barriers accordingly.

3. **Topology awareness**: On W790E-SAGE SE with 8 GPUs, PCIe switch topology and NUMA affinity determine TP communication latency distribution. Without topology-aware scheduling, NCCL picks worst-case paths → barriers never align → guaranteed hang.

### Result

After fix: TTFT < 0.3s, no hangs, MTP + b12x NSA coexist correctly.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: WIP [RFC]: SupportsReload, a single post-load contract and reload verifier (follow-up to #59502)
body:
## TL;DR

#59502 makes reload cheap and safe for **quant methods**. The weakest part of reload is everything **around** them:

- model-level `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL) hooks that reload never calls;
- `load_weights` code that writes params directly;
- weight-derived tensors that nobody owns;
- a global reload flag that every PWAL has to branch on.

On main, each of these silently serves stale or wrong weights.

This RFC proposes one small contract with a fixed place for every kind of post-load work. Model authors implement it, and the framework can **verify** it before an update starts:

| Kind of work | Where it goes | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| Per-shard transform (TP narrowing, permutation, layout scatter, `-exp(A_log)`) | the param's `weight_loader` | on every load |
| Per-module checkpoint → kernel conversion | module PWAL: **always transform, build once** | on every load, as the module completes |
| Weight-derived values held by kernels (alphas, `1/a_scale`, bmm scales) | kernel `refresh()`, **called by the framework** | after every load, cold start included |
| Cross-module derived values (mHC broadcast, DSpark stacks) | `SupportsReload.refresh_model()` | after every load, cold start included, last |
| Non-weight setup (compile, device placement, geometry) | `post_load_setup()` | cold start only |

Four consequences:

1. **No global reload flag.** The `reload_mode()` / `is_reloading()` flag from #59502 goes away.
2. **No model-level weight hook.** The free-form model `process_weights_after_loading()` stops doing weight work.
3. **One sanctioned pattern** for model-specific changes to generic layers.
4. **`SupportsReload` is a verifiable claim.** `verify_reload(model)` scans declarations, tensor ownership, the init snapshot vs the live model, load coverage, configuration, and post-update invariants. It returns SAFE, UNSAFE or UNVERIFIED per item, and the engine refuses unsafe updates under CUDA graphs.

## Background: what main does today

All references are to main @ `240785b82c`.

### Cold start
`BaseModelLoader.load_model` (`model_loader/base_loader.py:62`) runs these steps in order:

1. `initialize_model`, then `record_metadata_for_reloading` (the meta snapshot);
2. `load_weights`;
3. `process_weights_after_loading` (`model_loader/utils.py:133`), which itself runs:
   - retie;
   - quant-method PWAL for each module with a `QuantizeMethodBase`;
   - attention PWAL (`dtype`);
   - **model-level hook**.

Modules without a `quant_method` are visited by neither PWAL pass. The model hook exists mainly to reach them, through delegation loops like `for layer in layers: layer.ffn.finalize_mega_moe_weights()`.

### Reload
Layerwise reload (`model_loader/reload/layerwise.py`):

1. restores checkpoint-format params on meta;
2. buffers loader calls;
3. replays them;
4. runs quant PWAL;
5. `copy_`s the results into the original tensors.

It does **not** call the model hook or retie.

### Where post-load work lives today, and whether reload reproduces it

| Location | Examples | On reload today |
|---|---|---|
| Constructor | conv1d `unsqueeze(1)`, alias buffers, padding fills | Safe: the snapshot is taken after `__init__` |
| `weight_loader` | TP narrowing, Mamba `-exp(A_log)`, DSv4.1 permute-on-load (#60064), MegaMoE direct layout (#60096) | Safe |
| Model `load_weights` code outside loaders | sink copies, DSv4 shared-expert padding, V3.2 FP8 indexer pairing, finalize-in-load | **Risky**: params are on meta, so direct writes are no-ops |
| Quant PWAL | requant, transpose, repack, shuffle, **kernel build** | Values are right. Kernel objects and off-registry tensors are rebuilt at new addresses. |
| Attention PWAL | KV scales, MLA absorption | Re-run. Host-float scales can't reach captured graphs. |
| Model hook | MegaMoE, mHC, DSpark stacks, ROCm preshuffle, dots3 fusion, compile | **Not run**: stale or wrong |
| Forward / lazy caches | GLM-5-Next `_merged_conv_weight` | **Stale** |

### Problems this RFC addresses

1. **Model hooks are cold-start only and have no reload contract.** There are 20 of them, all under `vllm/models/`; none are in `vllm/model_executor/models/`. They fall into these kinds:
   - delegation;
   - transform-then-drop: MegaMoE sets its raw params to `None`; dots3 runs `del self.experts`;
   - derived-from-live;
   - in-place rewrite: ROCm preshuffle, with no guard;
   - storage aliasing;
   - non-weight setup.
2. **Direct writes skip the reload wrapper.** `param.data.copy_(...)` or `params_dict[n][:k].copy_(...)` in `load_weights` runs while params are on meta. `meta.copy_(cpu)` succeeds and does nothing (verified with PyTorch). The module never completes, and its old tensors are put back. Affected:
   - gpt-oss sinks (`gpt_oss.py:723-728`);
   - gpt-oss Quark experts;
   - gpt-oss fused BF16 experts;
   - DSv4 / V4.1 / HY-v4 `attn_sink`;
   - mimo-v2 FP8 qkv;
   - about 18 `default_weight_loader(param, …)` call sites.
3. **PWAL mixes transforms with one-time work, and `reload_mode()` is how #59502 separates them.** Every PWAL author has to know about the flag. The one-time work includes:
   - kernel construction: `Fp8MoEMethod._init_moe_kernel` runs on every PWAL (`fp8.py:693, 711`);
   - quant-config capture;
   - `register_buffer`;
   - the AITER MLA precompile (~50 s).
4. **Weight-derived state with no owner.** On reload these keep their old values while CUDA graphs keep reading their old addresses:
   - plain tensor attributes: `hc_attn_fn_broadcast`, `_context_kv_norm_weights`, ROCm `_gateup_scale`;
   - kernel-object tensors: `a1_gscale`, Triton MXFP4 `PrecisionConfig`;
   - closures: CPU `layer.cpu_linear`.
5. **Model-specific changes to generic layers are done ad hoc**, four different ways:
   - a model-hook rewrite (ROCm preshuffle);
   - a quant-method subclass (`DeepseekV4HeterogeneousMxfp4MoEMethod`);
   - a quant-method swap (GLM-5.2 `GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod`);
   - an **instance monkeypatch** of `quant_method.process_weights_after_loading` (DSv4 CPU `wo_a`, `cpu/cpu_sparse.py:308`).
6. **Nothing tells you in advance whether a reload will work.**
   - The loader's "all weights loaded" check exempts every module whose `quant_method` defines PWAL (`default_loader.py:519-528`). That's every linear, embedding and MoE layer, so a missing `q_proj` loads silently.
   - #59502's per-model `reload_safe` is an unchecked claim.

## Proposed design

### 1. Weight loaders: per-shard work, and "eliminate" first

**Rule L1.** Every write to a loadable param goes through that param's `weight_loader`. `load_weights` only routes names. A model may wrap a param's loader (see §5) but must not write the param directly.

**Rule L2.** If a transform is **separable per shard**, do it in the loader. Separable means each output byte depends on a single checkpoint tensor. Examples:
- fixed row/column permutations (#60064 `permute_on_load`);
- interleaves and scale repacks into kernel layout (#60096 MegaMoE: parameters created in DeepGEMM layout, `load_weight` writes each shard into a strided view of its final rows);
- elementwise maps (Mamba `A = -exp(A_log)`);
- **block-local quantization**.

Where L2 applies, there's nothing left for post-load code, and reload writes straight into the tensors the kernel reads.

**Rule L3.** State that pairs tensors across loader calls (weight + scale arriving separately) lives on `self`, not in a local dict, because streamed reloads call `load_weights` once per batch. V3.2 keeps its FP8-indexer pairing in a local dict (`deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py:349`), unlike V2 (`deepseek_v2.py:1610`). That loses a pair that spans batches.

**Rule L4.** `WeightsMapper` rules are applied exactly once per name. The VL wrapper already nulls the child mapper because suffix rules are not idempotent (`deepseek_v4/common/vl_model.py:169-175`).

### 2. Module PWAL: always transform, build once

PWAL keeps its current signature and stays the single place where checkpoint format becomes kernel format. It always runs on fresh checkpoint-format inputs (#59502 materializes them), so the requirement is not f(f(x)) = f(x). The requirement is this:

> Running PWAL again on new checkpoint inputs leaves the module's long-lived objects correct and at the same addresses.

Concretely:

```python
def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
    # (a) Transform: always runs, on the checkpoint data just loaded.
    w13, w2, s13, s2 = convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format(layer, ...)
    replace_parameter(layer, "w13_weight", w13)     # on reload, landing copies into the live tensor
    ...
    # (b) Construction: once per process, keyed on the object itself, not on a global flag.
    if self.moe_kernel is None:
        self.moe_quant_config = get_fused_moe_quant_config(layer)
        self.moe_kernel = make_fp8_moe_kernel(...)
    # (c) Derived values: not here. The framework calls kernel.refresh() after landing.
```

**Rules for PWAL authors:**

- **P1. No guards on transforms.** A guard like `if self._transformed is None` (MegaMoE) or `hasattr(self, "_fused_w13_fp8")` (dots3) skips work the new data needs. Guards are allowed **only** on construction, which doesn't depend on weight values.
- **P2. Kernels reference registered params**, so landing's in-place copy reaches them. Every other tensor a kernel holds is a **declared derived tensor**, allocated once and written by `refresh()`.
- **P3. Transforms embedded in construction move to (a).** Example: the ModelOpt NVFP4 build calls `experts.process_weights_after_loading`, which does `w13_weight_scale_2.mul_(input_scale)` (`fused_moe/experts/trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py:154`). Under build-once it wouldn't run on reload. The authors already keep "unfolded" copies for reruns (`:125`).
- **P4. Side effects on shared config must be repeatable.** Compute them from the tensors, not from config an earlier PWAL already changed. Good example: `align_moe_weights_for_fi` pads from `w2.shape` (`flashinfer_utils.py:350-355`), so reload pads again and writes back the same `intermediate_size_per_partition`.
- **P5. Don't delete what reload needs.** Release inputs with a framework helper, `release_param(module, name)`. It frees storage but keeps the Parameter so the snapshot can rematerialize it. Never set a param to `None` or `del` a submodule.
- **P6. Per-instance safety stays.** A backend whose kernel holds derived state without a `refresh()` keeps `reload_safe = False`. Under CUDA graphs the engine refuses to reload it (#59502 behavior), because skipping its rebuild would leave stale values.

Many methods already separate "transform" from "rebuild" for the weight-cache IPC loader's pre-processed mode (`is_weights_pre_processed()`). They're halfway there: `Fp8LinearMethod`, `Fp8MoEMethod`, `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`, `Mxfp4MoEMethod`, the KV-cache method, and the unquantized methods.

### 3. Kernel refresh: framework-driven

Kernel objects keep the `refresh()` from #59502: `FusedMoEKernel.refresh()` composes down through quant config → prepare/finalize → experts, and `register_derived` / `add_refresh` allocate the tensors once. Changes from #59502:

- **The framework always calls kernel refreshes.** Models never have to call `super()`.
- **It runs on cold start too,** right after PWAL. Cold start and reload then run the same code, and cold-start tests cover it.
- **Attention.** The attention impl `refresh(layer)` (e.g. FlashInfer bmm scales) runs in the attention phase. MLA absorption stays in attention PWAL; it's per layer and expensive, see §8.

### 4. `SupportsReload`

```python
@runtime_checkable
class SupportsReload(Protocol):
    supports_reload: ClassVar[Literal[True]] = True

    def refresh_model(self) -> None:
        """Recompute weight-derived values that span modules, from live tensors.
        Called by the framework after every load (cold start and reload), after all
        kernel and attention refreshes. Optional; default no-op."""

    def post_load_setup(self) -> None:
        """Non-weight setup: compile, device placement, geometry. Cold start only."""
```

**Contract for `refresh_model` (and any `refresh`):**

- **R1. Reads only live, landed tensors.** Reading another module's tensors is fine; this is the place for cross-module work.
- **R2. Writes only preallocated buffers,** using `copy_`, `out=` or `fill_`. The first call (cold start, before graph capture) may allocate; later calls must not. The framework checks pointers after every refresh.
- **R3. Idempotent and safe under partial updates.** It never rewrites a live weight in place, because on a module that wasn't updated that would apply the transform twice.
- **R4. Collectives are allowed** only if every rank calls them. The framework calls `refresh_model` on all ranks at finish.

**Order the framework runs things in, after every load and every kernel-format write:**

```
modules complete (loader → PWAL → land)  →  attention PWAL (+ impl refresh)  →  kernel refresh
  →  model.refresh_model()  →  [cold start only] post_load_setup()  →  verify invariants (§6.6)
```

**Write paths that must call it:**
- layerwise and modulewise finish;
- `reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)`;
- `sparse_nccl` patches;
- `sharded_rdt` finish;
- draft-model sessions, which call the drafter's own `refresh_model`.

**The model-level `process_weights_after_loading()` is not part of the contract.** A model implementing `SupportsReload` must not define one: the verifier reports UNSAFE, and new models fail CI. Models without `SupportsReload` keep today's behavior, warn on every update (the #59502 `UNSAFE WEIGHT UPDATE`), and are refused under strict mode.

**Name.** `refresh_model` is a placeholder. #54477 §6 proposed `refresh_derived_state()` on `nn.Module`. Using that name would converge the two RFCs; it's a question for reviewers below.

### 5. Customizing a generic layer: wrap it, don't hook it

Sometimes a model needs a framework layer to process its weights differently. Example: ROCm DSv4 needs `gate_up_proj`'s FP8 weight preshuffled for an AITER B-preshuffle GEMM. None of the slots above fits this:

- it runs on PWAL **output**, so it can't go in the loader;
- `Fp8LinearMethod` is framework code;
- in `refresh_model` it would be an in-place rewrite of a live weight, violating R3. A separate buffer instead would double the weight's memory.

Sanctioned pattern: **wrap the layer's quant method** for post-PWAL work, or **wrap the param's `weight_loader`** for per-shard work, at construction:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/wrap.py (new)
def wrap_quant_method(layer, *, after_pwal: Callable[[nn.Module], None]) -> None:
    """Run `after_pwal(layer)` right after the layer's own PWAL, on every load.
    Its outputs land like any PWAL result. Replaces instance monkeypatching."""

# ROCm DeepseekV4MLP.__init__
wrap_quant_method(self.gate_up_proj,
                  after_pwal=lambda l: replace_parameter(l, "weight", shuffle_weight(l.weight.data, (16, 16))))
```

The framework treats the wrapped method like any PWAL: it runs on fresh data every load, its output lands, and there's no double-shuffle or extra memory. This replaces #59502's `attach_processing_plan`, model-hook rewrites, and monkeypatching. Existing cases to migrate:
- ROCm preshuffle (`deepseek_v4/amd/model.py:137`, `amd/rocm.py:896`);
- DSv4 AMD heterogeneous shared expert (`amd/model.py:361`; already a subclass);
- DSv4 CPU `wo_a` packing (`cpu/cpu_sparse.py:308`; currently a monkeypatch);
- GLM-5.2 quant-method swap (`deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py:437`).

### 6. `verify_reload`: a verifier, not just a declaration

`SupportsReload` should be something the framework can check. `verify_reload(model, vllm_config, checkpoint_meta=None) -> ReloadReport` runs six checks and returns SAFE / UNSAFE / UNVERIFIED per item, with the module path and reason.

**6.1 Declarations** (once, after cold load)
- The model and every drafter implement `SupportsReload`. A drafter with no update policy is reported (§7).
- Every quant-method instance, MoE kernel and attention impl is `reload_safe`. This is checked per instance, because backends are chosen at runtime.
- Every module that defines its own PWAL with no `quant_method` is covered.
- No root `process_weights_after_loading`, and no `finalizes_weights_during_load = True`.
- No instance monkeypatches: `"process_weights_after_loading" in vars(quant_method)` is UNSAFE.

**6.2 Tensor ownership** (once, **after CUDA graph capture**, so lazy caches exist)
- Collect every device tensor reachable from the model: module `__dict__`s (not just `_parameters` / `_buffers`) and kernel objects (`moe_kernel`, `moe_quant_config`, `fp8_linear`, …), recursively.
- Each tensor's storage must be a registered param or buffer, a declared derived tensor, or declared constant (rope caches, expert maps). Anything else is UNSAFE.
- This one check catches:
  - DSpark `_context_kv_norm_weights`;
  - DSv4 `hc_attn_fn_broadcast` until it's registered;
  - ROCm `_gateup_scale`;
  - GLM-5-Next `_merged_conv_weight`;
  - Triton MXFP4 weights as plain attributes;
  - quant-config `a1_gscale`;
  - CT NVFP4 MoE unregistered input scales (`compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_nvfp4.py:245`).
- Reuse #60009's `persistent_tensors()` / `register_held_tensors` machinery and its `can_initialize` CI oracle.
- **Python floats derived from weights** can't be traced. Backends that read host scales (FlashInfer native decode, DCP decode, attention + output-quant fusion) declare it. Under FULL graphs with checkpoint-loaded KV scales, that's UNSAFE.

**6.3 Snapshot vs. live structure** (once)
- A param in the init snapshot that's now missing or `None` is UNSAFE, unless the framework recreates it (KV-scale params) or it was released through `release_param`. Examples: MegaMoE `w13_weight = None`, Triton MXFP4 `del`.
- A submodule in the snapshot that's missing from `model.modules()` is UNSAFE. Example: dots3 `del self.experts`.
- Record the `id()` of every kernel object, for 6.6.

**6.4 Load coverage** (dry run over checkpoint metadata)
- Input: names, dtypes and shapes only. They come from the safetensors index at cold start, or from the trainer's metadata at `init_weight_transfer_engine` (NCCL update info already carries them).
- Run `model.load_weights` on meta stand-ins under the reload wrapper (#59502 `trace_loads`). Report:
  - **Module never reaches its expected count:** a direct write (L1 violation) or a missing name. This catches the gpt-oss and DSv4 sinks, Quark experts and fused BF16 experts.
  - **Names the mappers drop:** listed for review. Today these disappear silently, e.g. `mtp.*` in the target model, `.g_idx` for every quantized model, KV-scale names with no target.
  - **One name feeding several params:** allowed only if declared. Example: K3 DSpark `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` → `context_kv_proj`.
  - **Loader raises on meta** (it branches on a param's value): UNVERIFIED, not UNSAFE, because modulewise runs loaders on real targets.

**6.5 Configuration** (once)
- **EPLB enabled:** UNSAFE until placement-aware loading lands (deferred, see below), unless the #59063 gate is on and no rebalance has happened.
- **CPU / UVA offload:** reload doesn't support it.
- **IPC weight cache in zero-copy mode:** incompatible with in-place writes and sleep mode.
- **Re-tied embeddings:** warn that `lm_head` updates will be ignored. Fix: skip `maybe_retie_word_embeddings` when weight transfer is configured.
- **LoRA:** warn that adapters are evicted on every update.
- **Transport engine capabilities:** `sharded_rdt` refuses EPLB; only NCCL and IPC support draft updates.
- **Partial updates allowed** when PWAL has collectives (online-quant amax all-reduce, MLA DCP all-gather) or the Engram loader barrier: require all ranks to agree on the module set at `start`.

**6.6 After every update** (runtime, cheap)
- Live tensors unchanged (#59502), **plus** kernel-object ids unchanged.
- Every required module completed; none left on meta or holding scratch.
- Refresh didn't allocate (ownership snapshot before and after).
- Any failure sets the dirty flag (#59502).

**API and policy**

```python
report = llm.check_reload_support()            # cached result of 6.1-6.3, 6.5
report = verify_reload(model, cfg, checkpoint_meta=names_and_shapes)   # adds 6.4
# ReloadReport(status=SAFE|UNSAFE|UNVERIFIED, items=[(check, module_path, reason, severity), ...])
```

- **When it runs:**
  - 6.1–6.3 and 6.5 after cold load and graph capture;
  - 6.4 at `init_weight_transfer_engine`, and in CI against the real checkpoint index;
  - 6.6 on every update.
- **Under CUDA graphs:** UNSAFE refuses `start_weight_update` before any live write.
- **Eager mode:** warn.
- **UNVERIFIED:** warn and point to the refit test.
- **Escape hatch:** `VLLM_RELOAD_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1`.

**What the verifier can't catch, and the CI policy for it.** It proves structure, not values. These all pass every check:
- a refresh with the wrong formula;
- a mapper rule pointing to the wrong param;
- a transform reading a config value an earlier PWAL changed.

The **refit-equals-fresh** harness (#59502 PR 0b) is the real check. **CI policy:** every model or backend that declares itself reload-safe has at least one refit case, and `verify_reload` must pass on it.

### 7. Drafters

- `reload_weights` reloads only the target.
- Weight transfer has a separate draft session, supported only by NCCL and IPC.
- Shared `embed_tokens` / `lm_head` modules follow the target automatically.
- Drafter-only weights stay stale: EAGLE layers, `fc`, `d2t`, MTP blocks, Medusa heads.
- DSv4's target mapper maps `mtp.` to `None`, so a trainer sending the full checkpoint in one target session has its MTP weights **silently dropped**.

Drafters implement `SupportsReload` like any model; DSpark and DFlash have derived stacks. The update policy is an open question for reviewers:
- **(a) Routed:** one session routes names to the target or the drafter, and finish refreshes both.
- **(b) Frozen:** drafters are declared frozen during RL, and the verifier warns when a target session drops `mtp.*` names.

### 8. Model conversions

| Hook today (all under `vllm/models/`) | New home |
|---|---|
| VL wrapper delegation (DSv4, V4.1, K3, Dots3), `_weights_finalized` | Deleted. The framework already visits every module. |
| MegaMoE `finalize_weights` (DSv4 / V4.1 / K3 NVIDIA, MTP, DSpark; AMD AITER variant) | Loader (#60096) on NVIDIA. AITER MegaMoE: same pattern, or module PWAL with `release_param`. |
| Shared-expert fusion into MegaMoE | Loader (#60096: decided at construction, shared tensors routed to kernel params) |
| mHC broadcast (DSv4, V4.1) | `refresh_model`, buffer allocated in `__init__` |
| K3 DSpark `_build_fused_context_kv_metadata` | Geometry → `__init__` / `post_load_setup`. Norm and KV-scale stacks → `refresh_model` with `out=`. One implementation instead of two. |
| DFlash / DSpark `_build_fused_kv_buffers` (inside `load_weights`) | `refresh_model` |
| dots3 vision FP8 fusion (`del self.experts`) | **Loader**: register fused FP8 params in kernel layout; each `experts.i.fc{1,3,2}.weight` is block-quantized into its slice. Block FP8 is local to 128×128 blocks and each weight is padded independently, so this is per tensor. Removes the resident-BF16 workaround. |
| dots3 `compile_block_modules` | `post_load_setup` |
| ROCm DSv4 preshuffle (gate_up, wqa_wkv, wo_b) | `wrap_quant_method(after_pwal=…)` |
| ROCm compressor GEMM fusion (`set_` aliasing) | `post_load_setup`. In-place landing keeps the alias. Needs direct loading to treat the shared storage as non-exclusive. |
| DSv4 AMD heterogeneous shared expert | Quant-method wrapper (already a subclass); audit for P1–P5 |
| DSv4 CPU `wo_a` monkeypatch | `wrap_quant_method` |
| CPU no-op hooks | Deleted |
| MiniCPM resampler device move (in `load_weights`) | `post_load_setup` |

With #60096 merged and dots3 moved into the loader, **no in-tree model needs a multi-module completion unit.** #59502's module-level PWAL path and `reload_outputs` have no in-tree users left (see the #59502 change summary).

**MLA.** Absorption stays in attention PWAL (per layer, landed `kv_b_proj`). Two fixes ride along:
- build-once guard on the AITER Triton BMM precompile (M = 1..1024, ~50 s);
- `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` checks "DeepGEMM supported" instead of "DeepGEMM selected" (`fp8.py:249-252` vs `quant_utils.py:539`). That sends Hopper/Blackwell FP8 `kv_b_proj` through the O(N³) identity-matmul path even under CUTLASS.

## Bugs found on main while auditing (separate fixes)

| Finding | Location | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| "All weights loaded" check exempts every module with a `quant_method`, so a missing linear isn't caught | `model_loader/default_loader.py:511-534` | verified |
| Tensorizer never runs PWAL (fixed by #57733) | `model_loader/tensorizer_loader.py:115-139` | verified |
| Direct writes are silent no-ops on reload (gpt-oss / DSv4 sinks, Quark, fused BF16 experts, mimo FP8 qkv, …) | §Problems 2 | verified primitive + code path |
| MegaMoE reload keeps old experts | `deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py:418` | confirmed by #60096 GSM8K 0.948 → 0.008 |
| CT MoE static `input_scale` loader branches on a param value: `bool(meta != 1)` raises in the layerwise dry run. Disappears under modulewise. | `fused_moe/routed_experts.py:823` | inferred; primitive verified |
| Reload after an EPLB rebalance writes experts into startup slots | `routed_experts.py:~1181`; DSv4 MegaMoE `p % num_logical` (`nvidia/model.py:308-315`) | inferred |
| ROCm DSv4 preshuffle not redone on reload | `deepseek_v4/amd/model.py:137`, `amd/rocm.py:896` | read |
| MoE quant config may reference temporary tensors after layerwise reload | `fp8.py:695`, `reload/layerwise.py:417` | inferred |
| CUTLASS FP8 padding calls `set_weight_attrs` on an existing `weight_loader` (should assert), and the second call targets the wrong name | `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py:222-242` | read |
| KV-cache `q_scale := k_scale` fallback overwritten with 1.0 | `quantization/kv_cache.py:145-197` | read |
| gpt-oss `w2_bias` loader zeros the caller's tensor on TP ranks ≠ 0 | `gpt_oss.py:717, 1071, 1254` | read |
| V3.2 FP8 indexer pairing in a local dict (lost across streamed batches) | `deepseek_v32/nvidia/model.py:349` | read |
| Medusa `token_map.to()` result discarded | `medusa.py:196` | read |
| Kernel-format reload warning says `True` where it means `False` | `v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5520` | read |
| `sharded_rdt` quant thread skips `update_param_tp_status()` | `distributed/weight_transfer/sharded_rdt_engine.py:1367` | read |
| Failed `update_weights` clears the session flag but leaves modules on meta, with nothing preventing serving | `v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:1536-1540` | verified (fixed by #59502 PR 1c) |
| "Limitations(4)" referenced but not defined | `reload/layerwise.py:170, 272` | read |
| Contributor docs stale: `linear_method`, hand-written `load_weights`, no `vllm/models/` layout | `docs/contributing/model/` | read |

## PR plan

Six PRs, grouped by what they change. Each PR is large but organized as logical commits that can be reviewed one at a time, and every commit passes the reload unit suite.

**Verifier burn-down.** SR-1 lands the verifier in report-only mode and checks in a baseline `ReloadReport` for a fixed model list (tiny real-format checkpoints from #59502 PR 0b). Every later PR states which UNSAFE items it removes and which refit cases it flips from `xfail(strict=True)` to passing. SR-6 turns the report into enforcement once the baseline is clean for in-tree models.

| PR | Title | Lands on | Depends on | Hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SR-1** | Reload correctness on main: verifier (report only), loader fixes, bug fixes | main | — | SM100 |
| **SR-2** | `SupportsReload` framework (replaces #59502 PR 2) | #59502 stack | #59502 PR 1d | SM100 |
| **SR-3** | Kernel backends and tensor ownership (replaces #59502 PR 2a) | after SR-2 | SR-2, #60009 | SM100 |
| **SR-4** | Model conversions and drafters (replaces #59502 PR 2m) | after SR-2 | SR-2, #60096 | SM100 |
| **SR-5** | ROCm | after SR-2 | SR-2 | **AMD** |
| **SR-6** | Enforcement and docs | last | SR-3, SR-4, SR-5 | — |

### SR-1: Reload correctness on main

Independent of #59502. It fixes real reload bugs under today's layerwise reload, and adds the verifier that measures everything after it.

Commits:
1. **Verifier framework.** `verify_reload`, `ReloadReport`, `llm.check_reload_support()`. Adds check 6.3 (snapshot vs live structure), 6.5 (configuration) and 6.6 (post-update invariants under layerwise: nothing left on meta, live tensors unchanged). Report only. Baseline report checked in.
2. **Load coverage at cold start.** An opt-in, CI-only observation of a real cold load. It reports params that a consumed name never reached through `weight_loader`, and names the mappers drop. This is the init-time form of check 6.4.
3. **Direct writes through `weight_loader` (rule L1):**
   - gpt-oss sinks, Quark experts and scales, fused BF16 experts;
   - DSv4 / V4.1 / HY-v4 `attn_sink`;
   - mimo-v2 FP8 qkv;
   - the `default_weight_loader(param, …)` sites.
   
   Reload e2e cases go from `xfail` to passing.
4. **Weight tying.** Skip `maybe_retie_word_embeddings` when weight transfer is configured; the verifier warns on re-tied embeddings.
5. **Bug fixes**, each with a regression test. Code-read findings get a failing test first.
   - `track_weights_loading` exempts only online-quant and KV-scale params. This lands as a warning first, because it surfaces real missing weights.
   - CUTLASS FP8 padding `set_weight_attrs`.
   - KV-cache `q_scale` fallback.
   - gpt-oss `w2_bias` in-place `zero_()`.
   - V3.2 FP8 indexer pairing state moved onto `self`.
   - Medusa `token_map.to()`.
   - `sharded_rdt` `update_param_tp_status()`.
   - MLA dequantization keyed on the *selected* DeepGEMM kernel.
   - The kernel-format warning text and the "Limitations(4)" reference.
6. **Contributor docs refresh:** `quant_config`, `WeightsMapper` + `AutoWeightsLoader`, and the `vllm/models/<name>/<platform>/` layout.

### SR-2: `SupportsReload` framework

Replaces #59502 PR 2's framework. It also carries the small additions to #59502 PR 1b and 1c, folded into those PRs if they haven't merged yet.

Commits:
1. **Protocol and order.** `SupportsReload` (`refresh_model`, `post_load_setup`) and the framework refresh order (§4). Refresh runs on cold start too, and is called from every write path: finish, kernel-format, `sparse_nccl`, `sharded_rdt`, draft sessions.
2. **Build once.** Remove `reload_mode()` / `is_reloading()`. Kernel construction is guarded by object presence. `Fp8MoEMethod` is the reference (rules P1–P5). Strict landing and `refresh_derived_state` stay.
3. **`wrap_quant_method`** (§5). Migrate the DSv4 CPU `wo_a` monkeypatch and the GLM-5.2 quant-method swap. Remove `attach_processing_plan` (#59502 PR 2c is dropped; #60064 already covers DSv4.1 mega attention).
4. **Verifier additions:**
   - check 6.1, declarations, report only;
   - check 6.4 made metadata-driven: `trace_loads` over the trainer's names and shapes at `init_weight_transfer_engine`, and over the checkpoint index in CI;
   - integrity: kernel-object ids added to the live-tensor check, and start-time agreement on the module set for partial updates.

### SR-3: Kernel backends and tensor ownership

Replaces #59502 PR 2a.

Commits:
1. **Backend declarations** with the P2–P5 audit: MXFP4, CT/Quark FP8, online FP8 / INT8 / MXFP8. One refit case per backend.
2. **NVFP4** (ModelOpt, CT), plus P3: move `w13_weight_scale_2.mul_(input_scale)` and any other transform out of `experts/*` construction.
3. **Ownership.**
   - `register_derived` wherever kernels hold weight-derived tensors.
   - Adopt #60009 `persistent_tensors()` / `register_held_tensors`.
   - Verifier check 6.2, run after graph capture.
   - Host-scale backends declare themselves.
4. **MLA:** build-once guard on the AITER Triton BMM precompile.

### SR-4: Model conversions and drafters

Replaces #59502 PR 2m. #59502 PR 2b is mostly dropped: MegaMoE is handled by #60096 and dots3 moves to its loader. Module-level PWAL stays as an escape hatch with no in-tree users. Each model family declares `SupportsReload` with a refit case and a cold-start bitwise A/B.

Commits:
1. **DSv4 + V4.1 NVIDIA** (main, MTP, DSpark):
   - mHC → `refresh_model`, with the buffer allocated in `__init__`;
   - delete the VL-wrapper delegation and `_weights_finalized`;
   - drop `finalizes_weights_during_load`.
2. **Kimi K3** (main, DSpark MLA, KDA):
   - DSpark stacks → `refresh_model` (one implementation instead of two);
   - geometry → `__init__` / `post_load_setup`.
3. **dots3:**
   - vision FP8 fusion moved into the loader (fused FP8 params in kernel layout, per-expert block quantization into slices, scale-write counting);
   - `compile_block_modules` → `post_load_setup`;
   - delete `del self.experts`.
4. **Misc:**
   - DFlash `_build_fused_kv_buffers` → `refresh_model`;
   - GLM-5-Next lazy `_merged_conv_weight` → registered and refreshed;
   - MiniCPM resampler device move → `post_load_setup`.
5. **Drafters:** `SupportsReload` on EAGLE / EAGLE3 / MTP / DSpark / DFlash / Medusa, plus the chosen policy: routed updates, or declared-frozen drafters with a warning on dropped `mtp.*`. **Blocked on Q5.**

### SR-5: ROCm

Commits:
1. **Preshuffle.** ROCm DSv4 / V4.1 preshuffle (gate_up, wqa_wkv, wo_b) moved from the model hook to `wrap_quant_method`.
2. **AITER MegaMoE finalize:** loader, or module PWAL with `release_param`.
3. **Compressor GEMM fusion** → `post_load_setup`. Direct loading must treat the aliased storage as non-exclusive.
4. **Heterogeneous shared expert** audited for P1–P5. Declare `SupportsReload`, with AMD refit cases.

### SR-6: Enforcement and docs

Commits:
1. **Enforcement.**
   - Refuse UNSAFE under CUDA graphs before any live write (`VLLM_RELOAD_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1` escape hatch).
   - CI requires a refit case and a passing verifier for every reload-safe declaration.
   - Models without `SupportsReload` go from warn to refuse.
2. **Docs:** "writing a reloadable model" (rules L1–L4, P1–P6, R1–R4, `wrap_quant_method`, verifier usage).

### Order and dependencies

```
SR-1 (main, now) ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
#59502 0a,0b,1,1b,1c,1d ─► SR-2 ─┬─► SR-3 (+#60009) ─┐        │
                                 ├─► SR-4 (+#60096) ─┼─► SR-6 ◄┘
                                 └─► SR-5 (AMD) ─────┘
#59502 3, 4 (direct loading, per-expert completion) follow SR-2, unchanged
```

SR-1 starts now. SR-3, SR-4 and SR-5 can be reviewed in parallel once SR-2 lands.

**Not in this plan (deferred, see below):**
- host-float scales under FULL graphs;
- true rollback;
- EPLB placement-aware loading (with #59063);
- hardware-gated backends;
- out-of-tree code;
- the Triton MXFP4 refill and LoRA-derived-state unknowns;
- the prefix-cache policy.

## Deferred (known, no fix in this RFC)

- **Host-float scales under FULL CUDA graphs:** FlashInfer native decode, DCP decode, attention + output-quant fusion. Needs device-scale entry points in FlashInfer, or a graph-recapture step after updates that change KV scales. Until then the update fails, as in #59502.
- **True rollback.** Direct loading overwrites old bytes early; the dirty flag is the contract.
- **EPLB placement-aware loading.** A mapping helper that reads the live physical→logical map (custom expert loaders such as MegaMoE must use it), the #59063 gate, and a regression test that forces a rebalance first. Until then the verifier reports EPLB as UNSAFE.
- **Hardware-gated backends:** AITER MoE, XQA device scales, XPU MegaMoE, and others. They stay refused under graphs until each has a refit case.
- **Out-of-tree models and quant methods,** including the BnB and GGUF plugins. Without `SupportsReload` or a backend declaration they're refused or warned.
- **Unknowns to check:**
  - whether Triton MXFP4's `triton_kernels` wrapper tensors can be refilled in place;
  - whether any LoRA backend caches state derived from base weights. That determines whether adapter eviction on every update can be relaxed.
- **Prefix cache under `pause_generation(mode="keep", clear_cache=False)`:** resumed requests keep KV from the old weights. A policy decision (clear on `weight_version` change, or document it).

## Alternatives considered

1. **Global reload flag inside PWAL** (#59502 `reload_mode()`). Works and is validated, but every PWAL author has to know about the flag, and correctness depends on branching right. The object-presence guard reaches the same build-once behavior locally and needs no global state.
2. **Call the model hook at finish with a `reloading` argument.** It works for derived-from-live work. It can't work for transforms that need checkpoint-format inputs (MegaMoE, the old DSv4.1 permute), because modulewise frees those before finish; keeping them alive costs memory unless they're hosted. It also leaves non-idempotent work (preshuffle) exposed to partial updates, and makes every author handle partial updates (`was_updated`). #60096 and #60064 removed the transform cases, which leaves exactly the derived-from-live work, now `refresh_model`.
3. **A full per-module protocol** (transform / refresh / setup on every module, phases, subtree completion units, cold-start generic dispatch of module PWAL). More general, but larger. Once the transforms move into loaders, no in-tree model needs subtree units, and generic cold-start dispatch changes cold-start ordering for every model.
4. **#54477's direct reload** (restore to checkpoint layout, then `refresh_derived_state`). Its shape for derived state (zero arguments, declared per module, phased) is what §3–§4 adopt. It differs in pulling transforms out of PWAL and restoring live params. This RFC keeps PWAL as the single transform path and doesn't mutate live params.

## Questions for reviewers

1. **Quant / MoE owners:** is "always transform, build once by object presence" plus framework-driven `refresh()` acceptable in place of `reload_mode()`? Which `experts/*` PWALs transform tensors during construction (P3)?
2. **#54477 authors:** should `refresh_model` be named `refresh_derived_state` to converge, and should kernel refresh share that protocol?
3. **#60009 authors:** can the ownership check (6.2) reuse `persistent_tensors()` / `register_held_tensors` and the `can_initialize` CI oracle directly?
4. **Model owners (DSv4, K3, dots3):** is the dots3 loader-side fusion acceptable? Any model-specific post-load work missing from §8?
5. **Drafters:** routed updates (a) or declared-frozen drafters (b)?
6. **Policy:** refuse UNSAFE under CUDA graphs by default with `VLLM_RELOAD_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1` as the escape hatch, and when should models without `SupportsReload` move from warn to refuse?
7. **ROCm owners:** does `wrap_quant_method` cover the DSv4 AITER preshuffle and the heterogeneous shared expert, and who can run refit cases on AMD?

## Related

| Ref | Relation |
|---|---|
| #59502 | Modulewise reload; this RFC changes PR 2, 2b, 2c and the detection model (see the comment there) |
| #54477 | Selective weight reload; source of the `refresh_derived_state` shape |

| #60096 | MegaMoE loads directly into DeepGEMM layout; removes the main transform-then-drop case |

title: [BugFix] Clamp Mooncake store token_len to hash coverage under MTP/async scheduling
body:
## Purpose
- Under speculative decoding (MTP) combined with async scheduling, the scheduler can advance its token count optimistically before `block_hashes` are extended to match, tripping an assertion in `ChunkedTokenDatabase.process_tokens` and crashing the engine. 

- Clamp `token_len` to the range actually covered by `block_hashes` and save only that prefix instead of asserting; the remaining tail is picked up on a later step once the hashes catch up. Also log a warning when the clamp engages so the race stays observable.

## Note on scope
This clamp stops the crash but does not fully close a smaller side effect: `KVCacheStoreSendingThread._record_saved` records the pre-clamp (optimistic) token count rather than what was actually saved, so the worker's own resume offset can advance past the clamped range and the skipped tokens for that block are never retried, leaving a small gap in what's persisted to the external Mooncake store for that request (generation correctness is unaffected). 
A more complete fix would have `_record_saved` (and the scheduler's `RequestTracker` bookkeeping) advance only by the actually-covered amount so the gap is retried instead of permanently dropped. That's left out of this PR since it touches block-lifecycle bookkeeping (`request_finished`/`delay_free_blocks`) and carries more risk than warranted for a crash hotfix; happy to follow up separately if the cache-hit-rate impact turns out to matter in practice.

## Test plan

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51805


## Test Plan

title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3
body:
## Summary

PR adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3 on ROCm. Part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion (#51303): each model needs varlen-capable sparse kernels before adaptive verification can redistribute draft tokens across requests
It was validated end to end with amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 and nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark on MI325.

Scope: only the ROCm Triton indexer and sparse-decode paths gain ragged decode support. The CUDA and AITER MiniMax M3 backends still report device/CPU query-length mismatch as unsupported, so adaptive verification stays disabled there. With adaptive verification off, the uniform decode path is unchanged.

## Changes

- MiniMax M3 indexer and sparse attention (ROCm Triton): device-side ragged decode metadata; both AMD index-score launch policies, the fused top-k selector, and sparse decode map packed query tokens to requests from device `query_start_loc`.
- `kernel_paged_attention_2d`: return for `query_len != 1` (previously `> 1`). FULL cudagraph replay can pad the request dimension with zero-length rows, which fell into the decode path and read one row past the logical query buffer.
- Rejection sampler: adaptive verification allows the regular chunked path for batches with no draft tokens, whose logits layout isnever compacted.
- Warmup: synthetic draft rows are bounded by the same rejection-sampler budget used at runtime, so large `max_num_seqs` configs nolonger fail at startup.
- Adaptive verification overhead: confidence D2H copies use a non-blocking ring, and only TP rank 0 computes the draft budget, thenbroadcasts it.
- DSpark config: prefer speculators-format top-level confidence-head fields and fall back to NVIDIA's legacy `dflash_config` fields.


Token-to-request mapping uses upstream's `compute_token_to_req_indices`, a device-side binary search over `query_start_loc`. It doesn't depend on `max_query_len` and handles zero-length rows and the padding tail.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs (adaptive verification, MiniMax M3 DSpark, token-to-request mapping, paged-decode zero-length). The closest is #52893, which skips AITER sparse PA under spec decode; this PR adds ragged decode to the Triton path instead.

## Testing

On MI325:
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`: 138 passed, 1 skipped.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: all passed.
- `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention` (`chunked_prefill_paged_decode`, source build of this branch): 128 passed, 256 skipped.

- Stress test of the ragged index top-k and sparse decode kernels at serving-sized batches: 60 random batches of 380–512 requests (1–8 query tokens each, up to 4K context, zero-length padding rows), reference-checked every 10th batch: all passed.

## End-to-end results 

MI325, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark` drafter with its default confidence head, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, FULL cudagraphs, default memory settings, `--max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 512`. Fixed vs adaptive verification on the same build.

GSM8K, full test set (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 64):

| Checkpoint | TP | Fixed | Adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` | 2 | 0.8196 | 0.8226 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` | 4 | 0.8779 | 0.8711 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` (BF16) | 8 | 0.8704 | 0.8688 |

Repeated MXFP8 runs vary by about ±0.01 for both modes (fixed 0.860–0.878 over 6 runs, adaptive 0.867–0.879 over 9 runs). One earlyadaptive MXFP8 run scored 0.801; it did not reproduce in 9 later runs and is still being investigated.

Sonnet 550 in / 150 out / 200 shared prefix, ignore EOS, output tok/s (adaptive gain vs fixed):

| Concurrency | MXFP4, TP=2 | MXFP8, TP=4 | BF16, TP=8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 649.96 → 674.59 (+3.8%) | 2241.79 → 2166.80 (−3.3%) | 3451.90 → 3327.16 (−3.6%) |
| 256 | 882.77 → 930.58 (+5.4%) | 2560.18 → 2605.40 (+1.8%) | 4005.66 → 4063.85 (+1.5%) |
| 320 | 965.59 → 1020.85 (+5.7%) | 2643.30 → 2733.47 (+3.4%) | 4099.15 → 4268.66 (+4.1%) |
| 380 | 1013.94 → 1071.63 (+5.7%) | 2686.83 → 2778.46 (+3.4%) | 4190.48 → crash (see below) |
| 420 | 1040.76 → 1102.05 (+5.9%) | 2713.55 → 2692.00 (−0.8%) | 4263.58 → crash |
| 500 | 1089.06 → 1146.61 (+5.3%) | fixed OOM → 1929.71 | 4228.05 → crash |

The gain shrinks as verification gets cheaper: TP=4 and TP=8 leave little verify cost for adaptive budgeting to save. MXFP8 fixed verification at concurrency 500 runs out of memory allocating the full verification logits (1.6 GB) at the default `--gpu-memory-utilization`; adaptive verification bounds that allocation and completes all requests.

### Known issue: BF16, TP=8, adaptive, concurrency ≥ 380

The adaptive BF16 server aborts with `HW Exception by GPU node-N ... reason: GPU Hang` under sustained load at concurrency 380–420 (reproduced twice; fixed verification is stable at the same load, MXFP4 TP=2 and MXFP8 TP=4 adaptive are stable through concurrency 500). The ragged MiniMax kernels pass the stress test above. Most likely root cause fix in #56831 - this is well-known issue at this point. Need to run TP=8 test with this PR applied).

## Earlier results (before rebase)

MXFP4 target with the `olka-fi/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-DSpark` drafter, TP=2, same Sonnet workload, 3–5 minute steady-state runs; 9,040 requests, none failed.

| Concurrency | Fixed tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | Fixed median TPOT | Adaptive median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 299.82 | 330.13 | +10.1% | 381.78 ms | 342.55 ms |
| 256 | 413.86 | 479.84 | +15.9% | 500.45 ms | 406.09 ms |
| 320 | 471.08 | 573.31 | +21.7% | 570.16 ms | 446.81 ms |
| 380 | 488.89 | 603.86 | +23.5% | 615.22 ms | 478.64 ms |
| 420 | 528.18 | 658.30 | +24.6% | 645.89 ms | 489.64 ms |
| 500 | 568.84 | 731.51 | +28.6% | 667.91 ms | 521.15 ms |

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Enable DSpark adaptive verification
body: ## Purpose Enable DSpark confidence-scheduled adaptive verification for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm. Developed with contributions from [@larryli2-amd](https://github.com/larryli2-amd), who added explicit missing-confidence-head error handling and provided the MI350X performance validation. This change: - adds AMD confidence-head construction, inference, checkpoint remapping, and safe fallback when a checkpoint has no confidence head - enables variable-length FULL graph support in the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm sparse MLA and sparse SWA metadata builders when adaptive verification is enabled, while retaining their existing support classification otherwise - extends the shared DeepSeek indexer flattening capability to the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 path, deriving adaptive request ownership from device query boundaries - adds focused confidence-loading and graph-replay regression coverage Adaptive verification can redistribute a fixed draft-token budget between requests on device, so CPU request boundaries can differ from final device boundaries. The flattened path builds request ownership, context lengths, and block-table rows from device decode lengths. It reuses the shared flattening selection introduced by [#52795](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52795) and keeps the ROCm capability scoped to the DeepSeek-V4 builder. NVIDIA and unrelated ROCm indexers are unchanged. The ROCm sparse MLA/SWA declarations are similarly scoped. Their ragged metadata is device-boundary-derived and copied into persistent buffers before FULL graph replay. AI assistance was used in preparing this PR. ## Test plan - changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13; - focused AMD confidence-head, ROCm adaptive metadata, native `next_n`, and adaptive-verification tests; - complete GSM8K 5-shot evaluation for no speculation, fixed K=7, and adaptive K<=7; - SPEED-Bench throughput comparison on 8x MI350X at TP=8 and client concurrency 4/8/16/32/64/128/256. - Rocm vllm nightly ShareGPT throughput comparison on 8x MI355X at TP=8 and client concurrency 4/8/16/32/64/128/256. ## Test results ### Source and focused tests - rebased PR head `ea586873d5210d9e1624c42333be1b02c276c832` onto upstream `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`; - changed-file pre-commit passed, including Ruff and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13; - the two PR-specific test files passed (`10 passed`) and the shared adaptive-verification suite passed (`13 passed`). ### Performance validation — 8x MI350X Performance validation contributed by [@larryli2-amd](https://github.com/larryli2-amd) used 8x AMD Instinct MI350X at TP=8 with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`. This PR changes only vLLM; it does not modify or vendor AITER source code. The benchmark environment used a locally rebuilt, pinned AITER wheel installed into the derived image with `--no-deps`, leaving the base PyTorch and Triton installations unchanged: - base image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:72e90adf360ccffb231a098a15eadfb808719c029c6cd43f6386095064552b7e`; - AITER version: `0.1.21.post2.dev2+g804648bcb`; - AITER source: `804648bcbf87646ddef4b7add10da9c3b322567c`; - AITER wheel SHA256: `30360d15819a9c8e3ec8e4ae665683abf4c5358d5be1f49a9aa2f7962c0032db`; - PyTorch: `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`. The pinned wheel was used because the stock AITER post1 environment had a known GPU-fault issue in this setup. The server used Model Runner V2, breakable CUDA graphs, async scheduling, prefix caching, FP8 KV cache, `max_num_seqs=256`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` capture through 2048. Adaptive DSpark used K<=7 and an 8192-token profiling context. The benchmark used a frozen 880-request SPEED-Bench Throughput-1K request set at temperature 1, top-p 1, and maximum output length 2048. Concurrency ran in descending order from 256 to 4. Each point used an independent cold server boot, two 64-request warmups, matching client/server generated-token counts, zero preemptions, and no GPU faults. Compared with fixed-length verification, confidence-scheduled DSpark delivered comparable performance at low concurrency and higher throughput at high concurrency. The complete serving command and environment details are preserved in the [reproduction comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52362#issuecomment-5675603735). ### ROCm nightly validation — 8x MI355X The main rerun used upstream `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`, PR head `ea586873d5210d9e1624c42333be1b02c276c832`, and stock-AITER image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`. The server used TP=8, FP8 KV, `max_num_seqs=256`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `max_model_len=4096`, synchronous scheduling, prefix caching disabled, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` capture through 2048. Both DSpark arms used probabilistic sampling. `AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=1` avoids a stock AITER post1 sorting fault; AITER MLA/OPUS remained enabled. ShareGPT output throughput, tokens/s: | Concurrency | No speculation | Fixed K=7 | Adaptive K<=7 | Adaptive vs fixed K=7 | Adaptive vs no-spec | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 381.53 | 970.33 | 902.37 | -7.00% | +136.51% | | 8 | 729.20 | 1,762.59 | 1,616.77 | -8.27% | +121.72% | | 16 | 1,342.83 | 2,909.52 | 2,773.69 | -4.67% | +106.56% | | 32 | 2,392.99 | 4,756.32 | 4,501.11 | -5.37% | +88.10% | | 64 | 4,094.75 | 6,712.35 | 7,144.12 | +6.43% | +74.47% | | 128 | 6,340.78 | 8,778.87 | 10,356.48 | +17.97% | +63.33% | | 256 | 8,878.57 | 7,852.42 | 13,324.67 | +69.69% | +50.08% | Each cell used a fresh server, one readiness request, a 64-request c32 warmup, a 64-request cell-concurrency warmup, and 880 measured raw-ShareGPT requests with forced output length 512. All 21 cells completed 880/880 requests with the expected 450,560 generated tokens, no preemptions, and no GPU faults. At c256, adaptive K<=7 reached 13,324.67 tok/s: 69.69% above fixed K=7 and 50.08% above no speculation. Adaptive trades 4.7–8.3% against fixed K=7 at c4–c32 and crosses ahead at c64. The complete three-arm, 1,319-sample GSM8K 5-shot gate also passed: | Mode | Flexible exact match | Strict exact match | |---|---:|---:| | No speculation | `0.9484 +/- 0.0061` | `0.9484 +/- 0.0061` | | Fixed K=7 | `0.9431 +/- 0.0064` | `0.9431 +/- 0.0064` | | Adaptive K<=7 | `0.9492 +/- 0.0060` | `0.9492 +/- 0.0060` | The score range was `0.0061`, within one reported standard error. Reproduction environment and base command: ```bash export AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=1 export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --no-async_scheduling \ --block_size 256 \ --compilation_config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \ --distributed_executor_backend mp \ --enable_auto_tool_choice \ --no-enable_prefix_caching \ --gpu_memory_utilization 0.9 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --kv_cache_dtype fp8 \ --max_model_len 4096 \ --max_num_batched_tokens 4096 \ --max_num_seqs 256 \ --port 8000 \ --reasoning_config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"","reasoning_end_str":""}' \ --reasoning_parser deepseek_v4 \ --tensor_parallel_size 8 \ --tokenizer_mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool_call_parser deepseek_v4 \ --trust_remote_code ``` Fixed K=7 appends: ```bash --speculative_config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' ``` Adaptive K<=7 changes the final field to `"enable_adaptive_verification":true`. For each concurrency, start a fresh server, run the two 64-request warmups described above, then run: ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --dataset-name sharegpt \ --dataset-path "$SHAREGPT_PATH" \ --disable-shuffle \ --ignore-eos \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" \ --num-prompts 880 \ --sharegpt-output-len 512 \ --temperature 1.0 \ --seed 20260902 \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --trust-remote-code ``` The GSM8K gate used: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenizer_backend=none,tokenized_requests=False \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --batch_size 1 \ --seed 42 ``` ## Current ROCm qualification On current ROCm main/nightly, DeepSeek-V4 defaults to Model Runner V1, while DSpark requires Model Runner V2. Set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` when launching this feature. ROCm breakable CUDA graphs were disabled by default for every architecture in [#53155](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53155). DeepSeek V4 adaptive throughput regresses without that execution mode, so the validated launch configuration also sets `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`.

title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support adaptive verification
body:
## Motivation

Adaptive verification chooses on the GPU how many draft tokens to verify for each request. During full CUDA graph replay, the physical token buffer and captured control flow remain fixed, while the live request boundaries can change. GLM-5.3-Flash previously made two assumptions that were incompatible with this behavior:

- GDN captured the ordinary one-token decode path, even though replay could group those token rows into fewer requests with multiple verification tokens.
- The k-pool scatter path assumed every physical token row belonged to a live request, but a replayed graph can contain additional padding rows.

This PR updates both paths to handle GPU-selected request lengths and graph padding.

## Changes

- Allow the GDN backend to replay CUDA graphs whose per-request query lengths are chosen on the GPU.
- Capture GDN’s speculative path and the k-pool indexer at the maximum configured verification width.
- Update the k-pool scatter path to safely discard CUDA graph padding without synchronizing lengths back to the CPU.
- Add tests for variable verification lengths, graph padding, and sparse-indexer alignment.

## Testing

Added and ran focused tests covering:

- Mixed per-request GDN verification lengths
- CUDA graph padding in the k-pool scatter path
- Sparse-indexer sequence-length alignment
- Capture-time and replay-time request partition differences

## Throughput results

I benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP on four B300 GPUs (TEP4). The sweep covered:

- Speculative depths `kmax = 1...5`
- 18 batch sizes from `B = 1` through `B = 256`
- Prefix lengths `S = 512, 8192, 32768`

The table reports decode throughput for adaptive verification relative to fixed verification at the same maximum depth. Each value is the unweighted mean over the `(B, S)` at that speculative depth.

| Maximum depth | Adaptive / fixed at same depth |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.965× |
| 2 | 0.958× |
| 3 | 0.965× |
| 4 | 1.065× |
| 5 | 1.127× |

---

title: [Spec decode] Support variable-length decode for Kimi-K3 adaptive ver
body: ## Summary Make Kimi-K3's MLA and KDA decode paths capturable as FULL varlen CUDA graphs so they work under adaptive DSpark verification (#47808), which schedules ragged per-request draft budgets and requires device-sourced query lengths. Before this change K3's `FLASHINFER_MLA` reported `UNIFORM_BATCH`/`UNIFORM`, and the decode builders derived per-request query length from a measured/averaged count, so a graph captured on a uniform dummy did not match ragged replay. ## Changes **FlashInfer MLA** (`flashinfer_mla.py`) - Promote `_cudagraph_support` to `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` and `query_len_support` to `QueryLenSupport.VARLEN`. - On the causal spec-decode path, pass `cum_seq_lens_q` + `max_q_len` to `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` (flashinfer #3238); assert this path runs on trtllm-gen and does not return LSE (mutually exclusive with DCP). - Flatten non-causal and DCP decode rows by mapping each row to its request with `searchsorted` on the device query offsets instead of `repeat_interleave(uniform_len)`. - Carry `query_start_loc_device`, `cum_seq_lens_q`, and `max_query_len` on the decode metadata; set `cum_seq_lens_q` only when `max_query_len > 1`. **MLA common** (`mla_attention.py` + subclass builders) - Thread a promised `max_query_len` through `MLACommonMetadataBuilder._build_decode` (clamped to `reorder_batch_threshold`) and the `flashmla`, `flashattn_mla`, `rocm_aiter_mla`, and `dots3_note` builders. **KDA** (`kda_metadata.py`) - Promote `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder` to `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`. - Route every active decode through the spec path by masking on `is_prefilling` rather than draft count. - Return `True` from `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch`. **KDA RecoverSSM** (`kda_metadata.py`, opt-in via `--use-replayssm`, off by default) - Make RecoverSSM co-exist with the adaptive path so it can drop the KDA spec-decode SSM state from `num_spec+1` slots to 1 per request (kernels already in #51855): - Restore `self.layer_names` on the builder so RecoverSSM's commit context can resolve the per-layer forward context (the GDN base does not retain it; inert when RecoverSSM is off). - Demote spec rows whose `query_len` exceeds `num_spec+1` out of the RecoverSSM path instead of raising. Adaptive's cost-table profiler probes token counts past the cudagraph limit by even-splitting them over the capped request slots, producing eager dummy rows longer than RecoverSSM's `num_spec+1` verify buffers; real captured/serving decode rows are always `<= num_spec+1`, so they are unaffected. **Mamba-hybrid model state** (`mamba_hybrid.py`) - Prefer the batch's promised `max_query_len`, and classify spec-decode rows off `is_prefilling` rather than `num_scheduled_tokens == draft_count + 1`. **K3 DSpark draft** (`dspark_mla.py`) - Build the confidence head when the config enables it, load its weights (skipped only when the draft did not build one), and expose `compute_confidence`. Related Issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51867 ## Test plan - [x] Updated the MLA backend metadata tests for the new `_build_decode` signature (`test_mla_backends.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`). - [x] Adaptive DSpark spec decode on Kimi-K3 (TP8, fp8 KV). - [x] RecoverSSM + adaptive on Kimi-K3: boots and serves through full-graph capture; validated against the base-adaptive checks (accuracy/coherence artifacts were overwritten by later runs and are being regenerated). ## Validation Kimi-K3 (target) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` (draft), TP8 on 8×B300, FP8 KV cache, `attention_backend=FLASHINFER_MLA`, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, `enable_adaptive_verification=true`. (Numbers below are RecoverSSM off; it is opt-in.) ### Accuracy — lossless vs. no-spec (GSM8K, in-tree runner, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0) | max-concurrency | no-spec | adaptive | |---|---|---| | 16 | 0.949 | 0.949 | | 64 | 0.951 | 0.949 | | 128 | 0.948 | 0.948 | Adaptive matches no-spec within run-to-run noise (invalid-response rate ~0.1% in every run), i.e. adaptive verification is lossless at temperature 0. ### Coherence (MTBench, 80 prompts, temperature 1) Adaptive: 80/80 successful requests, 0 failed, ~19.5K generated tokens; no repetition or degeneration in the saved completions. ### Speculative-decoding health (speed_bench, temperature 1, c16) Acceptance rate 28.95%, acceptance length 3.03, per-position acceptance decaying 74.5% (pos 0) → 6.9% (pos 6) — non-zero at every position, confirming the draft + confidence head + varlen verification path is exercised end to end. ### RecoverSSM (opt-in) health Adaptive + RecoverSSM serves through full-graph capture with healthy acceptance length (2.4–2.9 across c1–c256), confirming the RecoverSSM verify/commit path is exercised end to end; matches base-adaptive accuracy/coherence. ## Benchmarking Pareto sweep of the varlen decode path: 16 configurations × 9 concurrency levels = 144 serving runs. Configurations are fixed draft length K=1..7 plus adaptive, each with and without RecoverSSM. Kimi-K3 (target) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` (draft), TP8 on 8×B300, FP8 KV cache, `attention_backend=FLASHINFER_MLA`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, `num_speculative_tokens=7` for adaptive. `speed_bench` qualitative, `--speed-bench-output-len 2048`, `--max-model-len 16384`, prompt count scaled with concurrency. Axes: per-user token rate (`1000 / median TPOT`) vs aggregate output throughput. Overlaying both families lets a non-RecoverSSM point appear to overtake a RecoverSSM one it never competes with, so each family is also plotted with its own frontier. ### RecoverSSM, adaptive off vs on | c | off | on | gain | |---|---|---|---| | 64 | 2248.6 | 2349.4 | +4.5% | | 128 | 2241.5 | 4454.7 | +98.7% | | 256 | 2222.9 | 4887.9 | +119.9% |

title: [Feature][Spec-Decode]: Cascade: Utility-Driven Adaptive k for MoE Speculative Decoding in V1
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Status Quo
In `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `num_spec_tokens` is set once at engine init and never changes:

```python
self.num_spec_tokens = speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens
if speculative_config.use_eagle():
    self.use_eagle = True
    self.num_lookahead_tokens = self.num_spec_tokens  # fixed for lifetime of engine
```
`num_lookahead_tokens` flows into `kv_cache_manager.allocate_slots()` which pre-allocates KV slots assuming every request in every batch will use exactly `k` draft tokens. Today, there exists no mechanism to vary `k` per-request or disable speculation for a specific request mid-flight without restarting the engine.

This is fine for dense models, however, **for MoE it is actively harmful**. On a dense model, verification overhead is roughly constant because the target model reads all weights regardless of how many draft tokens it verifies. On the other hand, on MoE, every additional draft token activates a different expert subset, so verification data movement scales with `k`, not batch size.  At typical math or reasoning acceptance rates, this makes speculation a net loss.  Cascade (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675) quantifies this precisely across five MoE models.

In `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`, `propose()` has no per-request state. There is nowhere to track acceptance history, utility, or current `k` per request — the entire batch gets the same `num_spec_tokens`.

## Proposed Solution
Upstream [**Cascade** (MLSys 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675) to vLLM V1. Cascade introduces per-request **speculation utility**:
 
```
utility = tokens_accepted / verification_cost(k)
```

Two phases per request — short **test** phase probes k=1..K_max, long **set** phase locks the utility-maximizing K*. If utility < 1.0, speculation is disabled for that request without evicting the draft model.

Paper results on H100: worst-case slowdown **54% → 5%**, throughput improvement **7–14%** over static k.

## What changes in V1
Three components need to change: 
- `per-request state` tracking in the proposer,
- `per-request slot allocation` in the scheduler, and 
- `variable-length draft` handling in the model runner

For CUDA graphs, draft inputs will be padded to `K_max` with masked unused positions, consistent with how existing spec-decode graph captures handle variable batch sizes in `gpu_model_runner.py`.

#### Validation target: NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell)

cc @benchislett 

### Alternatives

Static k tuning reduces but does not eliminate the problem, optimal k varies per request and per task. Prior work #26504 explored `acceptance-rate-based dynamic k` but that does not account for expert activation overhead, which is the dominant cost on MoE verification. 

### Additional context

- Cascade paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20675
- MLSys 2026 poster: https://mlsys.org/virtual/2026/poster/10189
- Prior variable-k PR: #26504
- Spec-decode tracking issue: #28947
- Q2 2026 roadmap: #39749
