title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Warm up adaptive verification budget kernel at startup
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adaptive verification's draft-budget kernel (`_assign_draft_token_budget`, `torch.compile(dynamic=True)`) never runs at startup. Dynamo therefore compiles it during serving: on the first trimmed step, and again for each specialization it meets later. This PR compiles those specializations at startup.

## Claims

- No budget-kernel compiles during generation (main: 2 per run).
- Adaptive throughput +10% at concurrency 16, matching fixed verification again.
- About 1 s extra startup.

## Validation

`pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py -v` → 18 passed (RTX 5000 Ada). The new test checks that no recompile happens under `fail_on_recompile`. It fails with `warmup()` stubbed out, and with an int32 `idx_mapping`.

`pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` passes locally, including mypy.

GSM8K 1-shot, `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`, 7 speculative tokens, probabilistic drafts, concurrency 16, 128 prompts, RTX 5000 Ada, `TRITON_ATTN`. Main and this PR alternated:

| | Output tok/s, median (range) | Compiles during generation | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed verification (n=2) | 1,909 | – | 0.828 |
| Adaptive, main (n=5) | 1,738 (1,615–1,753) | 2 | 0.82–0.84 |
| Adaptive, this PR (n=5) | 1,914 (1,710–1,921) | 0 | 0.820 |

An earlier RTX 3090 run (Qwen3.5-0.8B) showed the same: −7.9% before, no loss after.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

Compiles were counted with `TORCH_LOGS=dynamo`, as `start tracing _assign_draft_token_budget` lines between the two markers. "Main" runs used this branch with `vllm/` checked out at `HEAD~1`.

```python
import json
import sys

from tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval import evaluate_gsm8k_offline
from vllm import LLM

mode, conc = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "dspark",
        "model": "deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 7,
        "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
        "enable_adaptive_verification": mode == "adaptive",
    },
    max_num_seqs=conc,
    max_model_len=4096,
    enable_prefix_caching=False,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
    attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN",
)
print("=== GENERATE START ===", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
result = evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=8 * conc, num_shots=1)
print("=== GENERATE END ===", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
print("RESULT", json.dumps({"mode": mode, "conc": conc, **result}), flush=True)
```

</details>

## Details

- Startup never reaches the kernel: `warmup_kernels` disables adaptive verification, and cost profiling never trims. Dynamo then specializes on a full batch (duck-sized to `confidence_probs`), a single request, and a budget of 1.
- `warmup()` runs batch sizes {1, max−1, max} × budgets {1, 2}. It uses the manager's real buffers and `prepare_inputs`' int64 `idx_mapping` (#60736), since guards check dispatch keys and dtypes. It's skipped on the `profile_only` pass, whose buffers are torn down.
- Not a duplicate: #59976 skips adaptive verification; #58340 only adds metrics.

title: [Spec Decode] Enable Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification with FlashInfer
body: ## Purpose Enable Gemma4 DSpark adaptive verification with FlashInfer TRTLLM-GEN, building on #52157 (#51871): graph-safe variable-length decode, trained confidence-head loading, graph-cache separation, and RoPE config normalization. Adaptive verification replays FULL decode CUDA graphs in which each request has 1 to 1 + k query tokens, read from the device `query_start_loc` (k = `num_speculative_tokens`). On `main` it requires every target builder to report `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`, which also promises graphs for mixed prefill/decode batches. FlashInfer's TRTLLM-GEN path can replay variable-length decode batches but not mixed ones, so, per review, this PR declares that capability separately instead of adding an enum member: - **`AttentionCGSupport` is unchanged.** - **New builder classmethod** `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec) -> int | None`: the largest per-request query length L for which one FULL cudagraph replays any decode batch with 1 to L query tokens per request. It returns `None` for `ALWAYS` builders, which replay any batch, and for builders without variable-length support. | Builder | `get_cudagraph_support()` | `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len()` | Adaptive verification | |---|---|---|---| | `ALWAYS` builders (FA3, Triton, FlexAttention, Kimi-K3 KDA, FlashInfer MLA, ...) | `ALWAYS` | `None` | supported | | FlashInfer with its TRTLLM-GEN varlen path active (adaptive verification on, SM100 family, no DCP) | `UNIFORM_BATCH` | `1 + k` | supported (needs at least `1 + k`) | | FlashInfer otherwise, and other builders below `ALWAYS` | unchanged | `None` | not supported | - **Readers.** Adaptive verification is the only reader: every target builder must report `ALWAYS` or a bound of at least `1 + k`. CUDA graph mode resolution and capture are unchanged. - **Batches with a prefill no longer replay varlen decode graphs.** Dispatch matched those graphs on `max(num_scheduled_tokens)` alone, so decodes plus a prefill chunk of at most `1 + k` tokens replayed a decode graph. That is harmless for FlashInfer and FlashInfer MLA, which run short prefills on their decode kernels, but not for Kimi-K3's KDA builder (`ALWAYS` since #52988): it classifies rows by request state and does not restage its graph buffers when a prefill row is present. The runner now passes `max_query_len=None` for any batch with a prefill. - **Decode width on model runner V2.** Six copies of `1 + (2 if parallel_drafting else 1) * k` now share `max_decode_query_len()`. The 2× covers model runner V1's parallel drafter only, so on V2 the spec-as-decode width is `1 + k`, and DFlash/DSpark prefill chunks of `k + 2` to `2k + 1` tokens take the prefill kernel. Not a duplicate: #53929 proposes a `VARLEN_DECODE` member to enable adaptive DSpark verification for Qwen GDN; under this design GDN would override `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len()` instead. ## Test Plan On one GB300, BF16, model runner V2, rebased on `9ef37771be` (includes #52988): ```bash pre-commit run --files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \ tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \ tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py \ tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \ tests/test_config.py tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py ``` The full list, 31 files, also covers the linear-attention, chunked-local, DCP, batch splitting and reordering, Gemma4 model and TRTLLM-GEN varlen kernel suites. End to end, Gemma4-12B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` K=7, comparing this revision with the previous one: - GSM8K, 50 questions, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, fixed and adaptive verification. - A mix of 4 long generations and 40 prompts of 2 to 7 tokens under adaptive verification, `max_num_seqs=8`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, so that verification rows and short prefills share steps. Full GSM8K, all 1,319 test questions, 5-shot raw completions, temperature 0 / seed 0, 512-token cap, pretrained Gemma4-12B, BF16 TP1 (measured on the first revision; the captured graphs are unchanged since): | Mode | Correct / total | Accuracy | | --- | ---: | ---: | | No speculation | 822 / 1,319 | 62.32% | | DSpark K=7 | 828 / 1,319 | 62.77% | | DSpark K=7 + adaptive | 826 / 1,319 | 62.62% | Adaptive versus fixed: −0.15 percentage points (two questions), exact paired McNemar p=0.868. All 3,957 requests completed with no preemptions or request errors. ## Test Result - **Lint:** pre-commit and mypy 3.12 pass. - **Tests:** 3,201 pass. The 9 failures are all accounted for: - 6 DCP distributed tests in `tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py` and 2 tests on gated `meta-llama` repos also fail on the previous revision. - One fp8 `TRTLLM_RAGGED` `small_decode` case in `test_mla_backends.py` passed 3/3 on rerun on both revisions. - **Short-prefill mix:** the previous revision replayed the varlen decode graph for all 31 steps that paired verification rows with a prefill of at most 7 tokens. This revision runs all 32 such steps piecewise, and decode-only steps still replay FULL graphs. 36 of 44 completions are token-identical; the other 8 diverge at greedy near-ties, and within a single run the same prompt also yields both variants depending on its batch. - **GSM8K:** captured FULL graphs are identical to the previous revision (fixed 2 + 32, adaptive 2 + 35). Accuracy is 25/50 fixed and 24/50 adaptive, against 24/50 and 24/50; 47/50 and 50/50 answers are identical. ## Perf Benchmark No speculation vs DSpark K=7 vs DSpark K=7 with adaptive verification, Gemma4-12B with `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7`, one GB300, TP1, BF16 (first revision): AI assistance was used (OpenAI Codex and Claude Code). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [DFlash] Capture the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph
body:
## Purpose

Even when the query forward replays a FULL CUDA graph, the DFlash/DSpark draft step still runs the context K/V precompute (`precompute_and_store_context_kv`) eagerly outside the graph, because the number of context tokens varies from step to step.

This PR captures the context K/V precompute ahead of the query forward in the draft's FULL decode graph. Each graph stores one full verify of context rows per request; rows past the batch are padded with `PAD_SLOT_ID` so they write no K/V, and any prefill context beyond the graph's rows is stored eagerly before replay. The precompute has no host syncs, so every DFlash drafter captures it. The draft attention metadata build stays eager, as before.


## Validation

Capturing the context K/V precompute must not change the speculator's proposals. The checks below therefore compare acceptance and accuracy between this branch's parent commit (`c723a831a8`) and `d8de1d3a2f`, and serving performance against current main, with everything else held fixed.

### Setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Speculative decoding:** DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and full decode CUDA graphs.
- **Topologies:**
  - **DEP4:** MegaMoE backend with adaptive verification.
  - **TP4:** auto MoE backend with fixed verification.

### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each pair runs the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction.

Acceptance length is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the whole run for DEP4. For TP4, it is aggregated from the engine's periodic SpecDecoding log windows over the steady state; the same method is used on both sides of each pair.

| Configuration | Acceptance length, incl. bonus (parent → PR) | GSM8K (parent → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.411 → **3.434** | 1234 → 1228 / 1319 (93.56% → 93.10%) |
| TP4 | 3.471 → **3.463** | 1227 → 1219 / 1319 (93.03% → 92.42%) |

- The acceptance deltas are within ±1% and have opposite signs across the two topologies, and the per-position acceptance curves coincide. The captured precompute therefore does not change what the drafter proposes.
- The GSM8K deltas are run-to-run noise: two repeats of the same DEP4 parent configuration scored 0.9219 and 0.9356 (an 18/1319 spread), which is wider than any delta in the table.
- These results establish parity with the parent; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K server configuration</summary>

Common flags:

```bash
--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128
```

DSpark is configured with 5 speculative tokens.

- **DEP4:** `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`, with adaptive verification enabled.
- **TP4:** `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, with the auto MoE backend and adaptive verification disabled.

</details>

### Serving benchmark

TP4, DSpark (5 speculative tokens, synthetic acceptance length 5.5), random dataset with 128 input / 1,024 output tokens. **Base** is main and **PR** is `d8de1d3a2f`. CPU/step is the host time per engine step, measured with an injected per-step probe.

| Concurrency | CPU/step | TPOT | ITL |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.77 → 5.03 ms | 1.27 → 1.08 ms (−15.2%) | 6.95 → 5.88 ms (−15.3%) |
| 8 | 6.64 → 5.24 ms | 1.87 → 1.84 ms (−1.6%) | 9.96 → 9.90 ms (−0.6%) |
| 64 | 6.82 → 5.43 ms | 3.90 → 3.87 ms (−0.7%) | 19.97 → 20.01 ms (+0.2%) |

The PR cuts host time per step by 1.4–1.7 ms. At concurrency 1 the step is host-bound, so this carries through to a ~15% lower TPOT and ITL; at higher concurrency the GPU dominates and latency is roughly unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark configuration</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":5.5}'

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|64>
```

</details>

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q
```

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change: the implementation, the evaluation runs, and this description were produced with Claude Code.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] Overlap the unfused shared expert with AITER MegaMoE
body:
## Overview

With `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` and an unfused shared expert, DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm ran the shared expert after the router and MegaMoE, on the main stream. This PR runs it on the aux stream next to the router + MegaMoE through `maybe_execute_in_parallel`. It follows the existing `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM` / `VLLM_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` convention: the overlap applies to steps of at most 256 tokens by default, and `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1` keeps the serial order. ATOM overlaps its shared expert with the routed experts the same way.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro, AgentX agentic workload: P90 interactivity +2.7% at concurrency 128 and +6.4% at concurrency 64.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k.
- Prefill-sized steps and the fused shared-expert path are unchanged.

## Validation

Setup:
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, DP8 attention + EP8 AITER MegaMoE, shared expert unfused.
- AgentX agentic workload, 1200 s runs, requests counted in the 300-1200 s window.
- Single runs per configuration.

| | Without | With this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| c128 (same node, same job): P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 27.13 | 27.87 (+2.7%) |
| c128: output tok/s/GPU | 335 | 346 (+3.3%) |
| c128: total tok/s/GPU | | +1.4% |
| c64 (same node, separate jobs): P90 interactivity | 48.26 | 51.33 (+6.4%) |
| c64: P50 interactivity | 61.65 | 64.31 (+4.3%) |
| c64: total tok/s/GPU | | -1.5% |
| gsm8k 5-shot, real speculative decoding (flexible / strict) | 0.9697 / 0.9704 | 0.9727 / 0.9735 |

Unit tests and lint:
- `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` on MI355X: 10 passed, against 6 on main. The 4 new cases run the shared expert on the aux stream.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed, mypy included. This was rerun on the current main, which includes #61262.

## Details

- When MegaMoE fuses the shared expert, `shared_experts` is `None` and the routed path runs alone, as before.
- `maybe_execute_in_parallel` falls back to sequential execution when the stream is `None` and during breakable CUDA graph capture.
- #61262's runtime selection runs inside the MegaMoE call on the main stream, so it is not affected.

title: [Model][Experimental] DeepSeek V4 w4a4 MegaMoE support
body:
seealso: #42845 https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/issues/338
## Purpose

MegaMoE currently packs activations as FP8 (E4M3) in the symmetric buffer before dispatch. On Blackwell (SM100), FP4 (E2M1) packing would halve the buffer footprint and unlock the MXF4 mainloop (K=64 dense vs K=32 padded) in DeepGEMM.

However, upstream DeepGEMM does not yet support FP4 activations end-to-end. The `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` kernel hardcodes `a_dtype_t = float_e4m3_t`, `get_symm_buffer_size_for_mega_moe` allocates input token buffers at FP8 width (`hidden` bytes/token), and the dispatch stage TMA loads assume FP8 layout. The `use_fp8_dispatch` parameter exists in the API signature but is not wired through to the buffer sizing or kernel logic. An RFC has been filed at deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM to track this.

This PR provides a **proof-of-concept** using `sgl-deep-gemm>=0.1.0`, which ships a `mega_moe_pre_dispatch()` CUDA kernel that handles E2M1 packing + FP4-aware buffer allocation. Two opt-in env vars, both default off:
- `VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS` -- use `deep_gemm.mega_moe_pre_dispatch()` for E2M1 activation packing instead of the Triton staging kernel
- `VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND` -- switches to `kind::mxf4` mainloop, requires FP4 acts

When enabled, imports external `deep_gemm` for buffer allocation and pre-dispatch. When disabled, vendored `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` is used as before -- zero change to default path.

Flags forwarded to the external deep_gemm via `os.environ.setdefault("DG_USE_FP4_ACTS", ...)` so explicit `DG_USE_*` overrides still win.

Files: `vllm/envs.py`, `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py`

## Upstream Gap Analysis

Checked deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM (latest, identical to vendored commit 891d57b for the mega module):

- `csrc/apis/mega.hpp`: `get_symm_buffer_size_for_mega_moe` accepts `use_fp8_dispatch` but ignores it -- `input_token_buffer` is always `layout::Data(hidden)` (FP8, 1 byte/element)
- `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.cuh` line 162-163: `a_dtype_t = cutlass::float_e4m3_t` -- UMMA configured for FP8 activations only
- Dispatch pull stage: TMA loads `kHidden` bytes per token (FP8 width)
- `slice_input_buffers` returns `x` as `[tokens, hidden]` float8, `x_sf` as `[tokens, hidden/128]`

None of these support FP4 activations. Full FP4 activation support requires changes at the C++/CUDA kernel level (buffer sizing, TMA load widths, UMMA A-matrix dtype), which is being tracked via the upstream RFC.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 8x B200 (SM100, 183GB). Accuracy: GSM8K full test set (1319 samples), greedy decoding, max_tokens=2048, concurrency=32.

Dep: `pip install sgl-deep-gemm==0.1.0`

V4-Flash (256 experts, hidden=4096, 43 layers), DP=4:

```bash
# w4a8 baseline
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager

# w4a4 (this PR)
VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1 \
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager
```

V4-Pro (384 experts, hidden=7168, 61 layers), TP=8:

```bash
# w4a8 baseline
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager

# w4a4 (this PR)
VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 VLLM_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1 \
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enforce-eager
```

Eval: hit `/v1/chat/completions`, extract final number after `####`, compare against reference.

## Test Result

### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 samples, greedy)

V4-Flash: w4a8 93.86% (1238/1319) -> w4a4 94.39% (1245/1319), delta +0.53%
V4-Pro: w4a8 91.81% (1211/1319) -> w4a4 91.13% (1202/1319), delta -0.68%

Both within noise. No meaningful accuracy degradation from FP4 activation packing.

### Performance (V4-Flash, DP=4, 8×B200)

Benchmark config: 500 prompts, input_len=1024, output_len=8, max-concurrency=64, request-rate=inf, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512`, random dataset.

| Metric | w4a8 | w4a4 | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 11.21 | 17.73 | **+58.2%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 11,565.65 | 18,294.09 | **+58.2%** |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 89.66 | 141.81 | **+58.2%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3,789.39 | 1,834.52 | **-51.6%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 832.51 | 639.82 | **-23.1%** |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 12,302.93 | 12,063.23 | -1.9% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 272.46 | 251.78 | **-7.6%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 75.91 | 69.89 | **-7.9%** |

Key takeaway: ~58% throughput improvement, ~52% mean TTFT reduction. The gain is dominated by prefill (MXF4 mainloop K=64 dense vs K=32 padded). Decode TPOT improves ~8% from reduced buffer bandwidth.

## What Happens When Upstream Supports FP4 Acts

Once deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM wires `use_fp8_dispatch=False` through to buffer sizing + kernel:
1. Bump vendored commit in `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake`
2. Replace `sgl-deep-gemm` path with a Triton FP4 staging kernel (~40 lines, E2M1 bucketize + pack) or use whatever staging API upstream provides
3. Change `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe(..., use_fp8_dispatch=False)` -- the parameter already exists
4. Remove import branches (3 sites), drop `sgl-deep-gemm` dep
5. `DG_USE_FP4_ACTS` / `DG_USE_MXF4_KIND` env forwarding likely becomes unnecessary -- remove `_apply_mega_moe_dg_env`
6. Move env vars from experimental to stable

title: [RFC]: support hopper FP8 MegaMoE backend for DeepSeek-V4
body: ### Motivation. DeepSeek-V4's fused MoE expert kernel ("MegaMoE") is wired into vLLM for Blackwell (sm_100) as `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`, calling `deep_gemm.fp8_fp4_mega_moe`. On **Hopper (sm_90 — H20 / H100 / H800)** that path is unusable because Hopper has no FP4 tensor cores. [DeepGEMM PR #323](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/323)has just landed an SM90 sibling, `fp8_mega_moe`, that fuses the same five steps and accepts block-(128, 128) MN-major `float32` weight SF tensors **directly** This RFC proposes wiring `deep_gemm.fp8_mega_moe` into vLLM as a sibling of the existing FP4 MegaMoE class so DeepSeek-V4 served on Hopper (especially H20) gets the fused kernel benefit Blackwell already enjoys. ### Proposed Change. ### Adaptation points One file changed | Where | What | | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v4.py` | Add `DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts` (block-FP8 sibling of `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`) + an SM90 input-staging Triton kernel + a custom op. | | `DeepseekV4MoE._init_mega_moe_experts` (same file) | Dispatch on `expert_dtype`: `"fp4"` → existing class (sm_100), `"fp8"` → new class (sm_90). | | `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` | Extend with Hopper unit tests. | | `tests/models/run_hopper_mega_moe_ep8.py` + `scripts/run_megamoe_bench.sh` | Manual EP8 multi-GPU correctness + bench harness. | ```bash python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kernel-config '{"moe_backend": "deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ``` ### Code sketch `DeepseekV4MoE._init_mega_moe_experts` becomes (existing `if/else` shown for context, the `fp8` branch is new): ```python if self._mega_moe_expert_dtype == "fp4": self.experts = DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts(...) # sm_100, existing else: # "fp8" self.experts = DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts(...) # sm_90, NEW ``` `DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts.finalize_weights` (one-shot weight transform; idempotent): ```python import deep_gemm # DeepGEMM PR #323: SM90 weight transform = gate/up gran-8 N interleave # only; block-(128, 128) float32 SF flows through unchanged. l1, l2 = deep_gemm.transform_weights_for_mega_moe_sm90( (self.w13_weight.data, self.w13_weight_scale_inv.data), (self.w2_weight.data, self.w2_weight_scale_inv.data), ) self._transformed_l1_weights, self._transformed_l2_weights = l1, l2 ``` `DeepseekV4HopperMegaMoEExperts._run_hopper_mega_moe` (one fused launch per layer per forward): ```python import deep_gemm # Stage hidden -> FP8 + per-128-K float SF into the symmetric buffer. _stage_deepseek_v4_mega_moe_inputs_sm90( hidden_states, topk_weights, topk_ids, symm_buffer.x[:n], symm_buffer.x_sf[:n], symm_buffer.topk_idx[:n], symm_buffer.topk_weights[:n], ) deep_gemm.fp8_mega_moe( y, self._transformed_l1_weights, self._transformed_l2_weights, symm_buffer, recipe=(128, 128, 128), # required by the SM90 host-side check activation="swiglu", activation_clamp=activation_clamp, fast_math=fast_math, ) ``` ### Hard guards The new class fails loudly (`NotImplementedError` / `ValueError`) when: * device is not sm_90; * `--enable-expert-parallel` is missing; * `scoring_func != "sqrtsoftplus"`; * `hidden % 128 != 0` or `intermediate % 128 != 0`; * SF dtype != `float32` or shape != `(E, M//128, K//128)`. ##### This RFC depends on upstream [DeepGEMM PR #323](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/323) (HEAD `192a513a`), which adds the SM90 `fp8_mega_moe` kernel, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe_sm90`, and `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe`. The corresponding vLLM implementation is **already written and locally verified** (10 unit tests passed, 1 skipped-by-design; full EP8 correctness + bench harness in place). However, **no further development on the vLLM side will happen until DeepGEMM #323 is merged**: * the implementation PR will not be opened (or will stay in `Draft`) while the upstream API can still change; * no request for review will be made of vLLM maintainers until 323 lands; ## Test Plan * **Unit (CI-friendly)** — `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` ```bash pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -v ``` * **vLLM EP benchmark (8×H20)** — ```bash bash scripts/run_megamoe_bench.sh small full ``` Spawns 8 ranks via `torch.multiprocessing.spawn`, then for each shape compares (a) direct DeepGEMM call vs (b)`DeepEP-LL + BatchedDeepGemmExperts` pipeline for a latency baseline. Numbers will be pasted into the implementation PR description. ### Feedback Period. two weeks ### CC List. @WoosukKwon ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM
body:
## Summary

Integrate DeepGEMM Mega-Gate into the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 DeepGEMM MegaMoE path, fusing the gate GEMM and expert selection. Prepare routing metadata once per model forward and reuse it across layers. Preserve hash routing for V4, image routing bias for V4.1, draft-layer expert counts, MTP warmup, and decoder auxiliary-state capture.

Two integration fixes are included:

- Let CMake FetchContent update an existing DeepGEMM checkout when its pinned revision changes. Previously, finding `csrc/python_api.cpp` skipped the update entirely and could rebuild 2.6.1 without `bf16_mega_gate` despite the new pin.
- ~~Clear padded hidden-state rows in place before Mega-Gate. NaN padding can trigger the kernel's finite-score assertion, later surfacing as a CUDA launch failure or NCCL error. `masked_fill_` avoids allocating a separate hidden-state tensor; valid rows are unchanged. Regression cases cover NaN padding for both main/draft and text/image routing.~~ Removed, fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11

Update (17 Sep 2026)
- Since Mega-Gate underperforms for M<=16 (as LL-GEMM is very efficient), we only dispatch Mega-Gate for M>16

## Accuracy: full GSM8K

The final in-place implementation was evaluated locally through Vigil on **4× GB200**, using real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` weights, the current repository checkout, CUDA 13.1, and PyTorch 2.13.0. No engine overrides beyond TP4, EP, and the MegaMoE backend were supplied; CUDA Graphs remained enabled.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Questions | 1319 |
| Correct | **1194** |
| Accuracy | **90.5231%** |
| Invalid responses | **0** |
| API failures | **0** |
| Worker errors | **0** |
| Evaluation time | 161.79 s |


## Kernel benchmark: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Gate

Measured on a **single NVIDIA GB300 (SM103)** with BF16 inputs `[M, 5120]`, BF16 gate weights `[384, 5120]`, **top-k=6**, `sqrtsoftplus`, normalization, and routed scaling factor **1.5**. **M is the number of token rows processed on one GPU**, not serving request concurrency.

The baseline is `GateLinear + fused_topk_bias`, using its normal shape-dependent dispatch. Mega-Gate fuses the gate GEMM and expert selection. The updated DeepGEMM pin allows non-finite padding scores, eliminating the separate hidden-state padding clear; existing input staging discards padded routes.

**Mega-Gate achieves 1.18–1.31× routing speedup for M ≥ 32, with no meaningful speedup for M ≤ 16.** Speedup is baseline latency divided by Mega-Gate latency.

| Tokens M | GateLinear + top-k (μs) | Mega-Gate (μs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.640 | 8.096 | 0.820× |
| 2 | 6.848 | 8.032 | 0.853× |
| 4 | 6.752 | 8.032 | 0.841× |
| 8 | 8.064 | 8.224 | 0.981× |
| 16 | 8.256 | 8.256 | 1.000× |
| 32 | 10.112 | 8.304 | 1.218× |
| 64 | 10.353 | 8.448 | 1.225× |
| 128 | 11.200 | 8.896 | 1.259× |
| 256 | 11.488 | 9.696 | 1.185× |
| 512 | 13.520 | 10.720 | 1.261× |
| 1024 | 16.000 | 12.448 | 1.285× |
| 2048 | 18.913 | 15.872 | 1.192× |
| 4096 | 27.729 | 22.944 | 1.209× |
| 8192 | 46.752 | 35.745 | 1.308× |

**Method:** FlashInfer CUPTI timing of CUDA-graph replays with cold L2, 25 warmups, three rounds with alternating implementation order, and 100 samples per round. Values are medians of the round medians. Allocation, compilation, graph capture, input generation, routing metadata preparation, expert input staging, expert execution, and communication are outside the timed region. These measurements do not establish an E2E serving speedup.

**Correctness:** Expert IDs matched exactly at every batch size; routing weights matched with `rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-4`. Synthetic inputs and separated correction biases avoid ambiguous top-k boundaries. An additional 48 CUDA-graph replay cases passed with NaN/Inf padding across text, image, and hash/image routing.

**Versions:** vLLM `ef50fde183`, DeepGEMM `40d109bf`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA toolkit `13.1`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, and CUPTI Python `13.0.1`.

## Related work and AI assistance

This updates the existing Mega-Gate PR rather than opening another implementation. Open-PR searches for `56266 in:body` and `Mega-Gate` were checked before reopening. Dependency/API changes overlap intentionally with #56876; that PR supplies the dependency update, while this PR adds the Mega-Gate routing integration. The upstream Mega-Gate implementation is tracked in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/432.

OpenAI Codex assisted with the port, dependency alignment, conflict resolution, build-cache and padding fixes, compilation, debugging, and validation. Dependency/API changes adapted from #56876 are attributed in the commit history.

title: [ROCm][DSv4] EPLB for the AITER MegaMoE backend
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4's AITER MegaMoE backend (`--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`) rejected `--enable-eplb`. This PR hooks it into vLLM's EPLB, the same way the DeepGEMM MegaMoE path does. On DeepSeek-V4-Pro, ATOM's EPLB for the same kernels cuts the long-context prefill step by 14.6%. The last three commits are generic EPLB changes that MegaMoE EPLB needs on ROCm; each can be split out.

## Claims

- `--enable-eplb` works with `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`. It rebalances by permutation only (`num_redundant_experts=0`), as ATOM does.
- `EPLBConfig.max_rebalances` (new; default 0 = no limit, unchanged behaviour): stop after N rebalance points and keep the placement.
- ROCm: `torch_nccl` expert-weight transfers no longer hang RCCL.
- ROCm: the "skip rearrange" check no longer vetoes every MegaMoE rebalance.

Usage (sync EPLB; `torch_nccl` requires `use_async: false`):

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"use_async": false, "communicator": "torch_nccl", "max_rebalances": 2}'
```

## Validation

The numbers below come from a lab branch: vLLM 77154ca6 plus this change, alongside unrelated local patches. Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x MI355X, TP1 x DP8 attention, EP8 AITER MegaMoE, DSpark draft. EPLB ran with window 100 / interval 200 and at most 2 rebalances. The lab counted only engine steps that contain a prefill; that counting is not part of this PR, and a larger window and interval in engine steps give a similar cadence.

Prefill probe: each of the 8 ranks prefills 8,107 new tokens at ~108K context next to 16 decoding requests:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| prefill step (ms, median of 6 rounds) | 1102 | 944 (-14.3%) |
| MegaMoE combine wait per step (ms, mean over ranks; worst rank) | 167 (180) | 36 (55) |
| MegaMoE stage1 / stage2 per step (ms) | 165 / 231 | 164 / 225 |
| decode step at 16 req/rank (ms) | 55.6 | 55.5 - 56.3 |

ATOM gets -14.6% on the same probe. The gain is the combine wait: the expert GEMM time per rank stays the same, but the busiest rank no longer holds every rank back.

- gsm8k (lm-eval, real speculative decoding) with EPLB on: 0.9719 / 0.9727 (two runs).
- A rebalance moves ~2.5k of each rank's 2.9k expert slots across 61 layers. The first one took 5.2-5.7 s in the probe and load runs, ~2.3 s of it RCCL connection setup, and up to ~12 s under heavier live traffic. Later ones take ~2.5 s. ATOM's migration takes 5.4 s.
- Stress test under load: 34 forced full-permutation rebalances while serving 32 concurrent requests, 0 request errors, correct greedy answers before and after.
- Unit tests (CPU): `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py` (ring pairing, cap, per-layer imbalance) and `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py -m cpu_test` (weight views, remap before the runtime choice, MixtureOfExperts registration; importing it needs a ROCm build).

E2e and validation on this upstream branch are still to be added.

## Details

**MegaMoE EPLB (commit 1).**
- The AMD `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` implements `MixtureOfExperts` over the MegaMoE layers only; other AMD MoE paths keep `num_moe_layers == 0`.
- `DeepseekV4AiterMegaMoEExperts.get_expert_weights()` returns per-expert row views of the finalized w13 / w2 weights and scales. The a16w4 shuffles are within-expert, so EPLB rewrites rows in place. MegaMoEV2 reads the weights by pointer at every launch, so CUDA graphs stay valid.
- `forward()` maps logical to physical ids with `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` (load recording included) before the runtime choice. The fixed-slot decode runtime (#61262) and the prefill runtime therefore both dispatch physical ids. Per-expert slot capacity does not depend on placement.
- Redundant experts are rejected.
- The DSpark draft is not registered: its MoE only sees decode-sized batches, and it keeps its own static placement.

**`max_rebalances` (commit 2).** Every rebalance point blocks all EP ranks. A skipped point still pays an all-reduce, a host sync and the policy, and an applied one moves weights for seconds. When the placement only needs to adapt once (ATOM uses `ATOM_EPLB_MAX_REBALANCES=2` here), the cap stops further points; the remap stays and load recording stops.

**ROCm ring P2P order (commit 3), root cause.**
- `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace` posts a layer's sends and receives as one `batch_isend_irecv`: about 340 ops per rank here.
- With RCCL 2.27.7 on MI355X this deadlocks on some transfer plans. The trigger is a rank that sends to many peers while it also exchanges with one peer in both directions.
- It is deterministic for a given plan. A torch-only 8-GPU reproducer hangs on the same seeded plans every time, with one batch per layer and also with ATOM-style 32-expert chunks. In serving it killed the engine at the execute timeout during the first rebalance.
- The fix: on ROCm, `TorchDistNcclEplbCommunicator` runs the layer as ring batches. Batch d holds the sends to rank + d and the receives from rank - d, in the same d order on every rank, so a send and its receive meet in the same batch with one peer per direction.
- Results: 4k seeded plans in the reproducer and 4k plans through `rearrange_expert_weights_inplace` (random and default-policy plans), no hang, 0 misplaced rows, ~47 ms per layer.
- A no-op `EplbCommunicator.prepare_transfer()` hook lets the communicator create its group's communicator with a collective first, because a ring batch need not involve every rank. Other platforms keep one batch per layer.

**Per-layer skip check (commit 4).** The ROCm-only check skips a placement unless the rank-load imbalance improves by 5%. It summed each rank's load over all layers before taking max/mean, so per-layer skews on different ranks cancelled out. MegaMoE's per-layer max/mean of ~1.77 (to ~1.12 after rebalancing) read as 1.063 -> 1.118, and every rebalance was skipped. Each MoE layer waits for its busiest rank, so the check now uses the sum over layers of max over the sum over layers of mean, the same quantity `log_balancedness` reports.

**Not included / follow-ups.**
- This PR keeps the profile-time dummy rearrangement. With `torch_nccl` it all-gathers one layer of expert weights, and its load all-reduce creates the EP group's RCCL communicator, which MoRI otherwise never uses. Together that costs ~12 GiB of KV cache per rank here: 95.7 -> 83.3 GiB with EPLB on, vs 93.8 GiB in the lab with that step skipped. This can follow separately.
- `pynccl` transfers are not ring-ordered.
- No redundant experts.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description; the measurements come from the author's runs.

---

title: [DSv4.1][BI] Bitwise batch invariance for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with CUDA graphs
body:
## Purpose

Make DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash inference bitwise batch invariant under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with CUDA graphs on (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE), DEP4, DSpark MTP and MegaMoE. Under BI, token ids and logprobs are bitwise identical regardless of batch composition and order, chunk size, decode vs `prompt_logprobs` re-feed, prefix-cache hit vs miss and DP rank placement. Target is RL true on-policy rollouts.

BI=0 behavior is unchanged except for the DSv4.1 model fixes in the first commit (Engram stack entry, SWA block stride alignment, stale `-1` tail in combined indices).

## Changes (28 commits, grouped)

1. **DSv4.1 fixes**: Engram stack entry, 32 B SWA block stride, combine index tails, replay-disable conditions.
2. **BI CUDA op library** (`csrc/batch_invariant/`): K32 block-scaled GEMM, fused SiLU-mul + group quant, deterministic radix top-k (larger index wins ties), sparse decode gather, SWA-first index combine, ordered expert permute/combine.
3. **Dense**: row-invariant BF16 / MXFP8 projections, RMSNorm, logits and logprobs.
4. **Attention**: FlashMLA sparse and indexer under BI; decode and prefill produce the same bits (SWA-first layout, decode compressed length by position).
5. **Exact SWA bounded replay**: replay stays on but becomes exact under BI (decoder trimming keeps W+(n-1)(W-1) rows, prefix-hit replay recomputes W+L(W-1) tokens), optional layer-wise staging, padding rows masked.
6. **MoE**: MegaMoE under BI, ordered BF16 EP reduce-scatter + rank-order FP32 combine, router pinned, `empty_cache` before symmetric-memory allocation.
7. **mHC**: fixed split counts for every M, fused post+pre-norm kernel with warmup.
8. **DSpark**: draft rows and aux hidden-state capture under BI.
9. **Opt-in faster BI tiers** (`VLLM_BI_*`): tensor-core MXFP8/BF16 GEMM (non-split-K tactics only), MXFP8 prequant, startup precompile of every reachable M.
10. **Opt-in Mega tier**: Mega mHC with fixed split, split-mHC overlap side stream, mega attention under BI, Mega Gate in deterministic mode.

Opt-in tiers are bitwise batch invariant but round differently from the default BI path. A trainer that wants true on-policy must call the same kernels.

## Test Plan / Results

Measured on GB200 (DEP4, DSpark 5 tokens, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 8192 in / 1024 out) on the pre-rebase tree. This branch is the same stack rebased onto current main with mechanical conflict resolution; it has not been re-run on GPU after the rebase.

**Bitwise gates (BI=1, graphs on): all 0 diff.**
- alone / batch / reversed, pinned and unpinned DP ranks
- decode vs `prompt_logprobs` re-feed
- `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048 vs 8192 vs 16384, cross-run
- prefix cache hit vs miss
- MTP on, batch combinations

**Throughput, BI=1 / BI=0, same image and recipe, only `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` differs.** 12 AB/BA pairs, median output throughput ratio:

| c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.911 | 0.922 | 0.919 | 0.907 |

**Unit tests**: new BI op tests are bitwise against reference implementations on the target shapes, including decode == prefill across ragged/compact top-k, multi-chunk and h_q in {64, 128}. They run under BI=0 and BI=1. Remaining failures in the touched suites are pre-existing on the base.

**Lint**: `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passes, including mypy.

**After the rebase** (3 extra commits move the replay gather and decode top-k lengths from Triton to BI CUDA ops), the full bitwise gate matrix was re-run on an image built from this branch: all 0 diff, and 6711 token/logprob records are bitwise equal to the pre-rebase image. Rebase adaptations:
- `FixedBf16Gemm.dispatch` accepts the new `output_dtype` (#62042).
- BI forces `use_psum_layout=False` for DeepGemmFP4Experts (#59044).
- Compressor test config gains PCP fields (#59857).

## Image

`docker.io/aosheninferact/vllm-dsv41-bi:pr-d667e410e1` (linux/arm64, digest `sha256:fed655f0ba640908b11e71b9f188a2ea972c013e7697fb9ed14bebb81bd577fa`): official nightly `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294` plus one layer with this branch's vLLM package and the two rebuilt extensions, plus a Python-only layer with the last two commits (per-call eager breaks, CuTe stream).

## Known gaps

- Only the V2 model runner (the default) is supported under BI. The V1 runner is not covered.

- `prompt_logprobs` with very large row counts can still JIT-compile the lm_head GEMM while serving.
- Validated on GB200 only.

## Duplicate-work check

This overlaps with in-flight work on batch invariance (#54955 and its splits #59925, #59929, #60442; #59863 fused SiLU-mul quant; #62208 / #60613 DSv4.1 fixes; my own #57815). This PR is the end-to-end DSv4.1-Flash stack that the bitwise gates above were measured on. It is submitted as one PR at the maintainer's request; reconciling with those PRs can follow in review.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and audit this change. The submitter reviewed the change and the results above.

title: [Weight Reload][MegaMoE] Rebuild module-owned packed expert buffers
body:
## Purpose

Declare routed MegaMoE packed weights/scales as derived buffers for DeepSeek V4 NVIDIA/XPU and Kimi K3. Kernel tuple properties read the current owned buffers rather than retaining stale temporary tensors. Stage new checkpoint sources until packing completes, then commit new values into the existing graph-visible storage.

Native shared experts own all four packed tensors as well. Keep the shared projection loader topology, release raw storage after conversion, and skip unused serial PWAL to avoid retaining another processed copy. The enclosing MoE participates in completion when shared sources change. Adds repeated routed reload coverage and updates shared ownership assertions. XPU's existing unsupported runtime guard remains in place; this does not enable an XPU MegaMoE backend.

## Merge order

Merge #53509 first, then this PR. The branch starts directly from main and includes no prerequisite PR commits. It is not stacked. FlashInfer alpha ownership (#59002) can merge afterwards; opaque FlashInfer packed weights are outside this native ownership implementation.

Tracks #57895 and ports the MegaMoE portion of aoshen02/vllm#56. Source-dropping transforms require a complete routed/shared checkpoint source group; this does not enable selective reload.

## Validation

Ruff formatting and lint checked locally. Linux/GPU integration and CUDA Graph replay validation remain pending; local Windows pytest collection is blocked by uvloop. No H20 or other remote GPU tests were run.

## AI disclosure

Code and PR text prepared with AI assistance. Human review is pending; this PR is intentionally a draft.

title: [Kernel] Integrate DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
body:
## Summary

Add a ModelOpt NVFP4 MegaMoE path backed by DeepGEMM, including fused BF16 shared-expert execution.

- Quantize NVFP4 activations and stage activation/scales/top-k directly into the symmetric buffer in one Triton launch.
- Transform routed NVFP4 weights/scales into the DeepGEMM layout.
- Fuse compatible BF16 shared experts; keep the ordinary shared path for unsupported modules.
- Keep symmetric-buffer allocation/rendezvous outside forward and CUDA Graph capture.
- Fail closed for unsupported router semantics, dtype, bias, LoRA, alignment, platform, DBO, or missing DeepGEMM APIs.
- Preserve the existing ModelOpt path unless `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is selected.

Requires a DeepGEMM build containing the NVFP4 MegaMoE APIs from the merged [deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#409](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/409).

### Why this is not a duplicate

The related open Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4 changes target model-specific paths; this PR is the only open change integrating NVFP4 MegaMoE with the ModelOpt/RoutedExperts path used by GLM-5.2.

### Design and review fixes

- Replaced `scaled_fp4_quant` plus temporary tensors and four `copy_` calls with direct-to-symmetric-buffer NVFP4 staging.
- Folded FP4 quantization, E4M3 scale packing, top-k conversion, and padding masking into one launch.
- Cached the reciprocal activation global scale outside forward.
- Added fail-closed handling for `apply_router_weight_on_input` and other unsupported configurations.
- Restricted shared fusion to modules whose semantics are preserved; otherwise shared execution remains unfused.
- Fixed the real startup contract found on GB300: router IDs may be `int32` or `int64`, while the symmetric `topk_idx` output is `int64`.
- Expanded contract, padding, dtype, H=6144, and CUDA Graph replay tests.

## Test Plan

### Environment

- 8x GB300, two hosts x four GPUs, DP8/EP8 and TP1.
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`.
- CUDA 13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.15.post1`.
- vLLM V2 model runner with compilation mode 0 (no `torch.compile`).
- FULL CUDA Graph requested; sparse MLA selects `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at runtime.
- Maximum sequences per rank: 1024; maximum batched tokens: 16,384; prefix caching disabled.
- Performance revision: `8d37d14`; current PR head: `9febe8a2e`. Later commits add contract guards and tests, then remove redundant adapter state and over-strict weight-scale validation; they do not change the timed DP8/EP8, TP1 path.
- DeepGEMM revision: `0c067ed4` from the dependent PR.

### Serve recipe

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-num-seqs 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"}'
```

For the FlashInfer baseline, replace `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with `--moe-backend auto --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`.

### Workload and measurement

- [NVIDIA SPEED-Bench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SPEED-Bench) `throughput_16k`, `low_entropy` category. Download it with:

  ```bash
  curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Skills/refs/heads/main/nemo_skills/dataset/speed-bench/prepare.py | \
    python3 - --config throughput_16k --output_dir ./speed-bench
  ```

- Deterministically sample exact 128-token windows across source rows without replacement. Each point uses `8 * M` distinct prompts.
- ISL `128`, OSL `256`, `temperature=0`, `ignore_eos=true`.
- M/rank: `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024`; global request concurrency is `8 * M`.
- Send exactly M requests directly to each rank endpoint. Warm each point with one short request per rank, then run two formal repeats. The final DeepGEMM M1024 point uses three repeats.
- For each repeat, measure the common steady-decode interval from the latest first-token timestamp to the earliest request-completion timestamp. Count streamed output tokens in that interval and report aggregate throughput across all eight ranks. The table reports the median repeat.
- Model loading, JIT compilation, backend autotuning, CUDA Graph capture, prefill, first-token latency, and drain are outside the measured window.

## Test Results

### D-only: SPEED-Bench low entropy, 128 input / 256 output, DEP8

| M/rank | FlashInfer baseline (tok/s) | DeepGEMM fused (tok/s) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 532 | 560 | **+5.12%** |
| 2 | 982 | 1,030 | **+4.84%** |
| 4 | 1,778 | 1,860 | **+4.61%** |
| 8 | 3,227 | 3,404 | **+5.49%** |
| 16 | 6,182 | 6,533 | **+5.67%** |
| 32 | 11,787 | 12,422 | **+5.38%** |
| 64 | 22,040 | 23,606 | **+7.10%** |
| 128 | 41,878 | 44,571 | **+6.43%** |
| 256 | 68,145 | 76,152 | **+11.75%** |
| 512 | 96,883 | 108,828 | **+12.33%** |
| 1024 | 104,228 | 117,379 | **+12.62%** |


### P-only: random prompts, OSL=1, GB300 PCP8/EP8

| ISL | FlashInfer req/s | DeepGEMM req/s | Throughput gain | FlashInfer p50 TTFT | DeepGEMM p50 TTFT | p50 TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | 39.601 | 55.249 | **+39.51%** | 402.807 ms | 288.575 ms | **-28.36%** |
| 2K | 27.004 | 37.990 | **+40.68%** | 592.267 ms | 421.739 ms | **-28.79%** |
| 4K | 20.329 | 26.193 | **+28.84%** | 776.873 ms | 604.094 ms | **-22.24%** |
| 8K | 10.089 | 12.815 | **+27.01%** | 1539.304 ms | 1221.353 ms | **-20.66%** |

Every point completed all formal requests with zero failures. The initial sweep showed +38.12%/+41.91%/+29.93%/+28.72% throughput for 1K/2K/4K/8K; the repeat preserved the direction and magnitude at every point. Because `long_prefill_token_threshold=4096`, the 8K prompts were chunked; this flag was identical in both arms.

#### P-only serve recipe

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --max-model-len 9216 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

For the FlashInfer baseline, replace `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` with `--moe-backend auto`; all other serving flags are identical.

### Routing-imbalance sensitivity

The imbalance factor `x` is the busiest destination rank's received routed slots divided by the mean received slots across the eight destination ranks:

```text
x = max(slots_received_by_rank) / mean(slots_received_by_rank)
```

Thus, `1x` is perfectly balanced, while `2x`, `4x`, and `7x` mean that the busiest rank receives 2, 4, or 7 times the average routed slots. 
| Destination imbalance | DG gain at M32 | DG gain at M64 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1x | **+18.26%** | **+19.95%** |
| 2x | **+17.61%** | **+19.53%** |
| 4x | **+4.83%** | **+7.82%** |
| 7x | **-25.76%** | **-28.36%** |

## Accuracy

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| B300 dense PyTorch-reference UT | **PASS** on all eight ranks; relative output differences `1.49e-6` to `2.16e-6` with finite outputs and per-expert alpha/A2 scale paths |
| B300 full-size fusion-order test | Fused versus unfused output was exactly identical; deliberately wrong `(routed + shared) * 2.5` ordering differed by `0.2979`, validating `routed * 2.5 + shared` |
| Targeted GB300 integration smoke | **PASS**: M=1 `int32` IDs, M=8 `int64` IDs, and semantic guards |
| Targeted vLLM GPU tests | **16/16 passed** |
| DeepGEMM boundary/adversarial | **42/42 passed**, M/rank 1-2048, max rel-L2 `0.005421` |
| DeepGEMM random fuzz | **22/22 passed**, M/rank 3-3073, max rel-L2 `0.002655` |
| DeepGEMM shared-only | **10/10 passed**, max rel-L2 `0.001134` |
| Real GLM-5.2 MoE layer replays | **75/75 passed**; fused was closer to FP32 in 69/75 layers |
| Deterministic E2E prompts | **16/16 exact** for each arm across two runs |
| 700-repeat long-context probe | All three arms produced the same token sequence and content |
| Initial paired GSM8K canary, fixed 100 questions, 5-shot | FI **93%**, DG fused **93%**; invalid responses **0%** in both arms |
| GSM8K, 100 questions, 5-shot | FI **95%**, DG unfused **94%**, DG fused **95%**; invalid responses **0%** |

title: [MoE] Optimize fused MoE token alignment and adaptive block size for fine-grained experts
body:
## Summary

Fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures with high expert counts (such as Gemma 4 26B-A4B with E=128, top-k=8) experience severe fixed kernel launch overhead and padding inflation in vLLM's Triton fused MoE path during small-batch decode (M <= 4).

This PR introduces dynamic token alignment bypass when expert token collision is negligible (`M * topk * 4 <= E`), clamps naive block size to 16, and provides adaptive default tile sizing for fine-grained MoEs (E >= 128). Tested on upstream HEAD with an 8x NVIDIA H100 platform, this achieves up to a **1.50x speedup** on small-batch MoE dispatches (saving 35-46 µs per dispatch, ~1.05-1.38 ms per generated decode token across 30 layers) with zero loss in numerical accuracy.

---

## Purpose

- **Problem Statement**:
  1. **Fixed Kernel Launch Overhead**: In vLLM's Triton fused MoE implementation, `ops.moe_align_block_size` incurs a fixed ~20-27 µs CUDA kernel launch and prefix-sum latency per dispatch. Across the two GEMM dispatches (W13 and W2) in 30 decoder layers, this accounts for ~1.2-1.6 ms of invariant latency per generated decode token.
  2. **Padding Inflation**: The default `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 64` pads token-to-expert assignments up to multiples of 64. At M=1 (8 active tokens for top-k=8), this produces 512 padded tokens—a **64.00x padding overhead** where **98.4% of processed rows are dummy padding**.
  3. **Sorting Redundancy at Low Sparsity**: When `(M * topk) / E <= 0.25` (i.e. `M * topk * 4 <= E`), tokens are so sparsely distributed across experts that token collision on any individual expert is near zero (<= 1 token per expert). Under this regime, sorting and grouping tokens yields zero packing benefit while paying the full 20-27 µs alignment latency penalty.

- **Changes Made**:
  1. **Dynamic Token Alignment Bypass** (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`):
     - Dynamically evaluates `M * topk * 4 <= E` per forward pass.
     - When satisfied, sets `sorted_token_ids=None` to engage Triton's naive block assignment path, bypassing `ops.moe_align_block_size` entirely.
     - Enforces `BLOCK_SIZE_M = min(config.get("BLOCK_SIZE_M", 16), 16)` in naive mode to prevent redundant computation over dummy padding rows.
     - Adds full support for `expert_map` in the naive path via `expert_map[topk_ids.view(-1)]`.
     - Guards against quantized WNA16 formats which do not support naive assignment.
     - Routes `TritonWNA16Experts.forward()` through `_prepare_expert_assignment` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py`).
  2. **Adaptive Default Tile Sizes for Fine-Grained MoEs (E >= 128)**:
     - In `get_default_config()`, sets `BLOCK_SIZE_M` adaptively based on batch size: M <= 64 -> 16, M <= 256 -> 32, M > 256 -> 64.
     - Corrects the `tokens_per_expert` calculation to include top-k: `(M * topk) // max(E, 1)`.
  3. **Backwards-Compatible `moe_sum` Dispatcher** (`vllm/_custom_ops.py`):
     - Added dual 2-arg / 4-arg fallback to support differing C++ extension build signatures seamlessly.
  4. **Documentation**:
     - Internal kernel execution optimization; no public API changes or user-facing doc updates required.

---

## Test Plan

The following test suite verifies functional correctness, bit-for-bit numerical equivalence, regression freedom across existing alignment pathways, and end-to-end model generation:

1. **Unit Tests (Fine-Grained MoE & Crossover Logic)**:
   ```bash
   pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py
   ```
   Verifies:
   - Bit-for-bit numerical equivalence (`atol=0.0`) between naive bypass and aligned path.
   - Crossover boundary switching behavior from naive (M=4) to aligned (M=5) for E=128, top-k=8.
   - Dynamic block size selection and clamping behavior.
   - Custom `expert_map` index mapping in naive mode.

2. **Regression Suite (Existing MoE Alignment)**:
   ```bash
   pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_align_block_size.py
   ```

3. **Code Quality & Linters**:
   ```bash
   ruff check vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/ tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py vllm/_custom_ops.py
   ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/ tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py vllm/_custom_ops.py
   ```

4. **Kernel & Model Benchmarks**:
   ```bash
   # Crossover boundary benchmark across batch sizes
   python scratch/crossover_benchmark.py

   # End-to-end model generation benchmarks
   python scratch/benchmark_generation_moe_models.py
   ```

---

## Test Result

All tests and benchmarks were executed on an 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM5) platform on current upstream HEAD.

### 1. Unit Test Results
- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_moe_fine_grained.py`: **12 passed in 13.61s**.
- `ruff check` & `ruff format --check`: **All checks passed; clean formatting**.

### 2. Isolated Kernel Benchmark (E=128, top-k=8, H=2816, N=704)
| Batch Size (M) | Aligned Path (µs) | Naive Path (µs) | Time Saved (µs) | Speedup | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M = 1** (Decode) | 130.73 | **95.66** | **35.07** | **1.37x** | **NAIVE** |
| **M = 2** | 137.71 | **91.63** | **46.08** | **1.50x** | **NAIVE** |
| **M = 3** | 127.38 | **113.76** | **13.62** | **1.12x** | **NAIVE** |
| **M = 4** | 135.99 | 142.83 | -6.85 | 0.95x | ALIGNED |
| **M = 8** | 239.02 | 260.41 | -21.40 | 0.92x | ALIGNED |

- Saving 35.07 µs to 46.08 µs per dispatch translates to **~1.05 ms to 1.38 ms saved per generated decode token** across 30 decoder layers.
- **Numerical Parity**: `max |y_naive - y_aligned| = 0.000000` confirms bit-for-bit numerical equivalence.

### 3. End-to-End Model Generation Benchmarks
Tested with real pre-trained MoE models under greedy generation (64 output tokens per request):

- **OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct** (E=64, top-k=8):
  - Batch Size 1 (naive bypass): **12.85 ms/token** (77.8 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 2 (naive bypass): **13.02 ms/token** (153.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 4 (aligned path): **13.59 ms/token** (294.3 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 8 (aligned path): **13.74 ms/token** (582.4 tok/s)

- **Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat** (E=60, top-k=4):
  - Batch Size 1 (naive bypass): **24.00 ms/token** (41.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 2 (naive bypass): **25.74 ms/token** (77.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 4 (aligned path): **27.73 ms/token** (144.3 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 8 (aligned path): **27.87 ms/token** (287.1 tok/s)

- **Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it** (E=128, top-k=8):
  - Batch Size 1 (naive bypass): **36.10 ms/token** (27.7 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 2 (naive bypass): **36.06 ms/token** (55.5 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 4 (aligned path): **39.70 ms/token** (100.8 tok/s)
  - Batch Size 8 (aligned path): **38.58 ms/token** (207.4 tok/s)

- **Text Quality**: All generated samples match expected greedy outputs with zero degradation or token corruption.

---

## Duplicate-Work Check

Prior to opening this PR, the following searches were executed against upstream `vllm-project/vllm`:
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "moe token alignment"`
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "moe_align_block_size in:body"`

**Findings**: Existing open PRs touching MoE token alignment are ROCm-specific (#51515) or address deep EP / Marlin fusing (#53911, #44167). No existing PR implements dynamic alignment bypass for sparse regimes or fine-grained MoE tile size clamping for 128+ experts.

---

## Statement of AI Assistance

This pull request was prepared with AI assistance (Jetski pair programmer) and reviewed, benchmarked, and verified by Douglas Reid.

title: [Perf][Scheduler] Add risk-aware prefix-cache admission
body:
## Purpose

Related to #48485. This is an opt-in admission-side approach to prefix-cache
reuse loss under constrained KV capacity. It does not implement the issue's
proposed waiting-queue-informed eviction policy; block eviction remains unchanged.

Before allocating blocks for a fresh waiting request, the risk policy inspects
the free-block queue against estimated full-prompt block demand, excluding the
candidate's own cache-hit blocks. Potential cached-block exposure triggers
ranking of a bounded waiting window by cached-prefix length.

- Skip policy lookups when no admission slot is available, including slots held
  by paused streaming sessions.
- Recompute a promoted head's cache hit and allocation demand before allocation.
- Allow at most one risk-ranking attempt per admission position.
- Bound free-queue inspection; an inconclusive scan does not reject admission.

The window defaults to zero, leaving the policy disabled. The risk path currently
uses the custom scheduler entry point; selecting a nonzero window alone on the
base scheduler enables the threshold-based path instead. For the risk path, set:

```python
scheduler_cls="vllm.v1.core.sched.qwenfuse_risk.RiskPerfScheduler"
cache_aware_admission_window=16
enable_prefix_caching=True
async_scheduling=False
```

The supported risk-policy scope is synchronous FCFS with local prefix caching
and a single full-attention KV group. KV connectors, LoRA, encoder-decoder
models, speculative/lookahead decoding, and prefix replay are excluded by the
current guard. The risk subclass uses exposure, rather than the configured
legacy usage threshold, as its ranking trigger.

## Test Plan and Current Results

Validated after integrating upstream main at
`e5f3d08d722870a5301560fad0cfa65b7e333900`. The update adapts risk admission
to the upstream KV-holding waiting queue and deferred-request handling.
It retains upstream queue priority, avoids popping an admitted request twice,
and resets the bounded ranking retry when the admission position advances.
The change relative to that main snapshot remains confined to nine scheduler,
configuration, KV-manager, and test files.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py   -k 'cache_aware_admission or risk_admission' -q --tb=short
```

- Targeted admission regression: **25 passed**. Three added tests cover
  KV-holding request priority, risk rechecking after a successful admission,
  and risk rechecking after a promoted request is skipped.
- Full scheduler regression: **220 passed, 2 failed**. Both failures reproduce
  on unmodified target main in the same single-GPU environment:
  `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
  and `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait` fail GPU-count
  validation for PP=2 and PP=3 respectively. They were not skipped or
  reported as passing.
- Local style and type checks: **passed** on all nine changed Python files, using the applicable upstream hooks, including Ruff, typos, mypy for Python 3.10-3.13, SPDX headers, and Buildkite test tethering.
- Qwen3-8B BF16 / FlashAttention 2 eager smoke passed with the risk policy,
  APC, chunked prefill, window 4, and a 4 GiB KV budget. One warmup request
  and two subsequent requests completed with 8 output tokens each;
  the repeated prompt reused **224 cached tokens**.

This validation used the updated Python source with the existing Python
3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 environment and September 20 native extensions
on an A100-PCIE-40GB. It is not a fresh native build or new performance result.
The eager smoke does not establish CUDA Graph execution, model-quality
equivalence, or multi-GPU compatibility.

## Historical Performance Results

Measurements on commit `27757dde`, A100-PCIE-40GB, Qwen3-8B BF16,
FlashAttention 2, with APC and chunked prefill enabled. Baseline and risk-policy
runs used the same operator configuration; only the admission policy differed.

For the constrained 8 GiB random mixed fixed-burst workload:

- Median throughput improvement: **5.02%**.
- Median batch completion time reduction: **4.78%**.
- Five of six paired comparisons improved; throughput changes ranged from
  **-2.37% to +6.12%**.
- Sufficient-capacity and all-cold controls showed near-zero median changes.
- Cold-request TTFT increased substantially for one seed.

These are historical fixed-burst measurements, not sustained-serving results
or performance measurements on the current submitted head.

## Known Limits and Review Questions

- Cached-prefix ranking can delay cold requests; the current implementation
  does not provide an aging mechanism or a bound on waiting time.
- A bounded waiting window cannot discover reusable prefixes beyond that window.
- Exposure is a snapshot-based estimate, not proof that a particular waiting
  request's reusable prefix will be evicted. Decode growth and future frees
  are not predicted.
- Scheduler CPU overhead, sustained-load fairness, and updated-head performance
  still need measurement. No overhead-neutrality or starvation-free guarantee
  is claimed.
- The current integration uses a custom scheduler subclass and retains the
  threshold-based base path. Feedback on the preferred upstream configuration
  and integration surface is welcome.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Account for GPU copies during prefix admission
body:
A HiSparse host-prefix cache hit can re-pin free GPU shadow copies before allocating the request's hot region. Those pins were omitted from device-block admission, so a request could pass the capacity check and then crash the engine with `Cannot get 64 free blocks from the pool`.

This change counts the unique, currently free GPU copies associated with the local host-prefix hit. The host manager includes that cost in the existing admission calculation; running requests and already-pinned copies add no cost. Under pressure, admission returns `None` so the scheduler can defer the request instead of exhausting the pool. GPU-copy reuse is preserved.

The regression uses real CPU block pools through `KVCacheManager.allocate_slots`. It exercises three insufficient-capacity cases, an exact-fit case, retry after pressure is released, and preservation of surviving copies when one earlier copy was evicted.

### Validation

Base: upstream `213c379`.

- Unmodified production code: the new pressure regression reproduced three allocator exceptions; the exact-fit case passed.
- Final prefix-cache suite: **163 passed**, no deselected tests, on `8def699` (format-only changes after the test run).
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, and mypy.

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" VLLM_PLUGINS='' uv run --project "$TEST_ENV" --no-sync python "$CPU_TEST_WRAPPER" \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/core tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'not test_fewer_blocks_with_hma' -q
uv tool run --from 'pre-commit>=4.5.1' pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py
```

`TEST_ENV` is the prepared vLLM/Prime RL dependency environment. `CPU_TEST_WRAPPER` selects `vllm.platforms._current_platform = CpuPlatform()` and calls `pytest.main(sys.argv[1:])`. The negative name filter matched no test in this checkout; all 163 tests ran.

Tests are run with the prepared CUDA dependency environment on a GPU-less host, explicitly selecting `CpuPlatform` before pytest collection. The wrapper and logs are retained locally; no installed package files were modified.

### Model/serving evidence and limits

The equivalent admission accounting was exercised as a local runtime adapter on B300 before this upstream refactor. Configuration: one EP8 prefill node using DeepEP high throughput, one EP8 decode node using DeepEP low latency, GLM-5.3 FP8 revision `aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42`, BF16 KV, HiSparse on decode, index cache, NIXL pull and Mooncake CPU store. GPU KV was capped at 48 GiB/rank to force pressure. The tested vLLM source was `f7f56f01d0f588f46c20035d3ab87cf16f25addf`, with a separate complete-prefix NIXL adapter and the HiSparse layer-offset fix.

- Before the admission adapter, the 2,048-request wave crashed a decode worker with the allocation error above.
- With it, all 2,048 capacity requests completed. Peak active concurrency was 134/GPU with the remainder queued; 25 preemptions occurred in this intentional pressure wave.
- The full suite recorded 3,760 completions and 32 intentional cancellations, zero request errors/empty streams, and healthy idle endpoints at the end.
- The long-generation phase completed 256 requests while reloading 1,234.74 GiB of KV from CPU. There were no NIXL transfer/notification failures or failed required Mooncake GETs. The fixed-size prefill store rejected 15,019 optional PUT keys for lack of space.
- No pathological gibberish was observed in the output screens and inspected samples. Long-request identifier retrieval was 255/256 versus 256/256 in a resident control, whose output cap was shorter (256 versus up to 1,536 tokens). Four capacity responses also copied their identifiers incorrectly. Exact output parity is not established; this is not a general accuracy evaluation.

Those GPU results validate the local adapter's behavior, **not a model run of this new upstream commit**. The final upstream implementation is covered by the regression tests above. No throughput improvement is claimed.

### Duplicate-work check and scope

Reviewed issue #56699 and its comments, open PRs referencing it, and open PRs matching HiSparse/NIXL, admission, prefix, copies, and free blocks.

- #56946 already covers unaligned NIXL host imports, source-page clipping, and notify-only receives. Those changes are intentionally excluded here.
- #55398 adds direct GPU landing for P/D imports and admission-time tier selection. This patch instead fixes the uncounted re-pinning of existing GPU copies on a **local host-prefix hit**, without changing landing tiers.
- #56109 is a broader, not-for-merge resident-eviction design proposal; this patch preserves main's existing design.
- This does not claim to fix #56699's CUDA host-mirror failure, mixed-memory producers, or model accuracy discrepancies. Model/connector configurations and cluster-specific networking changes are not included.
